result.area_summary: The App Registrations slice is in good shape structurally: the detail pane, tabs and dialogs consistently use ConfirmDialog with subjects, `use_command`, keep-alive tabs, and the UriListEditor/DirectorySearch primitives are well-documented and unit-tested. The weak spots cluster around (a) the detail pane rebuilding every visited tab on each `on_changed`, which the credentials tab works around with deferred reloads but the permissions tab does not (its downgrade/consent outcome notes are torn down before they can be read, and consent failures never reach a toast); (b) a handful of ordering/state bugs (list Refresh races the cache invalidation, `pending_app_tab` leaks when the target is already open, identifier-URI writes replay a stale client snapshot); (c) primitive drift the docs explicitly forbid (OwnersTab/AddOwner hand-roll the directory search with the exact "No matches under an untouched box" bug, several tabs use red text instead of DetailLoadError, a value-only SharePoint gate); and (d) thin browser-test coverage for the Owners, Expose an API and Permissions tabs.

findings.title: List Refresh bumps the resource before the cache invalidation is awaited, so it can refetch the cached list
findings.rationale: Nothing orders the two IPC calls: the resource re-run is scheduled first and the backend's cache-hit path is fully synchronous (no await before `return Ok(cached)`), so `list_applications_with_pairing` can be served from the very cache `invalidate_list_cache` is about to drop. The Refresh button then spins and shows the same stale rows. The detail pane's own Refresh (application_detail_pane.rs:70-73) does it correctly: `invalidate_application_detail(...).await; reload.update(...)`. enterprise_application_list.rs:114-122 has the same shape, so the fix should land in both.
findings.proposal: In `on_refresh`, move `reload.update(...)` inside the spawned task after the `invalidate_list_cache(...).await` (mirroring application_detail_pane.rs:70-73), and do the same in enterprise_application_list.rs. Optionally add a GUI test in tests/gui/application_list.rs whose mock records call order (invalidate before list).

findings.title: Permissions tab consent/downgrade outcome notes are set right before `on_changed` unmounts the tab; consent failures never reach the operator
findings.rationale: `bump_reload` re-runs the pane's `LocalResource`; the `Suspend` closure in application_detail_pane.rs:136-148 builds a fresh view (new `detail_signal`, new tab components) so every local signal in PermissionsTab is discarded. The `consent_result` Callout (763-779, the only place `r.role_assignments_skipped.len()` and `r.failures.len()` are shown) and the `scope_note` Callout (759-761, the only report of the downgrade outcome, e.g. "narrower permission was already in place" / "was already gone") therefore flash at most for the refetch duration. The success toast omits `failures`, so a partial consent (`GrantResult.failures: Vec<GrantFailure>`, dto/permissions.rs:72) reads as an unqualified success. The comment at 205-206 is also stale: line 342 closes the chooser.
findings.proposal: Follow the credentials tab's documented pattern: report via the session toast stack before `on_changed`. For consent, `toast_error` when `!r.failures.is_empty()` naming the count (and ideally the first failure message), `toast_success` otherwise; drop the `consent_result` Callout. For downgrade, `session.toast_success(note)` and drop `scope_note`. Fix the stale comment. Longer term, see the detail-pane remount finding.

findings.title: SharePoint sites section is gated on the bare permission value, not the resource, contrary to the carry-the-resource rule
findings.rationale: The row-level gate `row_scope_kind` (lines 70-81) and the `has_mail` gate three lines earlier (781-786, `is_exchange_scopable_on(Some(&p.resource_app_id), v)`) are resource-aware; this section gate is not. An app holding `Sites.Read.All` only on Office 365 SharePoint Online (or any third-party API exposing a `Sites.*` role) gets the `SharePointSitesSection`, which reads Graph per-site grants and will report "no grants" for a permission that section cannot describe. The repo invariant (`the_resource_blind_mailbox_gates_are_not_reintroduced`) only pins the Exchange forms, so nothing catches this.
findings.proposal: Gate on `p.resource_app_id == MICROSOFT_GRAPH_APP_ID && (v == "Sites.Selected" || is_sharepoint_orgwide(v))` (or a new `is_sharepoint_site_grant_resource_permission(Some(&p.resource_app_id), v)` in core::scoping next to the existing gates), add a unit test beside `the_legacy_sharepoint_resource_gets_no_button`, and consider extending the repo invariant's GONE list with bare `is_sharepoint_orgwide(` calls outside core/scope_badge.

findings.title: `pending_app_tab` leaks to the next opened app when the deep-link target is already open
findings.rationale: The pane consumes `pending_app_tab` only in its constructor. If the credential dashboard's "Open" (credentials_dashboard.rs:114) or an audit row (audit_view/row.rs:179) targets an app that is already in the workspace, `open_item` just refocuses it, no pane mounts, and the flag stays `Some("credentials")`. The next unrelated app the operator opens from the list lands on Credentials instead of `last_app_tab`, with no visible cause. The MI variant's comment acknowledges an already-open window keeps its tab, but nobody clears the flag. The only test (state/mod.rs:456-487) covers the tenant-switch reset.
findings.proposal: In `open_app_on_tab` / `open_enterprise_on_tab`, check `self.is_open(kind, &id)` first: if open, don't set the pending flag (or set a per-open-item `requested_tab` the pane observes via an Effect so the live pane actually switches tab). Add a unit test asserting `pending_app_tab` is `None` after deep-linking to an already-open item.

findings.title: Every mutation rebuilds the whole detail pane and remounts all visited tabs (root cause of the deferred-reload workarounds)
findings.rationale: `bump_reload` re-runs the resource, the Suspend closure yields a brand-new view, and with `Suspense` (not `Transition`; no `<Transition` exists in web-rs) the skeleton flashes first. The keep-alive latch preserves state across tab switches but not across saves, so removing one owner re-runs `list_federated_credentials`, `get_expose_api`, `get_application_authentication`, the Activity audit query + sign-in lookup, the CA list, the Exchange mail-scope lookup and resets the usage panel for every tab that was visited — and discards half-typed forms in other tabs. It also forces the credentials tab's three "defer on_changed until the dialog is dismissed" dances (390-397, 578-584, 600-608) and causes the lost-notes bug in the permissions tab.
findings.proposal: Keep a long-lived `RwSignal<Option<Arc<ApplicationDetail>>>` on the pane, update it from an Effect over the resource (or in the Suspend on success), and mount `DetailHeader` + `TabBar` + the keep-alive tabs once outside the Suspend, passing `Signal<Arc<ApplicationDetail>>` derived from that signal; show `DetailSkeleton` only while the signal is `None`. Tabs then survive `on_changed`, the reveal-dialog deferrals become unnecessary, and per-tab sub-resources only re-run when their inputs change. Interim cheap step: switch `Suspense` to `Transition` to remove the skeleton flash.

findings.title: OwnersTab and AddOwnerButton hand-roll the directory search that DirectorySearch/OwnerPicker exist to replace, reintroducing the 'No matches under an untouched box' bug
findings.rationale: owners_tab.rs:36-67 + 449-536 and add_owner.rs:42-62 + 213-261 each carry their own 300 ms debounce, 2-char gate, Suspense + "Searching…" spinner and `.candidates` markup. Because the resource returns `Ok(Vec::new())` for short queries and the render only checks `filtered.is_empty()`, the Owners tab shows "No matches." beneath an empty search box on first paint — exactly the drift the primitive was extracted to end. Both files also duplicate the add-default-owners loop (owners_tab.rs:127-150 vs add_owner.rs:125-159) with slightly different `existing` sources. There is no backend `add_default_owners` command (grep of src-tauri/src/commands finds none).
findings.proposal: Replace both search blocks with `OwnerPicker`/`DirectorySearch` (`exclude` = current owners or staged set, `action_label` = "Add"/"Stage", `row_disabled` for the in-flight id, `clear_on_pick=false` + own `query` for the add path that clears on success). Move the default-owners loop into one backend command (`add_default_owners(tenant_id, object_id) -> {added, failures}`) or one shared frontend helper, and have both call sites use it.

findings.title: 'Rotate & remove existing' deletes every client secret with no confirmation and no count
findings.evidence:
<Button
                        class="button--danger"
                        appearance=Signal::derive(|| ButtonAppearance::Primary)
                        on_click=Box::new(move |_| do_rotate(true))
                        disabled=Signal::derive(move || cmd_rotate.busy.get())
                    >
(lines 512-516) let remove_key_ids: Vec<String> = if remove_existing { secrets.with(|list| list.iter().map(|s| s.key_id.clone()).collect()) } else { Vec::new() };
findings.rationale: Removing one secret goes through `ConfirmDialog` with the credential named as subject (1132-1146), and the expired sweep is confirm-gated too (1162-1177), but the rotate dialog's primary danger button strips all N secrets, active ones included, on a single click. The dialog body says only "optionally removes the existing secret(s)" and the button label carries no count, so an operator cannot see they are about to break every other caller of the app.
findings.proposal: Label the button with the live count ("Rotate & remove {n} existing"), and either route `do_rotate(true)` through a `ConfirmDialog` (subject = app name, body naming the count) or require `require_keyword` when `n > 1`. Also surface `r.warnings` content (currently "see the log", line 539) in the toast or an expandable Callout, since the log is not reachable from the UI.

findings.title: Lifetime/validity inputs are silently coerced (garbage → default, out of range → clamp) instead of validated
findings.evidence:
let days = rotate_lifetime
            .get()
            .parse::<u32>()
            .unwrap_or(180)
            .clamp(1, 730);
(lines 570-574) let days = gencert_validity.get().parse::<u32>().unwrap_or(365).clamp(1, 1095);
(lines 125-128) /// Resolves the Expires controls ... Mirrors the backend's validation (end after start, 24-month cap) for friendlier, pre-submit errors
findings.rationale: The new-secret dialog validates and reports (`resolve_expiry_fields` returns `Err("Secret lifetime cannot exceed 24 months.")`), but the rotate and generate-certificate dialogs accept "abc", "0", "3650" or "90 days" and mint a credential with a lifetime the operator did not type (180/365 days, or the cap), with no message. A certificate valid for 1095 days when 3650 was requested, or a rotated secret expiring in 180 days when "18" was a typo for "180", is a silent divergence from intent on a security-critical object. Neither path has a unit test.
findings.proposal: Extract `fn parse_days(raw: &str, min: u32, max: u32) -> Result<u32, String>` returning a message ("Enter a whole number of days between 1 and 730."), surface it via the shared `error` signal before dispatch like `resolve_expiry_fields`, and add table tests. Consider `<Select>` presets for both dialogs, matching the new-secret dialog.

findings.title: Identifier-URI add/remove replays the tab's stale snapshot as a full replace (lost-update), contradicting the module doc
findings.rationale: `uris` is a `StoredValue` captured from the DTO at mount (line 100). Scopes and pre-authorized clients are re-read live by the backend before their PATCH, but `set_identifier_uris` writes whatever list the client sends. If another admin (or the SSO wizard, which also edits identifierUris) added a URI after this tab loaded, Add or Remove here silently drops it. The module doc claims live re-read for every mutation, so a maintainer would not expect this.
findings.proposal: Either add `add_identifier_uri` / `remove_identifier_uri` backend commands that GET the live `identifierUris`, apply the delta, validate and PATCH (like `upsert_api_scope`), or have the frontend call `get_expose_api` immediately before computing the new list. Update the module doc either way.

findings.title: Tab-level load failures render red text with no Retry instead of the DetailLoadError primitive
findings.rationale: A transient 429/network failure on `get_expose_api`, `get_application_authentication`, `list_federated_credentials` or `list_resource_permissions` leaves the operator with a dead red line; the only recovery is the pane-level Refresh (which remounts everything) or reopening the wizard. Activity and Conditional Access tabs (activity_tab.rs:83-91, conditional_access_tab.rs:70-78) already use `DetailLoadError` with `on_retry` bumping their `reload`, so this is drift, not design.
findings.proposal: Replace the four `Body1.form-error` branches with `<DetailLoadError error=e on_retry=Callback::new(move |_| reload.update(|n| *n += 1)) />` (the picker can re-set `resource_app_id` to retrigger its resource). The `web-test-strings-check.sh` hook will flag nothing since no test references these strings.

findings.title: Authentication form has no Cancel/Reset or dirty tracking; Overview edit sends an empty PATCH when nothing changed
findings.evidence:
<div class="actions-row">
                <Button
                    appearance=Signal::derive(|| ButtonAppearance::Primary)
                    on_click=Box::new(save)
                    disabled=Signal::derive(move || cmd.busy.get())
                >
(overview_tab.rs:84-88) move |tenant_id| { let mut patch = UpdateApplicationInput::default(); let dn_t = dn.trim(); if dn_t != app.display_name { patch.display_name = Some(dn_t.to_string()); }
(overview_tab.rs:158-159) on_click=Box::new(save) disabled=Signal::derive(move || cmd.busy.get())
findings.rationale: The Authentication tab is a full-replace write of three URI lists plus five flags, yet the only control is Save: after mangling rows the operator has no way back short of refreshing the whole pane, and there is no indication that anything differs from the loaded DTO. The Overview edit computes the diff only inside the async closure, so an unchanged form still round-trips a `{}` PATCH and shows a spinner, and Save is never disabled for a clean form. Neither form warns when the open item is closed with unsaved edits.
findings.proposal: Derive a `dirty: Signal<bool>` per form (compare `to_uris()`/flags against the loaded DTO; compare the four overview fields against `app`), disable Save when clean, add a Reset/Cancel that rebuilds `UriListState` from the DTO (or bumps `reload`), and short-circuit `save` with a toast when the patch is empty. A small `use_unsaved_guard` hook on `Session.close_item` could prompt when a dirty form is about to be closed.

findings.title: Browser GUI tests do not exercise the Owners, Expose an API or Permissions tab actions, nor rotate/new-secret/federated flows
findings.rationale: The detail pane has four smoke tests, the certificate reveal and authentication tab are well covered, but the three most mutation-heavy tabs have no behavioural coverage: revoke/remove-declaration confirm routing (three always-mounted dialogs keyed on `PendingRevoke`), the downgrade chooser, the Application/Delegated filter toggles, Replace-all-owners staging and apply, default-owner addition, scope add/edit/delete and pre-authorized client editing, the new-secret dialog + `SecretRevealDialog`, and the rotate-into-Key-Vault dialog prefill. Regressions such as the lost consent/downgrade notes or a mis-wired `PendingRevoke` arm would pass CI.
findings.proposal: Add `tests/gui/owners_tab.rs`, `expose_api_tab.rs` and `permissions_tab.rs` modules (sharded by the detail-pane subtree per frontend-workspace.md) with mocked IPC: assert the confirm dialog names the row's subject and the mocked command receives the right ids; assert the downgrade chooser lists `downgrade_alternatives` and the outcome is reported; assert Replace-all sends exactly the staged ids; assert the new-secret flow shows the reveal and only reloads on Done. Reuse the `certificate_reveal.rs` mount helpers.

findings.title: Stale doc comments reference a deleted TSX frontend and the removed thaw TabList
findings.rationale: `apps/desktop/` contains only `src-tauri` and `web-rs`; the `.tsx` files referenced in application_detail_pane.rs:3, application_list.rs:2, owners_tab.rs:2, create_app_dialog.rs:3, tabs/mod.rs:1, views/mod.rs:1, hooks/mod.rs:1 and state/tenant.rs:17 no longer exist, and `AppTab`/`EnterpriseTab` still describe themselves in terms of thaw's `Tab`/`TabList`, which the architecture doc says was removed. A new contributor following these pointers finds nothing.
findings.proposal: Delete the "Mirrors …tsx" sentences (or replace with the one-line purpose) and reword app_tab.rs:59 / enterprise_tab.rs:27,64 to reference `components::ui::TabBar`. A repo-invariant test asserting no source mentions `apps/desktop/web/` would keep it that way.

findings.title: Shared helpers exist but are still bypassed: no_tenant(), copy_text(), MICROSOFT_GRAPH_APP_ID, sign-in-audience list
findings.rationale: `util::no_tenant()` was introduced to end the duplication its own doc describes, yet application_detail_pane.rs:44-50 and permission_picker.rs:130-135 still inline the struct. `util::copy_text` exists ("Shared by the detail panes and the SSO summary") but credentials_tab.rs:972-982 and secret_reveal_dialog.rs:21-29 re-implement the clipboard call. `azapptoolkit_core::scoping::MICROSOFT_GRAPH_APP_ID` is already imported by permissions_tab tests, but permission_picker.rs redefines it. create_app_dialog.rs:88-97 hard-codes the four sign-in audiences that overview_tab.rs:12-26 keeps in `SIGN_IN_AUDIENCES`.
findings.proposal: Use `no_tenant()` in both resources; use `copy_text` (or `CopyIconButton`) in the two dialogs; re-export core's `MICROSOFT_GRAPH_APP_ID` from the picker instead of redefining; move `SIGN_IN_AUDIENCES` to a shared module and render `create_app_dialog`'s options from it.

findings.title: Dead and duplicate IPC argument structs hidden by `#![allow(dead_code)]` on the bindings module
findings.rationale: `ResolvePermissionArgs` (applications.rs:75-81), `UpdateRequiredResourceArgs` (permissions.rs:53-59) and `SetArgs` (keyvault.rs:58-63) have no callers (grep finds only their definitions); `FederatedListArgs` (applications.rs:406-411) is field-for-field `ObjectIdArgs`; `TenantArgs` in keyvault.rs (and search.rs/sso.rs/defaults.rs) duplicates `common::TenantArg` despite common.rs existing to be the single source of truth. The crate-wide `#![allow(dead_code)]` means the compiler will never point any of this out, including a binding whose backend command is later removed.
findings.proposal: Delete the three unused structs, replace `FederatedListArgs` with `ObjectIdArgs` and the per-file `TenantArgs` with `TenantArg`, then narrow `#![allow(dead_code)]` to the specific re-exported DTO items that need it (or drop it and let clippy report genuinely dead bindings).

findings.title: SecretRevealDialog reports 'Copied' even when the clipboard write fails, and a reflex Escape dismisses the one-time secret
findings.rationale: `write_text` can reject (no focus, permission denied in some webviews); the dialog still flips to "Copied", and because `on_close` triggers `on_changed` the secret is gone for good once dismissed. Escape closes the reveal unconditionally, so an operator who habitually hits Esc after copying-that-failed loses the value. The credentials tab's `copy_pk` (972-982) gives no feedback at all, so a failed private-key copy is indistinguishable from success there.
findings.proposal: Set `copied` only on `Ok(_)` and show a Callout on `Err` ("Couldn't copy — select the text and copy manually"); for both one-time reveals gate Escape (`use_escape(|| false, ...)`) or require the explicit Done button, and reuse `CopyIconButton`/`copy_text` so the feedback is the app-wide badge.

findings.title: Permissions tab empty state points to the Entra portal and the hand-rolled kind filters can render an empty table silently
findings.evidence:
<Body1>
                            "No permissions declared. Use the Entra portal or restore from a saved manifest."
                        </Body1>
(lines 523-527) <button class=move || filter_chip_class(show_application.get()) type="button" on:click=move |_| show_application.update(|v| *v = !*v)>
(lines 484-489) <Button appearance=Signal::derive(|| ButtonAppearance::Primary) on_click=Box::new(move |_| wizard_open.set(true))> "Grant access"
findings.rationale: The empty-state copy predates the in-app "Grant access" wizard that sits two lines above it, so it sends the operator to the portal for something the tab now does. The Application/Delegated toggles are bespoke `permissions-tab__filter-chip` buttons (not `FilterChip`/`TabBar`), carry no `aria-pressed`, and with both toggled off the `<For>` renders nothing under the table header with no "no rows match" message.
findings.proposal: Reword to "No permissions declared — use Grant access to add one."; add `aria-pressed` (as a string) to the toggles or replace them with a three-value `TabBar` (All/Application/Delegated) which cannot reach the both-off state; if toggles stay, render an inline `Body1` when the filtered set is empty.

findings.title: Permission picker checkboxes share one aria-label and clone the counts map per option
findings.evidence:
<input
                            type="checkbox"
                            class="permission-picker__check"
                            aria-label="Select permission"
                            prop:checked=checked
                            on:change=on_change
                        />
(lines 172-174) let label = counts.get().get(&r.app_id)
(application_list.rs:703) let check_label = format!("Select {display_name} ({app_id_string}) for bulk actions");
findings.rationale: Microsoft Graph alone lists ~400 application permissions; every checkbox announcing "Select permission" makes the picker unusable with a screen reader, while the app-registration list already demonstrates the descriptive-label pattern. Separately, `counts.get()` inside the per-option `.map` clones the whole `HashMap` once per resource option on every render of the dropdown.
findings.proposal: Use `aria-label=format!("Select {}", r.value)` (and the same for delegated scopes at line 421); read counts with `counts.with(|c| c.get(&r.app_id).copied())`.

findings.title: Pre-authorized client is a free-text GUID with no validation or directory lookup
findings.rationale: Pre-authorizing a client skips user consent, so a mistyped or wrong GUID is a security-relevant error that today only surfaces as a Graph 400 (or silently pre-authorizes the wrong app if the GUID happens to exist). The frontend already has a tenant SP index and a `list_app_role_resources`-style picker group ("Tenant app registrations") that resolve name + appId; the row also renders the raw GUID with no display name (line 567), so the operator cannot tell which app is authorized.
findings.proposal: Validate the GUID shape client-side before dispatch; add a `DirectorySearch`-like typeahead over the tenant's app registrations/SPs (appId + display name) for the add path, and resolve display names for existing rows via the SP index (falling back to the GUID).

minor_nits: apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/tabs/credentials_tab.rs:745 — the Upload-certificate button does not clear the shared `error` signal, unlike its siblings at 649-651 and 736-738, so a stale inline error persists into the dialog

apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/tabs/credentials_tab.rs:1020-1022 — thumbprint SHA-1/SHA-256 in the generated-certificate reveal are plain `Body1.mono` while the PFX password beside them uses `CopyableId`; make them copyable too
apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/tabs/credentials_tab.rs:360-366 — `expired_count`/`remove_expired_passwords` sweep only secrets; expired certificates have no sweep affordance (feature gap)

apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/tabs/overview_tab.rs:59-70 — the 'mirrors React useEffect' reset Effect is dead after mount today (`detail_signal` never changes) and would clobber in-progress edits once the pane keeps `detail` alive; guard it with `!editing.get_untracked()`
apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/tabs/permissions_tab.rs:133-134 + 762 — `run_grant` reports the same error twice (toast_error and inline `consent_error`)
apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/tabs/permissions_tab.rs:945 — a granted Delegated row with `permission_value == None` gets no Trash button at all, so it has no way out
apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/application_detail_pane.rs:72-73 — `refreshing.set(false)` runs right after `reload.update`, before the refetch resolves, so the Refresh spinner stops early
apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/dialogs/confirm_dialog.rs:87 — inline `style="display:block;margin-top:4px;"` contradicts the global-CSS-only convention; move to `.confirm-dialog__keyword input`
apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/dialogs/upload_certificate_dialog.rs:686-691 — no client-side check that `pem` is non-empty before dispatch, unlike every other dialog in the slice
apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/tabs/federated_tab.rs:216-221 — the edit form keeps only `audiences.first()`, so saving drops any additional audiences Graph returned
apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/tabs/federated_tab.rs:91-93 — the creds resource returns `Ok(Vec::new())` for a missing tenant while sibling tabs return `no_tenant()`
apps/desktop/web-rs/src/components/permission_picker.rs:76-84 — an `Effect` with no tracked signal wraps a one-shot `spawn_local`; a plain `spawn_local` at mount reads clearer

apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/tabs/owners_tab.rs:17-28 — `owner_kind` classifies by substring on `odata_type` (`contains("user")`), fragile for e.g. `#microsoft.graph.userFlow`-style types; match the full `#microsoft.graph.*` string
apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/tabs/credentials_tab.rs:220 — `display_name` for a new secret is never reset after creation, so the second secret is also named `client-secret` by default
result.coverage_notes: All files in the slice were read end to end: views/{application_list,applications_view,application_detail_pane}.rs; every file in views/tabs/ (activity, app_tab, authentication, conditional_access, credentials, enterprise_tab, expose_api, federated_scenarios, federated, mod, overview, owners, permissions, usage_panel); views/dialogs/{add_owner,confirm_dialog,create_app_dialog,migrate_legacy_scope,new_app_chooser_dialog,secret_reveal_dialog,upload_certificate_dialog,mod}.rs; components/{uri_list_editor,owner_picker,directory_search,permission_picker,group_autocomplete,vault_picker}.rs; bindings/{mod,common,applications,credentials,expose_api,permissions,consent,keyvault}.rs; docs/architecture/frontend-workspace.md. Cross-checks were done by grep/sed only (no cargo commands run) into: util.rs, state/{navigation,open_items,mod}.rs, components/ui/{copyable_id,callout,copy_icon_button}.rs, components/modal_shell.rs, components/filter_{chip,toggle}.rs, scope_badge.rs (selected fns), core/scoping.rs (selected fns), dto/permissions.rs (GrantResult/DowngradeOutcome), src-tauri commands/expose_api.rs::set_identifier_uris and commands/applications/mod.rs::list_applications_with_pairing, repo_invariants/commands.rs (the resource-blind gate test), and test names in tests/gui/. Not read: styles.css, scope_wizard.rs, exchange_scoping_section.rs, the enterprise detail pane, and the remaining bindings files outside the slice (only grepped for duplicate arg structs). Leptos Suspense-vs-Transition refetch behaviour was not verified by running the app; the remount claim relies on the code authors' own comments in credentials_tab.rs and the `Suspend` construction in the pane.

result.area_summary: The fe-core slice is in good shape structurally: TenantScopedUi::reset() covers every declared field and the pinning test asserts all 22 of them, the open-items working set has a single write path with tenant-keyed localStorage persistence pinned by a cross-tenant test, and the error sink (report_command_error_for → dead-session → consent → plain toast) is coherent and tested. Weak spots are at the seams between these well-designed pieces: two one-shot deep-link signals leak when the target pane is already mounted, the `/` shortcut picks the first filter input in DOM order instead of the first visible one (broken under keep-alive), the inline-error `CommandState::run` path skips the dead-session recovery the sink promises, and the toast stack neither dedupes nor protects sticky recovery toasts from the drop-oldest cap. styles.css carries ~80 lines of dead rules (an old command palette, owner list, MI scope panel, kbd chip) plus one undefined token, and frontend-workspace.md has drifted from the open-items code it describes.

findings.title: Deep-link pending tab leaks into the next mounted pane when the target item is already open
findings.rationale: Panes are keep-alive (keyed <For> over open_items) and consume `pending_app_tab` / `pending_enterprise_tab` once on mount. When the credential dashboard or a finding calls `open_app_on_tab(id, "credentials")` for an app whose pane is ALREADY open, `open_item` dedupes and re-focuses without remounting, so the pending signal is never consumed. It stays `Some("credentials")` until the next app-reg pane mounts — i.e. the next unrelated app the operator opens from the list lands on the Credentials tab instead of their last-used tab. Same for `open_enterprise_on_tab` (line 117). The MI variant (`last_mi_tab`) is immune because it sets the persistent last-tab rather than a one-shot.
findings.proposal: In `open_app_on_tab` / `open_enterprise_on_tab`, only set the pending signal when `self.is_open(kind, &id).is_none()` (an already-open pane keeps its live tab, which is what the MI variant's doc already says is intended). Add a unit test in state/mod.rs: open app-1, call `open_app_on_tab(app-1, "credentials")`, assert `pending_app_tab` is `None`.

findings.title: `/` shortcut targets the first filter input in DOM order, so it no-ops once any earlier keep-alive pane has been visited
findings.rationale: `query_selector` returns the FIRST match in document order and the code then bails if that one element is hidden, rather than searching for the first laid-out match as the comment intends. Under keep-alive the App Registrations pane (placeholder "Filter App Registrations…") precedes Enterprise Apps, Managed Identities and Security in the DOM, so after visiting App Registrations once, pressing `/` on any later view finds the hidden Apps input, sees `offset_parent() == None`, and does nothing. Also, two of the three selector alternates (`input.search-input__field`, `.search-input input`) match nothing — the only `search-input*` class in src is `search-input__clear` — so only the placeholder heuristic is live. The GUI test (tests/gui/shortcuts.rs) only covers the negative case (no fire while typing), so this is untested.
findings.proposal: Use `query_selector_all` on `input[placeholder^='Filter']` and pick the first element whose `offset_parent()` is `Some`; drop the two dead selector alternates (or give `SearchInput` a real `search-input__field` class and match that). Add a GUI test that mounts two filter inputs with the first inside `display:none` and asserts `/` focuses the second.

findings.title: `CommandState::run` (inline-error path, 24 call sites) never offers the dead-session Re-authenticate recovery
findings.rationale: `run` was taught to raise the consent toast because 'the inline message can never resolve' a missing consent — but a dead session (`refresh_missing` / `not_signed_in`) is exactly as unresolvable inline, and the sink's own doc says inline-affordance surfaces must call `report_if_session_dead` first. Every form modal / tab mutation using `cmd.run(...)` (24 sites) on an expired session shows only the raw backend message in red with no Re-authenticate action; the operator's only route is to find the topbar Refresh-token button.
findings.proposal: In `run`'s `on_err`, call `session.report_if_session_dead(&e)` before `report_consent_required` (keep setting the inline `error` text as well), mirroring `report_command_error_for`'s ordering. Add a host unit test: `run` with an op returning `refresh_missing` pushes a toast whose `action_label == Some("Re-authenticate")`.

findings.title: Sign-in recovery hints point at 'Settings → Tenant connection', which the file itself says is unreachable before sign-in
findings.rationale: These two AADSTS hints are shown ON the sign-in card, where Settings cannot be reached; the module doc says so explicitly, and the card already renders the correct escape hatch (`Signing in to {tenant} · Change`). An operator who follows the hint looks for a Settings page that does not exist yet. The `recovery_hint` tests assert the text contains 'tenant doesn't resolve' but not the destination.
findings.proposal: Reword the 90002/900023 and 700016/700054 hints to point at the card's own affordance ('select Change above to correct the tenant/client ID'), and extend `an_aadsts_code_beats_the_generic_code_hint` to assert the hint does not mention Settings. Consider passing a `where_to_fix: &'static str` into `recovery_hint` so the same table can serve Settings → Tenant connection post-sign-in.

findings.title: Toast stack neither dedupes identical recovery toasts nor protects sticky ones from the drop-oldest cap
findings.rationale: A dead session fails every in-flight command at once (dr.rs alone has six `report_if_session_dead` call sites; the bulk bar and every `run_toast_err` route here too), so the stack fills with N identical 'Your session has expired' toasts. Worse, `drain(0..overflow)` is blind to stickiness: the sixth error evicts the first sticky Re-authenticate toast while transient 5-second successes survive. ToastHost's own rule ('errors with a retry action are sticky') is undone by the cap.
findings.proposal: In `push_toast`: (1) if a toast with the same `kind`, `message` and `action_label` is already present, return its id instead of pushing; (2) when over cap, evict non-sticky toasts (no action) first, oldest-first, and only then sticky ones. Add two host tests next to the existing toast tests.

findings.title: frontend-workspace.md describes an open-items model the code no longer has (drain-oldest, no persistence, stale state.rs path)
findings.evidence:
frontend-workspace.md:4
editing `web-rs/src/state.rs`, the shell, the list views, ...
frontend-workspace.md:114
  stack: `Vec` + seq + cap `MAX_OPEN_ITEMS = 8` + drain-oldest on overflow.

open_items.rs:87-94 (actual eviction)

                && let Some(pos) = list.iter().enumerate()
                    .min_by_key(|(_, it)| it.focused_at)
                    .map(|(pos, _)| pos)

open_items.rs:7-14 (persistence the doc never mentions)
//! The set is parked in `localStorage` between launches, under a **tenant-keyed**
//! key. That keying is not a nicety: an unkeyed snapshot restored into the next
//! tenant would reintroduce exactly the cross-tenant leak ...
findings.rationale: AGENTS.md sends every agent to this deep-dive before touching the workspace, and it currently (a) names `web-rs/src/state.rs`, which is now a `state/` directory of six files split by concern; (b) says eviction is drain-oldest with no mention of the Info toast + 'Reopen' action, when the code evicts least-recently-focused (`focused_at`) precisely because drain-oldest threw away the reference app; (c) omits the tenant-keyed `localStorage` snapshot (`azapptoolkit:workspace:{tenant_id}`), the single-write-path invariant (`update_open_items`) and the `restore_open_items_never_crosses_tenants` test — the read-side half of the #1 footgun. An agent following the doc would add a second write path or an unkeyed snapshot.
findings.proposal: Update the 'open-items workspace' section: path → `web-rs/src/state/` (mod.rs + tenant/navigation/open_items/toasts/errors), eviction → least-recently-focused with the Reopen toast, add a 'Persistence' bullet naming the key format, `update_open_items` as the only writer, `restore_open_items` as the only reader (called after the clear), the `open_seq` fast-forward, and that `OpenItemKind` variant names are a stored format. Also fix the `security_tab` comment in state/mod.rs:325-326 (lists 4 sub-tabs; the doc lists 6).

findings.title: VirtualList snaps to top on every `items` change, including a same-list refetch after a mutation
findings.rationale: The rationale ('the old offset pointed into a different list') is right for a search/facet change but wrong for the other trigger the comment lists — a refetch. After any mutation that bumps `apps_reload` / `enterprise_apps_reload` (delete, remove-expired, add owner from the pane, 'Fix' from a finding), the list resource yields a new `Arc<Vec>`, `items` changes, and the operator triaging row 3,800 of a 10k list is thrown back to row 0. This is the core 'work down a long list' workflow and the one place the frontend loses scroll state.
findings.proposal: Add an optional `reset_key: Signal<u64>` (or `Memo<(String, String, bool)>` of search/facet/extra) prop; reset scroll only when it changes, and on a plain `items` change clamp `scroll_top` to the new sizer height instead. The three call sites already own the filter signals via `use_filtered_list`. Cover with a GUI test: scroll, bump the items signal with same-length rows, assert `scrollTop` unchanged.

findings.title: ~80 lines of dead CSS: command palette, owner list, MI scope panel, kbd chip, DR secret values and others match nothing in src
findings.rationale: Global search replaced the command palette (global_search.rs owns Cmd/Ctrl-K), the enterprise owners tab no longer renders `.owner-list`, the MI pane uses `.detail-section`, the SSO wizard renders `.sso-claims` without rows, and dr.rs never renders individual secret values (only a count + 'Save the report'). None of these class names appear anywhere in Rust source or tests. Dead selectors are cheap at runtime but each is a trap for the next reader ('who uses this?') and the file is already 4,438 lines with no ownership signal.
findings.proposal: Delete the listed rules (verify `.sso-claims__row` in the 560px media block too). To stop regrowth, add a host-side unit test in web-rs (like the existing `demo_fixture_coverage.rs`) that extracts every `.class` selector from styles.css and asserts it appears in src/ as a literal or as a `{base}--` dynamic-modifier prefix, with an allowlist for `thaw-*`.

findings.title: Shortcut sheet <kbd> uses an undefined `--surface-alt` token (renders transparent) while the designed `.ui-kbd` rule sits unused
findings.rationale: `var(--surface-alt)` with no fallback and no definition makes `background` invalid-at-computed-value → `transparent`, so the key chips in the `?` sheet have a border and no fill in both themes. Meanwhile `.ui-kbd` is the finished key-chip style with the correct token and is referenced by no component.
findings.proposal: Give the `<kbd>` in shortcuts_help.rs `class="ui-kbd"` and delete the ad-hoc `.shortcuts__keys kbd` rule (or change it to `var(--bg-subtle)`). Also define or drop the other two undefined tokens used with fallbacks (`--surface-hover` at 1595, `--border-subtle` at 325) so the token set is closed.

findings.title: Two 'is the user typing?' predicates disagree: `?`/`/` are dead while a row checkbox has focus
findings.rationale: The grid hook correctly treats a bulk-select checkbox as not-a-text-field ('arrowing off it is exactly what a keyboard user expects'), but the window-level twin treats every `<input>` as typing. After Space-toggling a row checkbox, `?` (help) and `/` (focus filter) silently do nothing. The module comment forbids importing across the two hooks, but a shared leaf helper in `hooks/mod.rs` satisfies that boundary and removes the drift.
findings.proposal: Move `in_text_field` to `hooks/mod.rs` as `pub(crate) fn is_text_entry(ev)` and use it from both hooks; extend tests/gui/shortcuts.rs with a checkbox probe asserting `?` still opens the sheet.

findings.title: ModalShell hardcodes one `id="modal-shell-title"`; stacked modals get duplicate ids and both close on one Escape
findings.rationale: UpdateSplash, ReleaseNotesDialog, ShortcutsHelp and every form modal share ModalShell. Pressing `?` while any modal is open (focus on a modal button is not 'typing') stacks a second ModalShell: two elements with the same id, so `aria-labelledby` resolves to whichever the browser finds first, and the next Escape fires both `use_escape` listeners, closing the underlying dialog too.
findings.proposal: Mint a per-instance id (`StoredValue<u32>` from a static counter, or `format!("modal-title-{}", id)`), and either gate the bare `?` on `document.querySelector('[role=dialog]')` being absent or make `use_escape` only act for the topmost dialog (last `.modal-backdrop` in DOM).

findings.title: Date-range and saved-view inputs have no accessible name
findings.evidence:
date_range_filter.rs:62-68
        <div class="date-range-field">
            <label class="date-range-field__label">{label}</label>
            <div class="date-range-field__input">
                <input
                    type="date"
                    class="date-range-field__native"

saved_views.rs:113-117
                            <input
                                class="saved-views__input"
                                placeholder="View name"
                                prop:value=move || name_input.get()
findings.rationale: The `<label>` neither wraps the date input nor carries `for`/`id`, so screen readers announce two unnamed date pickers ('Created before' vs 'Created after' is exactly the distinction that matters). The saved-view name field relies on placeholder alone, which is not an accessible name. Elsewhere the slice is careful about this (every IconButton requires `aria_label`).
findings.proposal: Wrap the date `<input>` inside the `<label>` (or add `aria-label=label`), and add `aria-label="View name"` to the saved-views input. Both are one-line changes with no CSS impact.

findings.title: ExportMenu (and the account menu) claim `role="menu"` without the menu keyboard contract
findings.evidence:
export_menu.rs:67-83
            <Show when=move || open.get() fallback=|| view! { <></> }>
                <div class="export-menu__panel" role="menu">
                    {move || { options.get_value().into_iter().map(|(format, label)| {
                        view! {
                            <button type="button" role="menuitem" class="export-menu__item"
                                on:click=move |_| { open.set(false); on_select.run(format); }>

(no on:keydown, no focus() on open; shell.rs:~330 `.shell__account-menu` role="menu" is the same shape)
findings.rationale: `role="menu"` tells AT to expect the WAI-ARIA menu pattern (focus moves into the menu on open, Arrow Up/Down between items, Escape closes and returns focus). Neither menu moves focus in or handles arrows; only Escape (via `use_escape`) is implemented. The TabBar in this same slice shows the team knows the pattern; these two menus were built as plain disclosures for a documented WebView2 reason but kept the menu roles.
findings.proposal: Either drop `role=menu/menuitem` and keep `aria-expanded` on the trigger (disclosure pattern — semantically honest for what is rendered), or add a small `use_menu_keynav(panel_ref, open)` hook: focus first item on open, Arrow/Home/End roving, and restore focus to the trigger on close (reuse `use_focus_return`).

findings.title: `use_debounced` leaks one `Closure::once_into_js` per cancelled timer (every keystroke that resets the debounce)
findings.rationale: wasm-bindgen's `Closure::once_into_js` frees the Rust closure only when JS invokes it; a closure whose timer is cleared before firing is leaked for the life of the page. With a 300 ms debounce on every list filter, a fast typist cancels the pending timer on nearly every keystroke, leaking a boxed closure plus the captured `String` each time. Small per event, unbounded over a long session in a keep-alive app that never unmounts its lists. (`CopyIconButton` and `pairing.rs` also use `once_into_js`, but their timers always fire.)
findings.proposal: Keep a `StoredValue<Option<Closure<dyn FnMut()>>, LocalStorage>` alongside the handle and drop it in `clear_pending` (dropping a `Closure` invalidates the JS side), or create one persistent `Closure` per hook instance that reads the latest value from `source.get_untracked()` when it fires.

findings.title: Shell's refresh-token fallback duplicates `Session::spawn_reauth` and the two have already drifted (readiness reload)
findings.rationale: Same IPC call, same two toast strings, but the shell path bumps `readiness_reload` after a successful re-auth and the toast-action path (`report_if_session_dead` → `spawn_reauth`) does not — so re-authenticating from the recovery toast leaves a mounted Access Readiness checklist stale, while the topbar button refreshes it. A new post-re-auth side effect will have to be remembered in two places.
findings.proposal: Give `spawn_reauth` the `bump_readiness_reload()` on success and an optional `on_done: impl FnOnce(bool)` (for the shell's `reauthing` flag), then have `on_refresh_token`'s fatal branch call `session.spawn_reauth(...)` instead of re-implementing it. One home for the re-auth round trip, as the AGENTS.md 'one definition per policy' rule asks.

findings.title: Stale blanket `#![allow(dead_code)]` / `unused_imports` in icon.rs, toast.rs and ui/mod.rs hide two genuinely unused icons
findings.rationale: toast.rs's justification ('not every kind/helper has a call site yet') is no longer true — Info is used by the eviction and update toasts, Success/Error everywhere — so the allow now only masks future rot. ui/mod.rs's `unused_imports` allow is unnecessary today. icon.rs's allow hides two dead variants (`More`, `ExternalLink`); an icon catalog is a reasonable place to keep spares, but that should be an explicit per-variant `#[allow(dead_code)]` with a comment, not a file-wide blanket that also hides a dead helper fn.
findings.proposal: Remove the three module-level allows; delete `IconName::More`/`ExternalLink` or mark them individually with `#[allow(dead_code)] // kept for parity with Lucide set`. Let `just web-clippy` prove nothing else was hiding.

findings.title: `#![allow(private_interfaces)]` crate-wide is broader than needed; feature-gate module visibility instead
findings.rationale: The only consumers of the `pub` modules are the `tests/gui_*.rs` shards (25 `views::` imports), compiled with `--features test-support`; `main.rs` calls `run()` only and `demo` is in-crate. The shipped Trunk bundle therefore exports a public API nobody uses, and the crate-wide allow also silences the lint for any future accidental leak of a private type through a genuinely public item.
findings.proposal: Declare the modules twice under cfg: `#[cfg(feature = "test-support")] pub mod views;` / `#[cfg(not(feature = "test-support"))] pub(crate) mod views;` (same for components, hooks, state, util, bindings), and downgrade the allow to `#![cfg_attr(feature = "test-support", allow(private_interfaces))]`. Where a component prop type is module-private (e.g. `Route`), make it `pub(crate)` so even the test build needs no allow. Cheaper interim: move the allow from the crate root onto the `pub mod views;` / `pub mod components;` items only.

findings.title: `APPS_HARD_CAP` mirrors the backend's `APPS_MAX` by hand while the sibling lists ask the backend for the cap
findings.rationale: web-rs is outside the root workspace and cannot depend on src-tauri, so nothing pins the two 10_000s together; a backend change to `APPS_MAX` would silently make the App Registrations cap notice fire at the wrong count (or never). The Enterprise/MI lists already solved this by reading `sp_index_cap` from `get_directory_index_status`. (The comment's path is also stale: `commands/applications/mod.rs`.)
findings.proposal: Add `app_index_cap: usize` (and `app_index_truncated`) to the `DirectoryIndexStatus` DTO in azapptoolkit-dto, have the App Registrations list read it the same way `IndexCapNotice` does, and delete `APPS_HARD_CAP`. If keeping the constant, at least move it into azapptoolkit-dto so both trees share one definition.

findings.title: Saved views snapshot only facet + search; the drawer's date range is neither saved nor cleared on apply
findings.rationale: The drawer presents saved views and the created-on range as one filter set, but 'Save view' captures only two of the three inputs. A view like 'Disabled, created this quarter' cannot be saved, and applying any saved view leaves whatever date range is currently set still active — the `FilterToggle` badge keeps counting it — so the applied view shows fewer rows than when it was saved with no visible reason.
findings.proposal: Extend `SavedView` with `#[serde(default)] after: Option<NaiveDate>, before: Option<NaiveDate>` (backward-compatible with existing localStorage payloads), thread the two range signals from `ListScaffold` into `SavedViews`, write them on save and set them (including to `None`) on apply.

findings.title: Restored working set is not clamped to `MAX_OPEN_ITEMS`
findings.rationale: The cap is an invariant of the in-memory set, but the snapshot is trusted as-is. A snapshot written by a build with a larger cap (or a hand-edited/corrupted-but-valid JSON) restores >8 chips, and because `open_item` evicts exactly one per open, the dock stays over cap indefinitely. Cheap to close and keeps the 'restore cannot violate the model' property the module otherwise enforces.
findings.proposal: After decoding, sort by `focused_at` descending, `truncate(MAX_OPEN_ITEMS)`, and dedupe by `(kind, entity_id)` before `set`. Add an assertion to `restore_open_items_never_crosses_tenants` (or a new test) that a 9-item snapshot restores 8.

result.coverage_notes: Every file in the slice was read end to end: lib.rs, main.rs, constants.rs, util.rs; state/{mod,tenant,navigation,open_items,toasts,errors}.rs; all 11 hooks; all 15 components/ui files; the 20 listed components (toast, icon, modal_shell, list_scaffold, virtual_list, shortcuts_help, detail_header, type_chip, filter_chip, filter_toggle, select_all_bar, saved_views, export_menu, date_range_filter, index_cap_notice, requires_role, tenant_defaults_hint, release_notes, changelog_notes, update_splash); views/{shell,sign_in,config_screen,pairing}.rs; and styles.css in full (lines 1-4438, via five sed chunks). docs/architecture/frontend-workspace.md read in full. Outside the slice I only spot-read: application_detail_pane.rs:70-100 and enterprise_application_detail_pane/mod.rs:180-200 (pending-tab consumption), home_dashboard.rs:136-150/218-232 (dialog openers), tests/gui/shortcuts.rs (whole file), auth-and-consent.md:66-82, and single grep hits elsewhere. Per the ground rules I ran no cargo build/test/clippy; the CSS dead-class analysis was a grep-based script (scratchpad/css_classes.sh) over src/**/*.rs with a `{base}--` dynamic-modifier heuristic, then each candidate was confirmed by an exact-string grep; class names assembled at runtime by any other scheme would not be detected, so the 'dead CSS' list should be re-checked with `just web-itest` after deletion.

result.area_summary: The fe-security slice is in good shape structurally: the load-bearing decisions are pure functions with unit tests (filter::matches_finding / issue_lines_for, groups::group_findings / group_remediation_kinds, row::pick / target_tab, scope_wizard::cart_mechanism, scope_badge::scope_cell_for, the eight bulk parse_* helpers), the three workbench invariants hold (filtering has exactly two homes, BulkActionBar is the only bulk caller, BulkAction::Grant is never passed on an audit surface), and the "structured signals" rule is followed for every finding key that has a structured field. The weak spots are disclosure and consistency: a truncated or degraded run with findings is shown with no caveat anywhere on screen (only the cancelled case reaches the posture strip, and the truncated/degraded text lives in the no-findings branch), the Permissions-tab AAP migration toasts success on a `partial` report that the sibling audit dialog correctly keeps inline, the wizard's SharePoint/item paths have no way back from the org-wide radio, and the documented "adding a mechanism touches exactly three places" is overstated by roughly a factor of three. The two 1200-1500-line components split cleanly along existing seams, and the same consent-callout and mailbox-group-input markup is hand-rolled in 8 and 4 places respectively.

findings.title: Truncated/degraded runs with findings show no coverage caveat anywhere on screen; only `cancelled` reaches the posture strip
findings.evidence:
security_view.rs 220-226:
    ctrl.result.with(|r| {
        r.as_ref()
            .filter(|r| r.cancelled)
            .map(|r| (r.items.len(), r.total_apps))
    })
findings.rs 107,126-129 (the ONLY place `truncated` is rendered):
    {(!any_findings).then(|| { ... if truncated { view! { <Callout tone="warn"> "No actionable findings among the applications this scan reached — but the tenant holds more app registrations than one run scores..."
src-tauri commands/audit.rs 607-610: "the posture strip's cancelled callout, the Findings pane's truncated callout and degraded lede"
findings.rationale: AGENTS.md and audit-findings-and-remediation.md promise "a cancelled/truncated/degraded run is never ... shown as all-clear". The truncated callout is inside the `(!any_findings)` branch, so a truncated run that DOES have findings renders its groups, counts and every "Fix all N" over an arbitrary prefix with no notice at all; the All-apps pane renders none of the three caveats. The export (`coverage_sentences`) is more honest than the screen: it emits the truncated and degraded sentences unconditionally. The strip's own comment ("every number on this workbench ... is computed over that prefix") applies equally to truncated.
findings.proposal: In `PostureStrip` replace the cancelled-only callout with one driven by `r.coverage()`: when `!is_complete()`, render one line per caveat using the same sentences as the backend's `coverage_sentences` (cancelled with scored/total, truncated, degraded list). Keep FindingsPane's degraded lede or drop it to avoid a duplicate; keep the no-findings branch's warn-vs-ok tone logic. Add a GUI case with `truncated: true` and populated items asserting the callout text appears on both panes (the strip is above both).

findings.title: Exchange scoping section toasts "Migrated" on a `partial` AAP report (gate ignores item status, `incomplete`, `unattempted`); the audit dialog gates correctly
findings.rationale: The doc says `AapMigrationReportView`'s "one job is that a `partial` status never reads as success" and that partial means "kept the legacy policy because a grant is still org-wide". The operator walks away believing the app is migrated while the policy is the only thing still confining it. The toast noun is also wrong: `items` are per-app, not per-policy.
findings.proposal: Add `pub fn is_clean(&self) -> bool` on `AapMigrationReport` (or a free fn next to `AapMigrationReportView`) = `!dry_run && failures.is_empty() && !incomplete && unattempted.is_empty() && !items.is_empty() && items.iter().all(|i| i.status == "migrated")`; use it in both `do_migrate` and `migrate_legacy_scope.rs` so the two surfaces cannot disagree. In the section, keep `mig_result` inline unless clean. Toast "Migrated N app(s) / removed M policy(ies)" using `items.len()` and `Σ removed_policies.len()`. Unit-test `is_clean` on a partial item, an incomplete run, and an unattempted tail.

findings.title: ScopeWizard: selecting "Org-wide" on a SharePoint or SharePoint-item cart is a one-way door (no radio to return to Sites/Items mode)

findings.title: ScopeWizard preseed uses `scope_kind_for` while `mechanism` uses `cart_mechanism`; a non-Application/unscopable preseed leaves a scoped `scope_mode` with `mechanism == None` and a silent no-op Grant button
findings.evidence:
484-490 (preseed): if let Some(k) = scope_kind_for(Some(&sel.resource_app_id), &sel.permission_value) { ... scope_mode.set(default_mode(k)); } selected.set(vec![sel]); step.set(1);
392-404 cart_mechanism additionally requires `item.kind == PermissionKind::Application` (returns None for Delegated)
541-546 run_apply: let plan = if mode == ScopeMode::OrgWide { Plan::OrgWide } else { let Some(kind) = mechanism.get_untracked() else { return; }; ...
604: _ => return,
734-740 review_line matches scope_mode alone: ScopeMode::Managed | Existing => "Grant {perms}, scoped to the chosen mailbox group(s)..."
findings.rationale: `scope_mode` and `mechanism` are two independent signals that must agree, and the preseed path sets one from a predicate looser than the other's. A delegated `Mail.Read` preseed (or any future caller passing an unscopable row) leaves `scope_mode = Managed` with `mechanism = None`: step 2 shows the "can't be scoped together" hint but no org-wide callout, step 3's review claims the grant is scoped and the strip warning appears, and "Grant access" returns silently at the `else { return; }` with no error. Today's three callers (permissions_tab, enterprise permissions, MI pane) gate on scopable Application rows, so the bug is latent, but the wizard is the shared shell and has no defence.
findings.proposal: Introduce `let effective_mode = Signal::derive(move || if mechanism.get().is_none() { ScopeMode::OrgWide } else { scope_mode.get() })` and read it in `run_apply`, `review_line`, `review_targets`, `strip_warning`, `targets_label`, `consent_and_retry` and the radios; in the preseed effect use `cart_mechanism(&[sel.clone()])` instead of `scope_kind_for`. Replace the two silent `return`s (546, 604) with `error.set(Some("This selection can only be granted org-wide — go back and choose Org-wide."))`. Unit-test that a delegated preseed yields `None` and the derived mode is OrgWide.

findings.title: Doc claim "add a ScopeKind variant + a target panel + a Step-3 apply arm — nothing else branches on the concrete mechanism" is wrong: the wizard branches in ~10 places
findings.evidence:
docs/architecture/audit-findings-and-remediation.md ("The scope registry + the mechanism-dispatched wizard"): "**To teach the app a new mechanism**: add a `ScopeKind` variant + a target panel + a Step-3 apply arm — nothing else branches on the concrete mechanism."
scope_wizard.rs mechanism-specific branches: 83 fn default_mode(kind) match; 484-488 preseed `if k == ScopeKind::SharePoint { site_write.set(..) }`; 507 toggle `Some(ScopeKind::SharePoint) => {`; 548-604 Plan match on (kind, mode); 655 consent_and_retry match on ScopeKind; 782/819/828 three per-mechanism <Show> blocks; 687 targets_label, 698 review_targets, 722 strip_warning, 734 review_line all match ScopeMode (whose variants Managed/Existing/Sites/Items are per-mechanism); 866 hint text names each mechanism.
findings.rationale: `grep -c "ScopeKind::"` in scope_wizard.rs is 18. `ScopeMode` itself is a per-mechanism enum (Managed/Existing are Exchange, Sites is SharePoint, Items is SharePointItem), so every match on it is a mechanism branch. A contributor following the doc would add a variant and panel, get a non-exhaustive-match compile error in `default_mode` and the Plan match, and still silently miss the review strings, the consent feature key, the Step-1 Show block and the radio (see the SharePoint one-way-door finding, which is exactly this drift). The `admin_applicable() == false` seam the doc mentions for Teams RSC is not wired into the wizard at all.
findings.proposal: Either correct the doc to enumerate the real touch points, or make the claim true: a `struct MechanismSpec { default_mode, modes: &'static [(ScopeMode, &'static str)], consent_feature: &'static str, targets_label, review_scoped_line, strips_orgwide: bool }` looked up by `ScopeKind` (in core::scoping or a `scope_wizard/mechanisms.rs`), with the radios, review facts, consent key and Step-1 panel dispatch all reading the spec so only `apply_*` and the panel component remain per-mechanism. The refactor also naturally handles `admin_applicable() == false` (render guidance, hide apply).

findings.title: Split bulk_action_bar.rs (1546 lines) along its existing seams and fold the two remaining per-action matches into `Spec`
findings.rationale: The file holds four independent concerns: the action catalog (`BulkAction`/`Spec`/`Confirm`, ~120 lines), the pure result parsing (`Parsed`, `BulkRow`, `failures_of`, `unattempted_note`, `session_dead_error`, eight `parse_*`, ~300 lines) plus ~400 lines of tests for it, `BulkProgressRow` (~80 lines), and the `BulkActionBar` component + `armed_panel` (~600 lines). The Spec comment explains why parallel matches are a hazard, yet `confirm_label` and `description` are still two of them (a new action compiles without a confirm label only because `match` is exhaustive — but the copy is scattered across 700 lines).
findings.proposal: Create `components/bulk_action_bar/{mod.rs, actions.rs, parse.rs, progress.rs}`: `actions.rs` owns `BulkAction`, `Confirm`, `Spec` extended with `confirm_label: &'static str` and `description: fn(usize) -> String`; `parse.rs` owns `Parsed`, `BulkRow`, `failures_of`, `unattempted_note`, `session_dead_error`, the `parse_*` fns and their tests; `progress.rs` owns `BulkProgressRow`; `mod.rs` keeps `BulkActionBar`, `ArmedPanel`, `armed_panel` and re-exports `BulkAction`, `BulkFailure`, `BulkProgressRow`, `session_dead_error` so the four hosts (`audit_view`, `application_list`, `bulk_actions_view`, `sso_certificates_dashboard`) need no import changes.

findings.title: `ALL_ACTIONS` test table omits `StageSsoCertificate`, so the spec-coherence tests are not exhaustive-by-construction; the RemoveRedundant carve-out is unexplained
findings.rationale: groups.rs's sibling test pins every `RemediationKind` "exhaustive by construction: a new variant won't compile until it is listed"; this one silently skipped the last variant added. `every_action_has_a_coherent_spec` (label non-empty, keywords unique/uppercase) and `destructive_actions_are_keyword_gated` therefore never ran for StageSsoCertificate, and the next variant will be skipped the same way. The `RemoveRedundant` exemption from "destructive ⇒ keyword" has no comment stating why (presumably: the backend re-plans and only removes covered permissions, so it is safe-by-construction), so a reviewer cannot tell a deliberate exception from an oversight.
findings.proposal: Add `impl BulkAction { pub const ALL: [BulkAction; 9] = [...]; }` beside the enum plus a `#[test] fn all_is_exhaustive()` that `match`es every variant (non-exhaustive match = compile error on a new variant) and asserts `ALL.len()` equals the arm count; use `BulkAction::ALL` in the tests. Document the RemoveRedundant exception in `Spec` and in the test (or promote it to `Confirm::Keyword("REMOVE")`-style gating if the exception is not intended).

findings.title: No GUI test renders a cancelled, truncated or degraded audit run — the "never shown as all-clear" invariant is unpinned at the UI layer

findings.title: posture.rs, row.rs and findings.rs re-implement finding predicates and tone mapping that `filter.rs`/`groups.rs` already own

findings.title: `UNCONFINABLE_MAILBOX` / `UNCONFINABLE_SHAREPOINT` issues belong to no finding group, so the findings-first pane hides them
findings.rationale: The scorer deliberately splits org-wide mailbox reach into confinable (`ORG_WIDE_MAILBOX` → Fix) and unconfinable (`UNCONFINABLE_*` → remove the grant). The Findings pane — the default, "remediation-centric" view — has a group for the first and none for the second, so a principal whose only mailbox problem is a legacy Exchange Online `Mail.Read` grant (which `reconcile_orgwide_grant` treats as reaching every mailbox) is invisible there unless it also trips another rule. Advisory groups (`high_risk_perms`, `external_exposure`) already exist for exactly this "visible with Open, no bulk fix" shape.
findings.proposal: Add `GroupSpec { key: "unconfinable_orgwide", title: "Org-wide access RBAC cannot confine", tab: "permissions", section: Actionable }` with an `issue_marker` arm `|x| x.starts_with(issue::UNCONFINABLE_MAILBOX) || x.starts_with(issue::UNCONFINABLE_SHAREPOINT)`, no bulk action and no remediation kind (so `every_remediation_kind_is_owned_by_exactly_one_group` is unaffected); add it to `PostureCounts` and to `issue_marker_findings_match_exactly_their_finding`. Blurb should point at `LegacyExchangeGrantsCallout`'s advice (remove the grant / re-declare on Graph).

findings.title: AuditController seeds the synthetic first progress event with `in_flight_cap: 8`, duplicating the backend's `INITIAL_CONCURRENCY`; a downward change there makes the rate-limit notice fire on every scan
findings.evidence:
controller.rs 187-193: self.progress.set(Some(AuditProgress { done: 0, total: 0, current_app: None, in_flight_cap: 8, cancelled: false }));
controller.rs 72-75: Effect::new(move |_| match progress.get() { Some(p) => peak_cap.update(|peak| *peak = (*peak).max(p.in_flight_cap)), ... })
security_view.rs 203: <Show when=move || cap < peak_cap.get()> ... "Microsoft Graph is rate-limiting this scan"
src-tauri commands/audit.rs 76,133,287: const INITIAL_CONCURRENCY: usize = 8; ... FanOutMeter::attach(client.clone(), INITIAL_CONCURRENCY); ... in_flight_cap: meter.limit(),
findings.rationale: `peak_cap` is documented as a high-water mark of the backend's live cap, but the frontend pre-loads it with a literal 8 that only happens to equal `INITIAL_CONCURRENCY`. If the backend constant is ever lowered (or made tenant-adaptive), the first real event's `cap < 8` and the "Graph is rate-limiting" notice shows on a healthy scan.
findings.proposal: Seed `in_flight_cap: 0` (so `peak_cap` only tracks backend events), or make the synthetic progress carry no cap (`Option<usize>` like `BulkProgress`) and hide the cap/notice until the first backend event; the progress bar still renders from `done/total`.

Out-of-slice files were consulted only partially for cross-checks: views/tabs/permissions_tab.rs (lines 970-1000 + greps), views/dialogs/migrate_legacy_scope.rs (78-92 + greps), views/managed_identity_detail_pane.rs (grep), state/{mod,navigation,tenant}.rs (grep), src-tauri commands/audit.rs (76-82, 270-292, 600-640), core throttle.rs and audit/scoring.rs (grep + 340-372), dto audit.rs/exchange.rs/consent.rs (grep). GUI tests (tests/gui/security_audit.rs, security_findings.rs, scope_wizard.rs) were grepped, not read in full. No cargo commands were run, per instructions.

result.area_summary: The enterprise/SSO slice is mature and heavily annotated: the rollover panel derives phase from live state, the SSO certificate board keeps SP ids in their own selection set (verified: `selected_sso_cert_ids` feeds only `BulkAction::StageSsoCertificate` → `bulk_stage_sso_certificates`), the claims editor's TransformationMethod list matches Microsoft's reference, and destructive flows (delete SP, remove assignment, revoke, delete role, remove owner) are consistently staged behind `ConfirmDialog`. The weak spots cluster in the SSO tab: a claims policy the backend could not read (consent-gated read) is indistinguishable from "no policy", so the editor renders empty and a Save detaches the real policy; the "Rotate and activate immediately" reveal is torn down by the `reload` bump it triggers, losing the show-once certificate; rotate/retire have no confirmation; and the tab makes the same Graph chain twice plus a third SP read. Around it are primitive-reuse gaps (hand-rolled owner search, raw `error [code]` text instead of `DetailLoadError`, a private `CopyBlock`), a truncating expiry helper that the architecture docs explicitly call out as a bug class, and the wizard's documented but still-pending UriListEditor migration plus stale reset/rationale comments.

findings.title: SSO tab renders an unreadable claims policy as an empty editor; Save then detaches the real policy
findings.rationale: `SsoConfigDto.claims_policy` is `None` both when no policy is assigned AND when the read failed (the DTO doc at crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/sso.rs:297-299 says so). Because `list_assigned_claims_mapping_policies` requires `policy_write_token()`, every operator who has not yet consented `Policy.ReadWrite.ApplicationConfiguration` sees an EMPTY "Attributes & claims" editor for an app that has a custom policy. Clicking "Save claims" (e.g. to add one claim) triggers the consent flow, then `set_claims_mapping` detaches every existing policy and recreates one from the empty/partial editor — silently deleting the app's configured claims. Nothing in the UI warns that the current state was never loaded.
findings.proposal: Add a discriminator to `SsoConfigDto` (e.g. `claims_policy_unavailable: bool` or `claims_read_error: Option<UiError>`) set in `get_sso_config`'s `Err` arm. In `SsoEditor`, when it is set: render a `Callout tone="warn"` ("Couldn't read the current claims policy — grant consent to load it before editing") with a "Load claims" button that calls `request_scope_consent(.., "policy_write")` and bumps `reload`, and disable "Save claims" until a successful read. Add a GUI test: mock `get_sso_config` with the flag set and assert Save is disabled and no `set_claims_mapping` call happens. Expected effect: no path from an unread policy to a detach.

findings.title: "Rotate and activate immediately" reveals the show-once certificate, then the reload it triggers tears the reveal down
findings.rationale: Bumping the outer `reload` refetches `config`, the Suspense drops the current `SsoEditor`, and a fresh one is built with `rotated_cert = None` — so the `<pre class="secret-reveal">` at lines 766-774 is gone before the operator can copy it. This is the big-bang path where sign-in is already broken until the app owner installs the new certificate, and the base64 is exactly what they need. The staged path does not have this bug because `SigningCertRolloverPanel` bumps its own `reload` and `staged_pem` lives outside that Suspense. No GUI test covers the rotate reveal (grep for "Rotate and activate" in tests finds nothing).
findings.proposal: Lift `rotated_cert` (and `cert_subject`) to `SsoContent` and pass them into `SsoEditor`, or stop bumping the outer `reload` on rotate and instead bump a rollover-panel reload exposed via a shared `RwSignal<u32>` prop (the rotation only changes SP key state, which the rollover panel re-reads). Render the reveal through the shared `CopyBlock` (see the separate finding). Add a `sso_rollover.rs` GUI test: mock `rotate_saml_signing_certificate` with `base64: Some(..)`, click the button, assert `pre.secret-reveal` still contains it after the mocked reload resolves.

Contrast mod.rs:373-385 (delete SP: ConfirmDialog + typed DELETE for foreign SPs), access.rs:270-286, permissions.rs:315-332, app_roles.rs:453-464 — all stage a ConfirmDialog.

docs/architecture/auth-and-consent.md:191-193: "because the superseded certificate *is* the rollback, retiring is what ends the ability to revert, so it stays an explicit action."
findings.rationale: The backend doc for `rotate_saml_signing_certificate` calls it a "big-bang rotation" that stops sign-in for any app holding a static certificate; retire is the one action that permanently ends the rollback path. Both are irreversible and sit next to a Primary "Stage new certificate" button, yet neither asks for confirmation, unlike the remove-owner/assignment/revoke/delete flows in the same pane. An operator who mis-clicks rotate breaks SSO for every user of that app; the frontend-workspace.md guidance reserves the un-confirmed treatment for reversible actions (Disable sign-in).
findings.proposal: Stage `pending_rotate: RwSignal<bool>` and `pending_retire: RwSignal<Option<(thumbprint, key_id)>>` and reuse `ConfirmDialog` (subject = app display name / thumbprint; body restates the outage risk; consider `require_keyword="ROTATE"` for the big-bang path, matching the bulk-bar destructive treatment). Keep Remove-expired one-click (dead weight, documented). Update the sso_rollover GUI tests to click through the dialog.

findings.title: Certificate reveals are a bare <pre> with no copy/save; the existing CopyBlock is private and hand-rolls the clipboard call
findings.rationale: The staged/rotated public certificate is the artefact the app owner must receive, and the UI asks the operator to "upload this to the application" while offering no copy button, no label and no file save. `sso_summary::CopyBlock` is the codebase's primitive for exactly this (label + hint + pre + Copy) but is `fn` (private), and it duplicates the clipboard code `util::copy_text` claims to centralise. There are 12 `save_*_to_file` commands but none for a certificate, so an operator has to paste base64 into a file by hand to produce the `.cer` most SaaS admin consoles expect.
findings.proposal: Make `CopyBlock` `pub` and use it for both reveals in sso_tab.rs (label "New signing certificate (Base64)", hint about uploading). Route `CopyBlock`'s copy through `util::copy_text` (extend it to return the `JsFuture`/accept an on-done callback so the "Copied" state still works). Add a backend `save_certificate_to_file(base64, suggested_name)` command writing PEM (`-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----`, 64-col wrapped) via the OS save dialog, exposed as a "Save as .cer" button beside Copy.

findings.title: Opening the SSO tab runs the SP→app→app-SSO Graph chain twice and reads the SP a third time
findings.rationale: `get_sso_config` is get_service_principal_sso_fields + list_assigned_claims_mapping_policies + find_application_by_app_id + get_application_sso_fields (3-4 serial Graph calls). `get_sso_summary` re-runs all of it just to wrap the same fields in `SamlSsoSummary`/`OidcSsoSummary`, whose extra fields (`saml_summary_urls`, `oidc_summary_urls`) are pure functions of tenant id + app id. The rollover panel then fetches the SP fields a third time. Every SSO tab open is therefore ~8 Graph requests for data the tab already holds, and the summary crosses IPC as an untagged `serde_json::Value` that the frontend re-deserialises and swallows on mismatch.
findings.proposal: Either (a) have `get_sso_config` return the summary (or the `SigningCertRolloverDto`) as fields of `SsoConfigDto`, so one command feeds the whole tab, or (b) build the summary client-side from `SsoConfigDto` + the static URL formulas (move `saml_summary_urls`/`oidc_summary_urls` into `azapptoolkit-dto` so both trees share them). Delete `get_sso_summary` (and its binding) or type it as `#[serde(tag = "protocol")] enum SsoSummary { Saml(..), Oidc(..) }`. Expected effect: ~2x fewer Graph calls per SSO tab open and no double parse.

findings.title: Enterprise Credentials expiry badge truncates days ("0d left" for an expired credential) and is the fourth independent expiry helper
findings.rationale: `Duration::num_days()` truncates toward zero, so a credential that expired anywhere in the last 24h yields `days == 0`, misses the `< 0` arm and renders "0d left" — the exact misread the architecture doc says the backend was fixed to avoid. The enterprise pane's `cred_status`, the app-reg `credentials_tab::days_until`, `application_list.rs` and the two dashboards each carry their own copy of the thresholds and formatting, so the fix has to be made in five places and "Expiring Soon" can drift between boards (the auth doc's stated reason for reusing `EXPIRY_WARNING_DAYS`).
findings.proposal: Add one `util::days_until(end) -> Option<i64>` using `(end - now).num_seconds().div_euclid(86_400)` and one `components::ui::expiry_badge(days: Option<i64>)` that imports `azapptoolkit_core::audit::EXPIRY_WARNING_DAYS` (and a new `EXPIRY_CRITICAL_DAYS = 7` in core). Replace `cred_status`, `credentials_tab::{days_until,status_label,status_badge}`, the `application_list.rs` inline format and the two dashboards' `status_badge`. Add a unit test that an `end` 12h in the past renders "Expired".
