findings.rationale: An enterprise app assigned per-user (common for SaaS SSO apps) has hundreds to thousands of `appRoleAssignedTo` rows; the backend pages them all and the tab then paints one giant `<table>` with no search box, while the sibling lists virtualise. Because `principal_id` is dropped in `list_enterprise_app_assignments`, the DirectorySearch cannot grey out or hide principals already assigned (the Owners tab does that filter manually), so a duplicate assignment attempt round-trips to a generic Graph error. `ShowMore` (components/ui/show_more.rs) is the documented windowed-list primitive and is already used by the resource_access views.
findings.proposal: Add `principal_id` to `AppAssignmentDto` (a one-line copy in list_enterprise_app_assignments). In AccessContent: pass `exclude=Signal::derive(move || assigned_ids)` to `DirectorySearch`; add a client-side filter `<Input>` (name/type/role) over the loaded list and wrap the table in `ShowMore` with a 100-row window. Optionally show a role facet. Expected effect: usable on large apps, no duplicate-assignment errors.

findings.title: Access tab role picker offers app roles whose allowedMemberTypes exclude users/groups
findings.rationale: The Access tab only ever assigns users or groups (`DirectoryScope::Users|Groups`), but the picker lists every enabled role including Application-only roles (`allowedMemberTypes == ["Application"]`). Graph rejects such an assignment with an opaque 400, surfaced here as `error.set(Some(e.message))` after the confirm dialog — the operator has no hint which roles are valid for principals.
findings.proposal: Filter `role_options` to roles whose `allowed_member_types` contains `"User"` (and keep Default access); render excluded roles as `<option disabled>` with "(applications only)" so they remain discoverable. Add a unit test on the filter predicate.

findings.title: List-load failures in the enterprise pane render raw `error [code]: message` text without Retry instead of the DetailLoadError primitive
findings.rationale: Four list loads in one pane violate the documented one-primitive rule and give a transient 429/network failure no in-context Retry (the operator must switch tabs or hit the header Refresh). The `error [code]: message` format also leaks the machine code into body text, unlike every other surface. The correct primitive is already imported into `mod.rs` and used by two sibling tabs.
findings.proposal: Replace the four `Err(e)` arms with `<DetailLoadError error=e on_retry=Callback::new(move |_| reload.update(|n| *n += 1)) />` (each tab already owns a `reload` signal). Consider extending the repo_invariants callout scan to flag `class="form-error"` inside a `Suspend` `Err` arm.

findings.title: Both Owners tabs hand-roll the debounced user search that DirectorySearch provides (and the Access tab in the same pane already uses)
findings.rationale: `DirectorySearch` exists precisely to be "the" directory typeahead (debounce, min-length gate, Suspense, exclusion set, per-row disabled state, action label); the Access tab two tabs over uses it. Both Owners tabs instead carry ~80 lines of the same machinery, a different error class, and re-implement `exclude` by hand — so behaviour (2-char gate wording, spinner vs skeleton, keyboard handling) drifts between tabs of one pane and any fix lands in three places.
findings.proposal: Replace the query/candidates/Suspense block in both `owners.rs` and `tabs/owners_tab.rs` with `<DirectorySearch scope=Users exclude=existing_owner_ids query=raw_query clear_on_pick=false on_pick=... row_disabled=... label="Search users by name or UPN (2+ chars)" />`, keep the Add-default-owners button and the ConfirmDialog. Update any GUI tests that reference `.candidates`.

findings.title: Gallery create and the SSO wizard discard the created service-principal id — no post-create navigation to the SSO tab the hint promises
findings.rationale: After a gallery instantiate the operator's next step is, per the dialog's own hint, the new app's SSO tab — but the dialog just closes with no toast and no selection, leaving them to find the new row in a list that may be thousands long (and only after `bump_enterprise_apps` refetches). The wizard likewise ends on a summary with no way to open the app it just created. `session.open_enterprise_on_tab` is one call away and even sets `pending_enterprise_tab`.
findings.proposal: Gallery: in `on_ok`, `session.toast_success(format!("{} created.", s.display_name)); session.open_enterprise_on_tab(s.service_principal_id, "sso");` before `on_close`. Wizard step 3: add an "Open application" primary button next to Done that calls `open_enterprise_on_tab(summary.service_principal_id, "sso")` (SAML) or `"overview"` (OIDC) and then `close()`. Extend the gallery GUI test to assert `open_items` contains the new SP.

The review step, whose purpose is a last check before creating an app that is never auto-deleted on partial failure (backend comment: "a failure leaves a half-configured app"), does not show lifetimes, logout URL, redirect URIs, notification emails or the claims count. The three list fields are the migration the architecture doc explicitly lists as outstanding, and the notification-email rule is now written twice in the frontend and once in the backend while the SSO tab's own list has no validator.

(2) Add a shared `notification_email_reason: UriValidator` (contains '@', no whitespace) in `uri_list_editor.rs` and use `UriListState::validated` for the wizard's emails and the SSO tab's list; keep the count check as a `Callout` when `> 5`. (3) Migrate `redirect_uris`/`spa_uris` to `UriListEditor` with `redirect_uri_reason`, removing `lines_to_vec`. (4) Render every field in the review `<dl>`, including "Custom claims: N rows" and "Notification emails: a, b". Update frontend-workspace.md to drop the "one remaining migration" sentence.

findings.title: Wizard reset() and ClaimsEditorState::reset() rationale is stale — tool_dialog unmounts the dialog on close, so no instance is reused across opens
findings.rationale: Since `tool_dialog` renders nothing while the flag is false, closing the wizard drops the whole component and every signal in it; the next open constructs a fresh `SsoWizardDialog` and a fresh `ClaimsEditorState::empty()`. The `reset()` code path is therefore redundant, and its doc comment describes a reuse model (and a bug) that cannot occur under the current mount — a future reader will "fix" the wrong thing. The `Effect` at lines 78-92 that seeds emails "when the wizard opens" likewise runs exactly once at mount.
findings.proposal: Delete `SsoWizardDialog::reset` and `ClaimsEditorState::reset` (keep `close = on_close.run`), turn the seed `Effect` into a one-shot `spawn_local` at construction, and add a doc line matching gallery_dialog.rs ("mounted only while open; each open is a fresh component"). If a persistent-mount use is intended elsewhere, instead correct the comments to name that mount site.

findings.title: The basic-claim override test seeds from BASIC_CLAIM_SET[0], the one row the UI never offers (non-overridable placeholder URI)
findings.rationale: The test's stated purpose is to pin that the override buttons seed a correct SAML URI, but it exercises the single row whose `overridable` flag hides the button and whose "URI" is documented as a human-readable placeholder. It passes while asserting `saml_claim_type == "nameid (format emailAddress)"` — a value that must never reach Graph — and would keep passing if the four real rows' URIs were corrupted.
findings.proposal: Iterate `BASIC_CLAIM_SET.iter().filter(|r| r.3)` (or use index 1, `name`), assert each seeded row's `saml_claim_type` starts with `http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/` and `id == attribute`; add a second assertion that the `!overridable` entry's URI is never used as a seed (e.g. a `debug_assert!(overridable)` inside `seed_basic_override`'s call site or a test that the Name ID row yields no button).

findings.rationale: The editor drops fully blank rows but forwards half-typed ones: a row with a source attribute and no SAML/JWT claim name, a transformation-sourced claim referencing a transformation id that does not exist, or two rows with the same SamlClaimType (two clicks on "Edit") all reach `set_claims_mapping`, which has already detached the old policy before Graph rejects the new one — leaving the app with NO claims policy. Unchecking "Include the basic claim set" with nothing else defined removes name/email/givenname/surname from every assertion with no warning, which is the dangerous edit the `is_empty()` doc calls "suppressing the basic set".
findings.proposal: Add `ClaimsEditorState::problems(&self) -> Vec<String>` (reactive: reads the signals tracked) covering: row with neither SamlClaimType nor JwtClaimType; transformation source whose id matches no transform; duplicate SamlClaimType/JwtClaimType; `!include_basic && schema.is_empty()`; transform with no output claim. Render them in a `Callout tone="warn"` above the Save button in both hosts; advisory only. Additionally harden `set_claims_mapping` to create+assign the new policy BEFORE detaching the old one (Graph allows one assignment at a time, so detach → create is required, but validating the definition via a dry `create` first, then detach, then assign, avoids the no-policy end state). Unit-test `problems()`.

findings.title: Claims editor sub-row remove buttons are a bare "✕" glyph with no accessible name
findings.rationale: A screen reader announces U+2715 as "multiplication x" (or nothing), so a transformation with several inputs/parameters/outputs presents a run of identical unnamed buttons; the rest of the frontend uses `IconButton` with an explicit `aria_label` for icon-only controls, and the `.ui-icon-btn` styling the frontend doc describes for per-row destructive icons.
findings.proposal: Replace the three `"✕"` buttons with `<IconButton icon=IconName::Close aria_label=format!("Remove input claim {}", ir.reference_id.get_untracked()) title="Remove" on_click=... />` (or add `attr:aria-label` to the thaw Button). Consider the same for the row-level "Remove" buttons' subject (e.g. "Remove claim <SAML URI>") so multiple rows are distinguishable.

findings.title: sso_tab.rs packs a 370-line Suspend closure with five nested command closures; Overview's visibility toggle hand-rolls spawn_local unlike its two siblings
findings.rationale: The detail pane was already split per tab, but `sso_tab.rs` is now the largest view file in the pane and its rollover panel keeps row rendering, phase guidance and five mutations inside one async closure — every edit (e.g. adding the ConfirmDialogs above) has to thread through that closure's captures. In overview.rs the three toggles do the same thing three ways; the hand-rolled one also skips `report_command_error`'s re-auth handling path that `use_command` provides.
findings.proposal: Split into `sso_tab/{mod.rs (SsoContent+SsoEditor), rollover_panel.rs, rollover_row.rs (RolloverRow component taking a `SigningCertDto` + callbacks), phase_callout.rs}`; move `save_saml_urls`/`save_oidc_uris`/`save_notification_emails`/`save_claims` into small section components. Migrate `toggle_visibility` to `use_command().run_toast_err`. Keep `pub mod sso_tab` so `tests/gui/sso_rollover.rs` still mounts `SsoContent`.

findings.title: Stale comments after the UriListEditor migration and a stale pane module header
findings.rationale: The SSO tab no longer has textareas or one-per-line fields (they are `UriListEditor` rows), and the pane header lists four of ten tabs. The codebase leans on in-code rationale comments as documentation (AGENTS.md), so stale ones actively mislead the next editor about what the code does.

Also collapse the duplicate `badge--danger` arms at sso_tab.rs:257-258 into `Some(d) if d <= 7`.

findings.title: MI Azure RBAC assign form: eight hardcoded roles only, unvalidated free-text scope, and a consent button labelled the same as the grant wizard
findings.rationale: An admin scoping an MI to, say, `Storage Queue Data Contributor` or a custom role cannot do it here (no free GUID entry), and a scope typo (`/subscription/...`, a trailing slash, an RG path without the subscription prefix) only fails after the ARM round trip. Two buttons reading "Grant access" in one pane mean different things (consent to ARM vs open the permission wizard), which is confusing for sighted users and identical for screen readers.
findings.proposal: Add a "Custom role definition id…" option that reveals an `<Input>` validated as a GUID; validate the scope client-side against `^/subscriptions/[0-9a-f-]{36}(/resourceGroups/[^/]+(/providers/.+)?)?$` (advisory message, not a hard gate); relabel the ARM consent button "Grant consent to Azure" and keep "Grant access" for the wizard. Consider reading role definitions live via ARM `roleDefinitions?$filter=type eq 'BuiltInRole'` for the picked subscription (feature, M).

findings.title: Creation-date range filter on the Enterprise (and App Registrations) list is local state and survives a tenant switch
findings.rationale: The search and facet reset structurally on `set_active_tenant`, but a date range set in tenant A keeps filtering tenant B's list (the view stays mounted when the tenant switches while on it), with the drawer collapsed by default so only the small active-filter badge hints why rows are missing. result.area_summary: The fe-tools slice is in good shape structurally: every surface routes through Session helpers, the Resource Access panels and DR view are unusually honest about partial coverage, and the module docs record the reasoning behind most decisions. The weak spots are (1) one operator-facing claim in the DR view that the backend does not honour (a re-run restore duplicates the estate rather than "recreating only what is missing"), (2) the shared `report_if_session_dead` recovery convention being applied in only two of the nine error surfaces here, (3) a cross-tenant residue in the Key Vault browser (listed secrets survive tenant switch), and (4) an IPC layer whose error path `unwrap()`s deserialization so any non-`UiError` rejection panics the app. Test coverage is thin for exactly the surfaces with security-relevant behaviour (Key Vault reveal wipe, DR skipped-object notice, Home dashboard, cache dialog).

findings.title: DR view tells the operator a re-run restore "recreates only what is missing" — the backend creates every app unconditionally and the Restore button stays live after a run
findings.evidence:
dr.rs:502  "...Re-authenticate and run the restore again — it recreates only what is missing."
dr.rs:366  <Show when=move || plan.get().is_some() && !cloud_blocked() && !restoring.get()>
dr.rs:368      "Restore into this tenant…"
restore.rs:195-218  // ---- Pass 1: create shells ----
    for app in &backup.app_registrations {
        ...
        match create_application_core(&client, input).await {
findings.rationale: `restore_tenant` Pass 1 iterates every `app_registrations` entry and calls `create_application_core` with no lookup for an existing app by identifier URI or display name (grep for exist/duplicate in restore.rs finds nothing on the create path). So the session-expired callout's remedy — re-run the restore — creates a second copy of every app that was already created, each with a fresh appId, paired SP and regenerated secret. Independently, `plan`/`loaded` are never cleared after `report.set(Some(r))` (dr.rs:168), so the primary Restore button remains visible after a successful run and a second click duplicates the whole estate. The confirm modal (dr.rs:415) says only that nothing is overwritten or deleted, which is true but omits that duplicates are created. docs/architecture/backup-and-restore.md makes no idempotency claim; the UI does.
findings.proposal: Short term (S): change the callout to say a re-run will create the remaining apps AND re-create the ones listed above, so the operator must first delete the duplicates or edit the manifest; after `report.set(Some(r))` clear `loaded`/`plan` so the Restore button requires re-loading a file. Proper fix (M): in `restore_tenant` Pass 1, resolve each manifest app in the destination by `identifier_uris` (api://{new}) then by display name via the existing `find_application_by_app_id`/index accessors; skip a match, record it as a `ManualItem`/"already present" row, and continue wiring only the newly created ones — then the callout's promise becomes true. Add a unit test on the pure planner and a GUI test asserting the button disappears after a report renders.

findings.title: `invoke_result` unwraps the error deserialization — any rejection that is not a `UiError` JSON object panics the whole WASM app
findings.evidence:
bindings/*.rs:  use tauri_sys::core::invoke_result;   (every binding, no wrapper)
tauri-sys/src/core.rs:18-27
  pub async fn invoke_result<T, E>(command: &str, args: impl Serialize) -> Result<T, E> {
      inner::invoke_result(command, swb::to_value(&args).unwrap())
          .await
          .map(|val| swb::from_value(val).unwrap())
          .map_err(|err| swb::from_value(err).unwrap())
.claude/rules/backend-commands-and-caches.md:15  "use `invoke_result()` (never bare `invoke`, which panics on a rejected promise)"
findings.rationale: The repo's rule treats `invoke_result` as the safe path, but tauri-sys `unwrap`s `from_value::<UiError>(err)`. Tauri rejects with a plain string (not `{code,message,retryable}`) for arg-shape mismatches ("invalid args `tenantId` for command …"), unknown commands, and denied plugin permissions (e.g. if `dialog:allow-save` is ever narrowed in capabilities/default.json). Any of those turns into a `console_error_panic_hook` panic (lib.rs:69) that freezes the UI with no toast — worse than the bare-`invoke` failure the rule warns about. Nothing pins binding arg names to backend param names today (`command-parity-check.sh` checks command names only), so this is one rename away.
findings.proposal: Add `bindings::ipc::invoke_result<T: DeserializeOwned>(cmd, args) -> Result<T, UiError>` that calls `tauri_sys::core::invoke_result::<T, serde_json::Value>` and maps a value that fails `UiError` deserialization into `UiError::new("ipc", value.to_string(), false)` (also catching the success-side `from_value` failure). Mechanically switch every `use tauri_sys::core::invoke_result` in bindings/ to it, and add a repo_invariants source-scan test that bindings never import `tauri_sys::core::{invoke,invoke_result}` directly. Then `report_if_session_dead`/toasts see a real error instead of a panic.

findings.title: Key Vault browser: listed secrets, vault name and `loaded` survive a tenant switch/sign-out — only `revealed`/`error` are wiped
findings.rationale: `set_active_tenant` (state/tenant.rs:18-42) resets `tenant_ui` and sets view=Home, which does wipe `revealed` via the view-watch — but there is no `tenant.get()` dependency anywhere in this view, so tenant A's secret names, content types and expiry dates (and A's vault name in the picker) are still on screen when tenant B opens Key Vault. Clicking Reveal there sends `kv_get_secret(tenantB, vaultA, name)`. The Resource Access panels and the mailbox probe explicitly reset on `tenant.get()` for this reason ("cross-tenant leakage", mailboxes.rs:152-159); this view is the one tenant-scoped surface that does not.
findings.proposal: Either add an `Effect` tracking `session.active_tenant` that clears `listed`, `loaded`, `vault_name`, `revealed`, `error`; or (preferred, per the AGENTS.md rule that per-list state lives on `Session.tenant_ui` and resets structurally) move `vault_name`/`listed` into `TenantScopedUi` with a `reset()` line so `tenant_switch_resets_every_tenant_scoped_field` pins it. Add a GUI test: list secrets, `set_active_tenant(other)`, assert the table is empty and the vault field is blank.

findings.title: Dead-session recovery convention (`report_if_session_dead`) is applied in only 2 of the 9 error surfaces in this slice
findings.rationale: A `refresh_missing`/`not_signed_in` failure in the permission tester, any Resource Access panel, the Key Vault browser or the top-bar search renders a raw message with no Re-authenticate action; in global search it re-renders "Search failed: …" on every debounced keystroke. The DR view already shows the intended shape (`if !session.report_if_session_dead(&e) { error.set(...) }`). The `report_consent_required` twin is likewise unused where a consent feature applies (mailbox probe → "exchange").
findings.proposal: At each listed `Err(e)` arm, call `session.report_if_session_dead(&e)` first and only fall through to the inline banner when it returns false; in GlobalSearch render a single "Session expired — re-authenticate" row (and call the sink once per failure, not per keystroke — e.g. guard on `e.is_reauth_fatal()` and a `reported` flag reset when the query is cleared). Consider a repo_invariants scan: any `Err(e) => error.set(Some(e.message))` in web-rs/src/views must be preceded by the sink call.

findings.title: Restore dry-run skips the schema check and previews only app registrations — a too-new manifest passes the plan and fails only after the operator confirms
findings.rationale: `plan_restore` is documented as the operator's chance to inspect before writes (backup-and-restore.md "The frontend shows it before the operator confirms"). The cloud-mismatch blocker is computed there, but the newer-schema refusal is not, so the operator loads the file, reads a plausible plan, confirms the modal, and only then gets `schema_too_new`. The plan also says nothing about Pass 4/5 (enterprise-app access re-application, MI app-role re-binding, runbook items), even though the report afterwards has whole sections for them — the dry-run under-describes what Restore will do.
findings.proposal: In `build_restore_plan`, add `schema_too_new: Option<String>` (or reuse a `blocker` enum alongside `cloud_mismatch`) computed from `check_manifest_schema`, and counts `enterprise_apps_to_reapply` (paired, non-foreign SPs in `app_id_remap` scope), `enterprise_apps_manual`, `managed_identities_to_rebind`. Have `cloud_blocked()` in dr.rs become `plan_blocked()` covering both blockers, and render the new lines in `RestorePlanView`. Extend the existing pure `build_restore_plan` unit tests.

findings.title: Sites and Vault-access panels are ~400-line near-duplicates of one sweep-table pattern
findings.rationale: keyvault.rs opens with "Mirrors the Sites panel" and the body is a copy with the DTO types, consent feature ("sharepoint"→"arm"), noun and three `<td>`s swapped. Both already had to receive the same fixes in lockstep (the haystack corpus, the render-window reset, the still-active hydrate guard, the export-summary rider). The next fix — e.g. the dead-session sink above, or a "scan was partial: re-scan?" callout — has to land twice, and the mailbox panel is a third partial copy.
findings.proposal: Extract `hooks::use_sweep_table<Row, Res, Prog>(SweepSpec { fetch_cached, run, cancel, consent_feature, progress_stream, haystack: fn(&Row)->String, key: fn(&Row)->K, summary: fn(&Res, &[Row])->String, save })` returning `(result, filtered_rows, render_limit, summary, progress, scanning, error, consent_required, do_run, grant_consent, do_export, exporting)`; each panel keeps only its `row_haystack`, `row_key`, the three column renderers and its intro copy. Pin with a source-scan test that the two files no longer both define `filtered_rows`.

findings.title: Both comboboxes place non-option children (group labels, "Searching…", capped footers, cap Callout) directly inside `role="listbox"`

"Go to"
global_search.rs:730

findings.rationale: ARIA requires listbox children to be `option` (or `group` containing options). The footers were deliberately marked `role="presentation"` (good), but the group headings and the loading/empty/error text have no role, so screen readers either announce them as options or skip them. A `role="group" aria-labelledby` per group would also let AT announce "Go to, 3 items" as the roving index crosses groups.

Same for the tester picker.

result.coverage_notes: Read fully: home_dashboard.rs, dr.rs, settings_view.rs, key_vault_view.rs, permission_tester_view.rs, readiness_view.rs, resource_access/{mod,sites,mailboxes,keyvault}.rs, components/global_search.rs (all 1159 lines), dialogs/cache_diagnostics_dialog.rs, and bindings/{mod,common,search,backup,keyvault,keyvault_rbac,permission_tester,readiness,diagnostics,config,defaults,updater,usage,auth,consent}.rs; plus the four architecture docs named in the brief. Read by targeted section only (not end to end): src-tauri commands/restore.rs (lines 87-330 + greps), commands/search.rs (236-430), commands/diagnostics.rs (32-200), commands/defaults.rs (1-60), core/settings.rs (169-220, 339-362), state/{errors,tenant,navigation}.rs, components/{modal_shell,requires_role,ui/callout}.rs, hooks/use_list_export.rs, config_screen.rs (59-122), shell.rs (54-100), tests/gui/{view_smoke,key_vault,dr,global_search,settings,readiness}.rs headers, and tauri-sys core.rs from the cargo git checkout. Bindings owned by other finders (applications, audit, bulk, enterprise_application, events, exchange, expose_api, graph_roles, managed_identity, permissions, remediation, sharepoint, sso, activity, conditional_access, credentials) were only grepped for the dead-code sweep. No cargo build/test/clippy was run per the brief; line numbers come from cat -n/grep -n on the working tree.

result.area_summary: The fe-tests slice is in good shape structurally: the harness (test_support + ipc_mock) is well-reasoned (orphan-mount sweep, loud-reject unmocked policy, typed fixtures serialized through the real serde-wasm-bindgen path), the 4 shards hold 130 browser tests across 32 modules (42/27/32/29) with every module I read asserting on behaviour rather than markup alone, and demo_fixture_coverage genuinely pins the one panic-class invariant. The weaknesses are coverage shape and demo honesty: 125 of the 186 command literals in src/bindings are never referenced by any GUI test, and the untested set is exactly the mutation-heavy surfaces (SSO wizard, federated credentials, Expose-an-API full-collection PATCHes, create/delete app, enterprise access/app-roles, bulk Delete, UpdateSplash); the demo's audit/credential/SSO rows carry ids that do not match its own catalog so "Open" lands on a "Demo App" placeholder, its fixed credential dates have aged past today so list badges contradict the Credentials tab, and ~13 read commands are unregistered so whole tabs show the "not available in the live demo" rejection. Harness-level debt is small but real: `click_button` is copy-pasted in 11 modules, view_smoke sits in the wrong shard and double-links the DR view, and the build_support.rs comment claiming "nothing checks" parser agreement is stale while the invariant test that does check it re-implements the parser instead of mounting it.

findings.title: Mutation-heavy surfaces have zero GUI coverage: SSO wizard, federated credentials, Expose-an-API, create app, enterprise Access/App roles
findings.rationale: The suite is the frontend's only behavioural gate (AGENTS.md), yet the surfaces it skips are the ones that mint trust or do irreversible full-collection writes: `add/update/remove_federated_credential` (auth trusts), `set_identifier_uris`/`upsert_api_scope`/`set_pre_authorized_app` (Graph full-replaces the `api` arrays — the exact footgun AGENTS.md documents), `create_saml/oidc_sso_application` + `ClaimsEditor` (945 lines, untested), `create_application`, `assign/remove_enterprise_app_access`, `upsert/delete_enterprise_app_role`. Coverage map (direct mounts): tested = ApplicationList, EnterpriseApplicationList, ManagedIdentitiesView(+DetailWindow), ApplicationDetailPane (Overview only), AuthenticationTab, CredentialsTab (cert reveal + expired sweep only), SsoContent (rollover only), SecurityView, CredentialsDashboard, SsoCertificatesDashboard, ReadinessView, KeyVaultView, SettingsView, AppShell, OpenItemsDock/Workspace, ScopeWizard/PermissionPicker, SharePointSitesSection, OrgwideScopeCallout, GalleryDialog, ConfirmDialog, GlobalSearch, ToastHost, CopyableId, DisasterRecoveryView; smoke-only = BulkActionsView, ResourceAccessView, PermissionTesterView; untested = everything listed in evidence plus SecretRevealDialog's add_password path, PermissionsTab's remove_declared_permission/revoke_*/downgrade_application_permission.
findings.proposal: Add one GUI module per risk tier, in this order: (1) `federated_tab.rs` — mount FederatedTab with `list_federated_credentials` mocked; drive the GitHub scenario, assert `add_federated_credential` args carry the auto-built issuer/subject and that Remove goes through ConfirmDialog. (2) `expose_api_tab.rs` — assert upsert/delete scope and pre-authorized-app calls send the *whole* current state (the full-collection contract) and that a failed save leaves the form editable. (3) `sso_wizard.rs` — protocol → config → review → create for SAML and OIDC, asserting create_*_sso_application args and that the show-once summary renders. (4) `create_app.rs`, `enterprise_access.rs`, `enterprise_app_roles.rs`. Group (1)(2)(4-create) into shard 1 (they share ApplicationDetailPane's tab code), (3)/(4-enterprise) into shard 1 as well and re-measure with `just web-itest-size`; split a shard 5 if it crosses 52 MB. Expected effect: the highest-blast-radius mutations get a rename/regression gate.

findings.title: Two AGENTS.md invariants have no frontend test: bulk Delete's typed-DELETE gate and the interactive-only updater
findings.rationale: `confirm_dialog.rs` proves `require_keyword` on the shared dialog, but BulkActionBar implements its own `Confirm::Keyword` panel and is the ONLY bulk caller; nothing proves that `bulk_delete_applications` cannot fire until "DELETE" is typed, nor that the armed panel reports partial failures. Likewise AGENTS.md says auto-update is interactive ("never reintroduce a silent download_and_install"); the shell test deliberately leaves `check_for_update` unmocked, so the launch-check → toast → splash → explicit click → `perform_update` chain has no test and a regression that calls `perform_update` on launch would pass CI.
findings.proposal: (a) In security_findings.rs (SecurityView already mounts BulkActionBar) or a new bulk_delete.rs: select rows, arm Delete, assert `call_count("bulk_delete_applications") == 0` after typing "delete" (wrong case) and after a plain click, then == 1 after "DELETE", and assert a `BulkDeleteResult` with one failure renders the failed id. (b) In shell.rs: `mock_ok("check_for_update", &Some(UpdateInfo{..}))` and `mock_ok("perform_update", &())`; mount AppShell; wait for the update toast; assert `call_count("perform_update") == 0`; click the toast action, then "Update & restart"; assert == 1. Both reuse existing fixtures/DTOs; no new views linked, so shard size is unaffected.

findings.title: Demo audit, credential-expiry and SSO rows use ids that don't match the demo catalog, so every "Open" lands on a "Demo App" placeholder
findings.evidence:
fixtures.rs:470-472  app_id: format!("{name}-appid"),
        object_id: format!("obj-{name}"),
fixtures.rs:689  app_object_id: format!("obj-{app}"),
demo/mod.rs:34-38  fn obj_id(name: &str) -> String { f::guid(&format!("{name}:obj")) }
demo/mod.rs:280-284  detail_by_id
            .get(oid)
            .cloned()
            .unwrap_or_else(|| f::application_detail(oid, oid, "Demo App"))
demo/mod.rs:416  .unwrap_or_else(|| f::enterprise_application_detail(id, "Demo Enterprise App"))
fixtures.rs:329  service_principal_id: "sp-payroll".to_string(),
audit_view/row.rs:142  let object_id = item.object_id.clone();
findings.rationale: The demo registers `get_application_detail` args-aware precisely so the detail pane follows the selection (release-updater-demo.md calls a one-payload-for-all-ids mock "the wrong-detail bug to avoid"). But `audit_run_result()` rows are keyed `obj-Contoso CRM`, `credential_expirations()` rows `obj-Contoso CRM`, and `sso_certificate_rows()` `sp-payroll`, while the catalog ids are `guid("Contoso CRM:obj")`. So on the published demo, "Open" from any Security finding, any credential-expiry row, or any SSO-certificate row opens a pane titled "Demo App"/"Demo Enterprise App" whose tabs show none of the finding's permissions or credentials — the headline finding→fix→open journey is broken for visitors, and the `remediations` attached to those rows target ids that exist nowhere.
findings.proposal: Thread the id through the fixture builders: `audit_item(name, risk, issues)` → add an `object_id`/`app_id` source (e.g. `audit_item_with_ids(...)`, or take a `&dyn Fn(&str)->String`), `credential_row(app, ...)` likewise, and `sso_certificate_rows()` take the SP ids. In `demo::register_fixtures`, build the audit/credential/SSO rows from `catalog()`/`ent_specs` via `obj_id(name)`/`app_id(name)` so every row id resolves in `detail_by_id`/`ent_detail_by_id`. Add a native `#[test]` in demo (cfg(test) helper that calls `register_fixtures` is not possible without the bridge, so instead expose a pure `demo::consistency_check()` that asserts every audit/credential/SSO row id ∈ catalog ids) and run it under `just web-test`. Effect: Open, Fix and per-row detail all cohere in the demo.

findings.title: Demo credential and certificate dates are fixed and have aged past today, so list badges contradict the tabs they open
findings.evidence:
demo/mod.rs:116-117  f::password_credential("crm-prod-secret", "Hq9", f::date(2025, 8, 30)),
                f::password_credential("crm-legacy-secret", "a1Z", f::date(2024, 2, 1)),
demo/mod.rs:126  cred_status: S::Expiring,
demo/mod.rs:164-172  f::date(2025, 9, 28), ... cred_status: S::Active,
credentials_tab.rs:35-42  let now = chrono::Utc::now(); ... Some(d) if d < 0 => ("Expired", "badge--danger"),
fixtures.rs:332-333  end_date_time: Some("2026-08-27T00:00:00Z".to_string()),
            days_to_expiry: Some(15),
fixtures.rs:562-565  // Relative to "now" rather than a fixed date, so the demo renders a
        // plausible "Scanned 12 min ago" forever ... completed_at: Some((Utc::now() - chrono::Duration::minutes(12)).to_rfc3339()),
findings.rationale: The App Registrations list badge comes from the DTO's `credential_status` (Expiring/Active), but the Credentials tab computes status from `end_date_time` against `Utc::now()`. As of 2026-09-26 every showcase secret (2025-08-30, 2025-07-09, 2025-09-28, 2024-02-01) and all seven filler secrets (2026-01-31) are expired, so the list says "Expiring"/"Active" and the tab says "Expired" for the same app. The SSO board shows an expiry of 2026-08-27 next to "15 days". The author already solved this for `completed_at` (relative to now) but not for the dates that drive the credential story the demo exists to show.
findings.proposal: Replace `f::date(y,m,d)` in `catalog()` with `f::days_from_now(n)` (e.g. -30, +9, +180, +400) and derive `cred_status` from the soonest expiry (or drop the field from `DemoApp` and compute it in `list_row` with the same thresholds the backend uses); in `sso_certificate_rows()` and `signing_cert_rollover()` compute `end_date_time` from `days_to_expiry` rather than hard-coding both. Add a native test in fixtures (`cfg(test)`, runs under `just web-test`) asserting that for every demo app `row.credential_status` agrees with the detail's soonest `end_date_time` bucket. Effect: the demo stays coherent indefinitely.

findings.title: ~13 read commands are unregistered in the demo, so whole detail tabs render the 'not available in the live demo' rejection — and nothing inventories which reads are missing
findings.rationale: The demo already had to hand-patch Authentication, SSO, get_sso_summary, rollover, the grant lenses etc. after visitors hit rejections (the comments say so). The remaining gaps are systematic: in the demo the Federated credentials, Expose an API, Conditional Access, Activity and Usage tabs of an app registration, the Exchange role assignments panel, the Resource Access Sites/Key Vault panes (cached sweeps), and the MI Permissions tab's mail-scope lookup all render the DemoFriendly error. `demo_fixture_coverage` cannot see this because it only scans the infallible form, so each new read is discovered by a visitor.
findings.proposal: (1) Register fixtures for the listed reads (small typed builders in fixtures.rs: `federated_credentials()`, `expose_api()`, `conditional_access_policies()`, `sign_in_activity()`, `graph_usage()`, `exchange_role_assignments()`, `site_sweep_result()`, `key_vault_access()`; `get_cached_*` may return `None` legitimately — register `&Option::None` so the panes show their honest 'no scan yet' state instead of an error). (2) Extend demo_fixture_coverage.rs with a second test over `invoke_result` literals matching `^(list_|get_|search_|check_|find_|probe_|current_)`: every one must be registered in demo/mod.rs OR appear in a `DEMO_READS_LEFT_UNFIXTURED: &[(&str, &str)]` allowlist with a reason, mirroring the existing `NOT_DEMO_REACHABLE` honesty test. Effect: new read surfaces must be classified before they ship to Pages.

findings.title: The two-parser differential test re-implements section_for instead of mounting it, and build_support.rs still says nothing checks agreement
findings.rationale: AGENTS.md's claim "two parsers, pinned by test" is true in spirit, but the pin compares a hand-copied `rust_semantics` against a PowerShell port — so an edit to the real `section_for` (e.g. tolerating `##  [`) would not change the differential at all, and the test would keep passing while the baked notes and the updater notes diverge. Meanwhile build_support.rs's own header tells the next reader the check does not exist, which invites a second one.
findings.proposal: In repo_invariants/release.rs replace the `rust_semantics` copy with the real source: `#[path = "../../../web-rs/build_support.rs"] mod build_support;` (the same trick web-rs/src/lib.rs uses; the file's own `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` will also run there, or gate it with a `build_support_tests` feature if the doubled `include_str!("../../../CHANGELOG.md")` path resolution is a problem) and call `build_support::section_for`. Update the build_support.rs header to name `both_changelog_extractors_produce_the_same_notes` as the agreement check. Effort S; effect: the differential actually exercises the code that bakes the notes.

findings.title: view_smoke sits in the security shard, links four unrelated heavy subtrees, and double-links DisasterRecoveryView with shard 4
findings.rationale: frontend-workspace.md's grouping rule is "by the view subtree they mount"; view_smoke pulls BulkActionsView (+BulkActionBar), ResourceAccessView (Sites/Mailboxes/KeyVault panels), PermissionTesterView and DisasterRecoveryView into the audit shard, none of which the audit modules mount, and DR is linked a second time in shard 4 where dr.rs now has real tests (the smoke's own header says it exists 'until those land'). The shard's doc comment also names 'the whole-shell smoke test' although shell.rs lives in gui_4. Shard 2 has the fewest tests (27) but likely not the smallest wasm because of this.
findings.proposal: Delete `disaster_recovery_view_mounts` (superseded by dr.rs). Move the remaining three smoke tests to gui_4 (the 'small, self-contained surfaces' shard) or, if `just web-itest-size` shows gui_4 near 52 MB, into a new gui_5.rs; fix gui_2.rs's header to describe what it actually holds. Re-run `just web-itest-size` and record the per-shard numbers in the shard headers so the grouping rule is checkable.

findings.title: click_button / next_enabled / select_permission / has_button / focused_matches are copy-pasted across 11 test modules
findings.rationale: test_support already owns the DOM-interaction vocabulary (`click`, `focus`, `press_key`, `set_textarea_value`), but label-based clicking — the most common gesture in the flow tests — lives in 11 private copies with three slightly different panic messages (certificate_reveal.rs and credential_sweep.rs list the buttons seen; the others don't). The wizard-specific trio (`next_enabled`, `select_permission`, `click_modal_button`) is triplicated verbatim. Each copy is ~10 lines of `unchecked_into` boilerplate that a rename of `.permission-picker__row-head strong` would force to be fixed in three places.
findings.proposal: Add to `test_support`: `click_button_labelled(label)` (panics listing the labels seen), `click_button_labelled_in(scope_selector, label)` (covers click_modal_button/click_panel_button/button_in), `has_button_labelled(label)`, `button_labelled_enabled(label)`, and `focused_matches(selector)`. Add a `tests/gui/wizard_support.rs` (`#[path]`-included by the three wizard modules, or a `pub mod` under test_support behind the feature) holding `select_permission`/`next_enabled`. Replace the copies. Effect: one place to update when the picker markup changes; consistent failure messages.

findings.title: global_search_capped fixture is dead code and the capped-dropdown honesty states it exists for are untested
findings.rationale: The fixture's own doc comment states the rationale for testing the 'N of M' footer and index-cap notice, but nothing consumes it, so `GlobalSearch`'s truncation rendering — an operator-misleading state per AGENTS.md's 'a truncated run is never shown as all-clear' rule — has no gate. Dead fixtures also inflate the demo/test bundle for nothing.
findings.proposal: Add a test to tests/gui/global_search.rs: mock `global_search` with `fixtures::global_search_capped(&["A","B"], 250)`, focus + type, and assert the footer says '2 of 250' (or whatever the real copy is) and that the `IndexCapNotice` renders; assert neither renders with `global_search_apps`. If the product decision is that the notice is not wanted, delete the fixture instead.

findings.title: The one hand-written JSON demo fixture contradicts the 'typed fixtures cannot drift' guarantee
findings.rationale: Every other fixture is a typed struct serialized through the same serde path the bindings deserialize with, which is what makes fixture drift a compile error. `DirectoryIndexStatus` is defined frontend-side with `Deserialize` only, so the demo fell back to `json!` — the one place a renamed field (`sp_index_cap` → something) would silently turn into a deserialize error at demo runtime rather than a build failure. The DTO comment at dto/src/search.rs:55 even notes the frontend 'keeping its own copy in sync'.
findings.proposal: Either add `serde::Serialize` to `DirectoryIndexStatus` and register `&DirectoryIndexStatus { sp_index_truncated: false, sp_index_cap: 10_000 }` via a `fixtures::directory_index_status()` builder, or move the struct into `azapptoolkit-dto` (it mirrors a backend type already) so both sides share it. Effect: zero hand-written JSON in the mock path, matching the module's stated contract.

findings.title: Static per-SP demo fixtures contradict the documented args-aware rule: every enterprise app shows the same SAML config, assignments and roles
findings.evidence:
demo/mod.rs:450  mock_ok("get_sso_config", &f::sso_config("sp-demo", "app-demo"));
demo/mod.rs:421-427  mock_ok(
        "list_enterprise_app_assignments",
        &vec![ f::app_assignment("Sales Team", "Group"), ...
demo/mod.rs:337  "get_application_authentication",
docs/architecture/release-updater-demo.md:105-108  A plain `mock_ok` returns one payload for every id — the wrong-detail bug to avoid.
findings.rationale: The demo doc names one-payload-for-all-ids as the bug to avoid, and the detail/mail-scope/held-grant/Azure-role commands honour it, but `get_sso_config`/`get_sso_summary`/`get_signing_cert_rollover` return an SP `object_id: "sp-demo"` for Datadog, Slack and GitHub alike (with identical thumbprints), every SP has the same three assignments and roles, and every app registration has Contoso CRM's redirect URIs. `variant_index` already exists for exactly this; the same three-variant pattern would make the enterprise side coherent.
findings.proposal: Register `get_sso_config`, `get_sso_summary`, `get_signing_cert_rollover`, `list_enterprise_app_assignments`, `list_enterprise_app_roles`, `list_sp_group_memberships`, `get_enterprise_app_provisioning` and `get_application_authentication` with `mock_each`, keyed on the id arg and using `variant_index`; give non-SAML SPs an `sso_mode: None` variant so the SSO tab's 'not configured' state is also demonstrated, and pass the real SP `id`/`app_id` into `sso_config`. Effort S–M; effect: the demo shows per-object variety and one more degraded state.

findings.title: Stale size/count numbers in the sharding comments (Cargo.toml, justfile, gui_2.rs) disagree with each other
findings.evidence:
Cargo.toml:113-115  # The browser GUI tests (`just web-itest`) are the slowest CI step. Each of the
# ~21 integration-test binaries is a full debug wasm
Cargo.toml:132-133  # 19 MB and all 24 modules merged are 29 MB.
justfile:133-134  # A single merged test binary (~78 MB) exceeds what headless Chrome will
# instantiate, so `tests/gui_N.rs` shards exist to stay under ~52 MB each.
(actual: 4 shard binaries + demo_fixture_coverage; 36 modules under tests/gui/)
findings.rationale: The comments are the only record of why the 52 MB ceiling and the shard layout exist. Today they contradict one another — Cargo.toml says the merged suite is 29 MB at opt-level 1 (under the ceiling), the justfile says ~78 MB — and the counts (21 binaries, 24 modules) predate the current 4-shard layout. A future contributor cannot tell whether sharding is still load-bearing without re-measuring. This is not a case for un-sharding (no new evidence); it is a case for making the numbers current and checkable.
findings.proposal: Have `web-itest-size` also print the sum of shard sizes as 'merged estimate', paste the current per-shard and merged figures into the `[profile.test]` comment with a date, replace '~21 integration-test binaries'/'24 modules' with the shard count, and fix gui_2.rs's header ('whole-shell smoke test' → shell.rs is in gui_4). Effort S.

findings.title: demo_fixture_coverage scan has two blind spots: non-recursive bindings walk and comment-insensitive registration match
findings.rationale: Both are fine today (bindings is flat; no infallible invoke outside it) but each is one refactor away from silently disabling the guard: a `bindings/sso/` subdirectory would drop its files from the scan, and a comment in demo/mod.rs like `// see "cancel_audit"` would count as a registration. AGENTS.md leans on this test as the enforcement of a page-crash invariant.
findings.proposal: Walk `src/` recursively (skip `ipc_mock/` and `demo/`) so an infallible `invoke` anywhere is caught; strip `//` line comments from demo/mod.rs before the `contains` check and require the literal to be preceded by `mock_ok(`/`mock_each(`/`mock_err(` or to sit inside the `for cmd in [` array. Add a negative unit test for each (a comment-only mention must not satisfy the scan). Effort S.

findings.title: Two near-duplicate 'current version has a CHANGELOG section' tests; the docs name only one
findings.rationale: Both fail on the same condition (manifest version has no non-empty section). The release_notes one is strictly stronger — it checks the *baked* output, so it also catches a broken build.rs path or OUT_DIR write — and it is the one the architecture doc names. The build_support copy re-parses CHANGELOG.md with `include_str!` for the same assertion.
findings.proposal: Remove `the_repos_own_changelog_has_a_section_for_the_current_version` (keep the parser edge-case tests around it), or reduce it to a one-line pointer comment to the release_notes test. Effort S.
