result.coverage_notes: Read fully: every file under apps/desktop/web-rs/tests/ (gui_1..4.rs, all 33 gui/*.rs modules, demo_fixture_coverage.rs), src/ipc_mock/mod.rs and fixtures.rs (all 1634 lines), src/demo/mod.rs, src/test_support/mod.rs, build.rs, build_support.rs, Trunk.toml, index.html, Cargo.toml (whole file), the GUI-sharding section of docs/architecture/frontend-workspace.md and all of release-updater-demo.md, the two-parser test in src-tauri/tests/repo_invariants/release.rs (lines 245-370), the release.yml notes-extraction step, the web-itest/web-itest-size/web-test justfile recipes, ci.yml's web job, and .claude/hooks/web-test-strings-check.sh. Only grepped/skimmed (headers + specific lines) in src/views and src/components to build the coverage map and to verify how views render fixture fields (credentials_tab.rs, sso_certificates_dashboard.rs, application_list.rs, audit_view/row.rs, credentials_dashboard.rs, copy_icon_button.rs, toast.rs, use_progress_stream.rs, bindings/applications.rs, bindings/sharepoint.rs, lib.rs). Did not run cargo/wasm-pack (per ground rules), so shard wasm sizes and the 60 s budget were not measured — the shard-balance observations are test counts and linked-subtree reasoning only. Fixture-vs-DTO drift was checked by construction (typed builders compile against the DTO crates; the single hand-written JSON case is reported) rather than field-by-field against every DTO.

verdicts.notes: Evidence is real: application_list.rs:244-251 bumps `reload` synchronously and only then spawns `invalidate_list_cache`; enterprise_application_list.rs:114-122 is identical. The backend cache-hit path (commands/applications/mod.rs:136-148) is fully synchronous after `prove_tenant_session`, so the list IPC — dispatched first — is served from the cache the second IPC is about to drop. The in-repo comment's rationale ('after the backend has had a chance to drop its cache') is wrong because the invalidate call has not even been dispatched when the bump happens. The repo already knows the right shape: application_detail_pane.rs:70-73 and BOTH managed-identity refreshes (managed_identities/mod.rs:105-117, detail_window.rs:190-207) await the invalidate before bumping. One correction: a GUI test `refresh_invokes_invalidate_list_cache` already exists (tests/gui/application_list.rs:196, enterprise_application_list.rs:116) but only asserts the invalidate call happened — extend it to assert ordering (list call count rises only after the invalidate call) rather than adding a new test.
verdicts.corrected_proposal: Move `reload.update(...)` inside the spawned task after `invalidate_list_cache(...).await` in application_list.rs and enterprise_application_list.rs (mirroring managed_identities/mod.rs:105-117), fix the misleading comment, and extend the existing `refresh_invokes_invalidate_list_cache` GUI tests to assert the second `list_*` call is recorded only after `invalidate_list_cache`.

verdicts.notes: Premise verified. permissions_tab.rs:110-117 sets `consent_result` then calls `on_changed`; downgrade path at 341-343 sets `scope_note`, clears `pending_downgrade`, then `on_changed`. `on_changed` = `bump_reload` (application_detail_pane.rs:55), which re-runs the `LocalResource`; the `Suspend` closure at 136-148 rebuilds every tab, so the local `consent_result`/`scope_note` Callouts (759-779) are discarded — the same teardown the credentials tab documents at 470-473 and tests at tests/gui/certificate_reveal.rs:279. The backend (commands/permissions.rs:349-364) returns `Ok(GrantResult)` with `failures` collected rather than `Err`, so a partial consent yields the unqualified 'Admin consent granted' toast; `failures`/`role_assignments_skipped` are shown only in the doomed Callout. The comment at 205-206 ('keeps the chooser open') is contradicted by 342. Severity adjusted to medium: the information loss is real and misleading, but the effect is under-privilege reported as success (app fails at runtime), not a silent over-grant.

Evidence real at permissions_tab.rs:808-814; the same bare-value gate exists in enterprise_application_detail_pane/permissions.rs:253-258 (not mentioned by the reviewer). Contrast row_scope_kind (70-81) and the `has_mail` gate (781-786), both resource-aware. Core already defines the resource-aware forms: `is_scopable_sharepoint_resource_permission` (scoping.rs:406-411, Graph-only org-wide) and `is_scoped_sharepoint_resource_permission` (scoping.rs:431-436, Graph-only Sites.Selected) with a long doc block explaining why only Graph qualifies — so the finding matches the repo's documented position, and no new helper is needed: `scope_kind_for(Some(&p.resource_app_id), v) == Some(ScopeKind::SharePoint)` (scoping.rs:505-517) is exactly the desired gate. The repo invariant (repo_invariants/commands.rs:130) pins only the mailbox forms, confirmed. Severity lowered: the mis-gate only fires for an app whose Sites.* is solely on the legacy SPO resource or a third-party API, and the consequence is a section that reads 'no grants' — misleading, not a wrong write.
verdicts.corrected_proposal: In both permissions_tab.rs:808-814 and enterprise_application_detail_pane/permissions.rs:253-258, gate with `scope_kind_for(Some(&p.resource_app_id), v) == Some(ScopeKind::SharePoint)` (or the two existing Graph-only gates) instead of `v == "Sites.Selected" || is_sharepoint_orgwide(v)`; add a unit test next to the existing SharePoint gate tests; optionally extend the invariant's GONE list to bare `is_sharepoint_orgwide(` outside core/scope_badge/permission_picker.

verdicts.notes: Verified: navigation.rs:108-111 sets `pending_app_tab` unconditionally before `open_item`; open_items.rs:70-74 returns early on an already-open item (no pane mounts); the pane consumes the flag only in its constructor (application_detail_pane.rs:81-86). grep shows nothing else clears it besides `TenantScopedUi::reset` (state/mod.rs:264) and the pane, so the flag survives until the next new app pane mounts and lands it on the deep-linked tab. The MI variant's comment (navigation.rs:126-129) acknowledges already-open windows keep their tab but nothing handles the leak. Existing tests (state/mod.rs:456-488, tests/gui/security_findings.rs:568+) only cover reset and the set path. Severity lowered to low: a one-off wrong initial tab on the next open, no data impact.

Premise holds: application_detail_pane.rs:129-135 uses `Suspense` (no `Transition` anywhere in web-rs) and the `Suspend` closure at 136-148 rebuilds DetailHeader, TabBar and all keep_alive'd tabs on every `bump_reload`; the keep_alive comment (94-99) protects only tab switches; the credentials tab's three deferrals (390-397, 578-584, 600-608) and the consent/downgrade note loss are direct consequences, and no architecture doc frames the remount as deliberate. Overstated: the claim that after the refactor 'per-tab sub-resources only re-run when their inputs change' is not automatic — every tab reads `detail.with(|d| d.application.id...)` inside its `LocalResource`, so a new `Arc<ApplicationDetail>` still notifies them unless the inputs are `Memo`ized (or `Signal::derive` is replaced by field-level memos). The `on_title` callback, the error state (`DetailLoadError`) and the existing GUI test `the_reveal_defers_the_detail_reload_until_it_is_dismissed` (tests/gui/certificate_reveal.rs:279) also need reworking. Effort L is right.
verdicts.corrected_title: Every mutation rebuilds the whole detail pane and remounts all visited tabs (root cause of the deferred-reload workarounds); fixing it also needs memoized tab inputs
verdicts.corrected_proposal: Hold a long-lived `RwSignal<Option<Arc<ApplicationDetail>>>` on the pane, fed by the resource; mount header + TabBar + keep_alive tabs once outside the Suspend, showing `DetailSkeleton` only while `None` and `DetailLoadError` on a failed refetch with no prior value. Pass tabs `Memo`s of the fields they key on (object id, app id) so their sub-resources do not re-run on every detail refresh. Then retire the credentials-tab deferrals and update `the_reveal_defers_the_detail_reload_until_it_is_dismissed`. Interim: switch to `Transition` to stop the skeleton flash.

verdicts.notes: Verified. owners_tab.rs:50-67 and add_owner.rs:45-62 each carry their own 300 ms debounce + 2-char gate + `search_users` resource; owners_tab.rs:449-536 renders `'No matches.'` whenever `filtered.is_empty()` with no raw-query gate, so an untouched box shows 'No matches.' — exactly the bug directory_search.rs:190-197 was written to end. Nuance: add_owner.rs:214-221 does gate on the (debounced) query, so only the Owners tab reproduces the bug; add_owner is 'just' a duplicate. The default-owners loop is duplicated (owners_tab.rs:127-150 vs add_owner.rs:120-159) with different `existing` sources, and grep of src-tauri finds no `add_default_owners` command. Feasibility caveat: `DirectorySearch.action_label` is a plain `String` stored in a `StoredValue` (directory_search.rs:105,136), while the Owners tab flips 'Add'/'Stage' on the `replacing` signal and renders an in-row spinner — migrating needs `action_label` to become `Signal<String>` (or the block keyed on `replacing`) and `row_disabled` for the in-flight id.
verdicts.corrected_proposal: Replace both search blocks with `OwnerPicker`/`DirectorySearch` (`exclude` = current owners or staged set, `row_disabled` for the in-flight id, `clear_on_pick=false` + own `query` for the add path); make `action_label` reactive (`Signal<String>`) so the Owners tab's Add/Stage swap fits. Move the default-owners loop into one backend command (`add_default_owners(tenant_id, object_id) -> {added, failures}`) or one shared frontend helper used by both call sites.

verdicts.notes: Evidence real: credentials_tab.rs:1115-1131 danger button calls `do_rotate(true)` directly; 512-516 collects every `key_id` (active included) when `remove_existing`. Single-secret removal (1132-1146) and the expired sweep (1162-1177) both go through `ConfirmDialog` with a subject; the rotate path has no confirm, no count, and the label 'Rotate & remove existing' carries no N. `ConfirmDialog` already supports `require_keyword` (confirm_dialog.rs:37,59). `r.warnings` is reduced to a count with 'see the log' (539) and grep finds no in-UI log opener, so the warning content is unreachable. Severity medium is fair for a one-click multi-credential deletion in a security-critical tool.

Evidence real: credentials_tab.rs:507-511 (`unwrap_or(180).clamp(1, 730)`) and 570-574 (`unwrap_or(365).clamp(1, 1095)`), versus `resolve_expiry_fields` (125-135) which returns `Err` messages for the new-secret dialog. Stronger than the reviewer states: the backend `cert::generate_self_signed` (src-tauri/src/cert.rs:81-98) deliberately REJECTS validity outside 1..=1095 'so a user-supplied value is never silently' altered — the frontend clamp makes that guard unreachable and does exactly what the backend refuses to do. No frontend test covers either parse (grep finds only the preset tests at 1249). Proposal (shared `parse_days` -> `Result<u32, String>` surfaced via `error`, table tests, optional presets) fits the existing `resolve_expiry_fields` pattern.

Mechanics verified: expose_api_tab.rs:100 snapshots `identifier_uris` into a `StoredValue` at mount; add (123-136) and remove (144-155) send the full list to `set_identifier_uris`, whose backend (commands/expose_api.rs:254-283) PATCHes whatever it receives; the SAML SSO step (sso/mod.rs:197-199) full-replaces `identifierUris` on an existing app too, so a stale snapshot can drop another writer's URI. Overstated: (a) the module doc (lines 6-9) says the backend re-reads before writes to the `api` arrays — `identifierUris` is not an `api` array, and the backend doc (expose_api.rs:252-253) explicitly documents 'The editor loads the current list and sends the complete desired set', so this is a documented design with a stale window, not a contradiction; (b) the snapshot is refreshed after every save (`on_saved` bumps `reload`, lines 61-66), so the window is one tab-open session, and Graph has no delta op for identifierUris — a backend re-read shrinks the race but cannot remove it. Severity lowered to low.
verdicts.corrected_title: Identifier-URI add/remove replays the tab's mount-time snapshot as a full replace; a backend re-read would shrink the lost-update window
verdicts.corrected_proposal: Add `add_identifier_uri` / `remove_identifier_uri` commands that GET the live `identifierUris`, apply the delta, validate and PATCH (mirroring `upsert_api_scope`), or have the frontend call `get_expose_api` right before computing the list; clarify the module doc so it says which mutations re-read live state.

verdicts.notes: All four `Body1.form-error` branches verified: expose_api_tab.rs:81-83, authentication_tab.rs:66-69, federated_tab.rs:557-559, permission_picker.rs:243-248. activity_tab.rs:83-91 and conditional_access_tab.rs:70-78 already use `DetailLoadError` with `on_retry` bumping `reload`, and detail_load_error.rs:6-15 documents it as 'the single home for every load-failure surface' — so this is drift against the one-primitive rule (AGENTS.md / .claude/rules/frontend.md). Each affected tab already owns a `reload` signal (expose_api_tab.rs:48, authentication_tab.rs:40, federated_tab.rs:53), so the fix is mechanical; the picker can re-set `resource_app_id`. No GUI test references the replaced strings.

Authentication tab verified: authentication_tab.rs:184-199 has only a Save button, no Reset/Cancel and no dirty tracking for a full-replace write of three URI lists + flags. Overview verified: the diff is computed inside the async closure (overview_tab.rs:84-104) so a clean form still dispatches `update_application` with an all-`None` patch (backend mod.rs:390-397 forwards it to Graph, which accepts an empty PATCH) — true but harmless beyond a brief spinner and a needless `invalidate_app_lists`. The overview edit DOES have Cancel (overview_tab.rs:109-112), which the finding glosses over. The unsaved-edits-on-close guard is a new feature, not a defect. Severity lowered to low; the substantive part is the Authentication form.
verdicts.corrected_title: Authentication form has no Reset and no dirty tracking; Overview save dispatches an empty PATCH when nothing changed
verdicts.corrected_proposal: Derive `dirty: Signal<bool>` for the Authentication form (compare `to_uris()`/flags against the loaded DTO), disable Save when clean and add a Reset that rebuilds `UriListState` from the DTO or bumps `reload`; in overview_tab compute the patch before `cmd.run` and short-circuit with a toast when empty. Treat the close-time unsaved guard as a separate enhancement.

verdicts.notes: Verified against tests/gui/: application_detail.rs has four smoke tests; authentication_tab.rs (4), certificate_reveal.rs (5), credential_sweep.rs (2) and permission_picker.rs (2) exist, but grep for OwnersTab/ExposeApiTab/PermissionsTab, 'Replace all', 'Add Default Owners', 'Application ID URI', 'Downgrade', 'Grant admin consent', 'Rotate & remove', 'Rotate into Key Vault' finds no test module for the Owners, Expose an API or Permissions tabs, nor for the new-secret/rotate/federated flows. AGENTS.md names the browser tests as the frontend's only behavioural gate, so findings 1, 6, 7 and 8 here would all pass CI. The proposal (three new sharded modules reusing the certificate_reveal mount helpers) matches the frontend-workspace.md sharding conventions.

grep confirms `apps/desktop/` contains only `src-tauri` and `web-rs`, while eight sources still point at `apps/desktop/web/...`/`.tsx` (application_detail_pane.rs:3, application_list.rs:2, owners_tab.rs:2, create_app_dialog.rs:3, tabs/mod.rs:1, views/mod.rs:1, hooks/mod.rs:1, state/tenant.rs:17). app_tab.rs:59 and enterprise_tab.rs:27,64 still describe themselves via Thaw's `Tab`/`TabList`, which tab_bar.rs:19 says was replaced app-wide (filter_chip.rs:7-13 mentions TabList only as historical explanation and is fine). No repo_invariants test scans for these paths. Low, docs-only.

All four verified and slightly understated. `no_tenant()` (util.rs:88-97) is still inlined in FOUR places, not two: application_detail_pane.rs:44-50, permission_picker.rs:130-135, exchange_scoping_section.rs:173 and enterprise_application_detail_pane/mod.rs:113. `util::copy_text` (util.rs:80-86) exists but credentials_tab.rs:972-982 and secret_reveal_dialog.rs:21-29 re-implement the clipboard call. permission_picker.rs:31 redefines `MICROSOFT_GRAPH_APP_ID`, already exported by `azapptoolkit_core::scoping` (scoping.rs:26) which web-rs already depends on (scope_wizard.rs:1091, permissions_tab.rs). create_app_dialog.rs:87-98 hard-codes the four audiences that overview_tab.rs:12-26 keeps in `SIGN_IN_AUDIENCES`. All cleanups are mechanical.

bindings/mod.rs:1 is `#![allow(dead_code)]` with no rationale comment. grep confirms `ResolvePermissionArgs` (applications.rs:75-81), `UpdateRequiredResourceArgs` (permissions.rs:53-59) and keyvault's `SetArgs` (keyvault.rs:58-63; the `SetArgs` hit in defaults.rs:40 is a different local struct) have no callers. `FederatedListArgs` (applications.rs:406-411) is field-for-field `common::ObjectIdArgs` (common.rs:22-27); per-file `TenantArgs` in keyvault.rs:79-83, search.rs:30, sso.rs:188 and defaults.rs:22 duplicate `common::TenantArg` (common.rs:15-19) despite common.rs's stated single-source purpose. Caveat on the proposal: dropping the crate-wide allow may surface warnings on DTO fields that are deserialized but never read; those need targeted `#[allow(dead_code)]` rather than the blanket one.

Premise verified: secret_reveal_dialog.rs:21-29 discards the `write_text` promise result and sets `copied` unconditionally; line 32 `use_escape(|| true, ...)` closes the one-time reveal on a reflex Escape, and `on_close` triggers the deferred `on_changed` (credentials_tab.rs:390-397) so the value is gone; credentials_tab.rs:972-982 `copy_pk` gives no feedback at all. Overstated proposal: `CopyIconButton` (copy_icon_button.rs:28-30) and `util::copy_text` (util.rs:80-86) are equally fire-and-forget and set `copied` optimistically, so 'reuse CopyIconButton so the feedback is the app-wide badge' would reproduce the same false 'Copied'. Fixing it properly means making the shared helper report the promise outcome.
verdicts.corrected_proposal: Make `util::copy_text` return the clipboard promise result (async `Result<(), ()>`) and have `CopyIconButton`, `SecretRevealDialog` and `copy_pk` all consume it, setting `copied` only on `Ok` and showing a small Callout ('Couldn't copy — select the text and copy manually') on `Err`; gate Escape in both one-time reveals (`use_escape(|| false, ...)` or require the explicit Done button).

verdicts.notes: Verified: permissions_tab.rs:573-575 empty-state copy sends operators to the Entra portal while the 'Grant access' wizard button sits at 484-489 in the same header. The Application/Delegated toggles (523-536) are bespoke `permissions-tab__filter-chip` `<button>`s with no `aria-pressed` (grep shows the pattern is used in open_items_dock.rs:96 and application_list.rs:529), and the `<For>` at 592+ renders nothing when both are off — grep finds no 'no rows match' string in the tab. `FilterChip` (filter_chip.rs) is single-select by design so it does not fit directly; a three-value `TabBar` or an inline empty message are both reasonable.

Verified: identical `aria-label="Select permission"` on both checkbox inputs (permission_picker.rs:421 delegated, 474 application), while application_list.rs:700-703 documents the descriptive per-row label pattern for the same reason. `counts` is `RwSignal<HashMap<String,(usize,usize)>>` (line 89) and `counts.get()` at 172-174 runs inside the per-resource `.map`, cloning the whole map once per `<option>`; `counts.with(|c| c.get(&r.app_id).copied())` is the idiomatic fix. No GUI test references the current aria-label.

UI part verified: expose_api_tab.rs:289-293 only checks non-empty; 741-746 is a free-text GUID input; 567 renders the raw `app_id` with no display name. Refuted in part: the backend `set_pre_authorized_app` (commands/expose_api.rs:368-373) already validates the GUID shape (`is_guid`) and returns a `validation` error 'Client ID must be the application (client) ID GUID…' before any Graph call, so a malformed GUID does NOT surface 'only as a Graph 400' — client-side shape validation adds little. What remains is the genuine enhancement: a well-formed but wrong GUID that exists pre-authorizes the wrong app with no consent prompt, and neither the add path nor the table shows a display name. The picker's 'Tenant app registrations' group (permission_picker.rs:190) and the SP index are plausible sources for a typeahead/name resolution.
verdicts.corrected_title: Pre-authorized client is entered as a bare GUID with no directory lookup, and existing rows show no display name
verdicts.corrected_proposal: Add a `DirectorySearch`-style typeahead over the tenant's app registrations/SPs (appId + display name) for the add path and resolve display names for existing rows via the SP index, falling back to the GUID; keep the backend's `is_guid` as the shape check (optionally mirror its message client-side for a pre-submit error).

verdicts.notes: navigation.rs:108-111 and :117-122 set `tenant_ui.pending_app_tab` / `pending_enterprise_tab` unconditionally BEFORE `open_item`; open_items.rs:70-74 dedupes an already-open (kind, entity_id) and only re-titles + `focus_item`s, never remounting. The only consumers are on-mount reads: application_detail_pane.rs:80-86 and enterprise_application_detail_pane/mod.rs:188-193 (`get_untracked()` then `set(None)`). Nothing else clears the signal except `TenantScopedUi::reset` (state/mod.rs:264-265), so a stale `Some("credentials")` survives until the next AppReg pane mounts. Callers hit this in practice: credentials_dashboard.rs:114, audit_view/row.rs:179-182, resource_access/mailboxes.rs:73-76, consent_grants_view.rs:110, sso_certificates_dashboard.rs:271 all target apps that are often already open. The existing GUI test (tests/gui/security_findings.rs:568-586) only asserts the signal is SET after click, never that it is consumed, so the leak is untested. The MI variant (navigation.rs:129-136) is immune as stated. Proposal (guard on `is_open(..).is_none()`) matches the documented intent at navigation.rs:127-128 and is a two-line change plus a host unit test.

use_shortcuts.rs:54-67: `query_selector` (first match in document order) then bails if THAT element has no `offset_parent`, contrary to the comment's intent of 'the first filter input that is actually laid out'. `SearchInput` (components/ui/search_input.rs:20-42) renders a Thaw `<Input>`; the only `search-input*` class in src is `search-input__clear` on the clear button, so `input.search-input__field` and `.search-input input` match nothing — only `input[placeholder^='Filter']` is live (placeholders at application_list.rs:304, enterprise_application_list.rs:156, managed_identities/mod.rs:150, audit_view/mod.rs:224, etc. all start with 'Filter'). lib.rs:260-274 mounts keep-alive panes in fixed declaration order (Home, Apps, EnterpriseApps, ManagedIdentities, Security, ...), and util.rs:45-47 hides inactive panes with `display:none`, which yields `offsetParent == null`. So after visiting App Registrations once, `/` on any later view resolves the hidden Apps input and returns false. tests/gui/shortcuts.rs has only the negative test (line 52-67) and the `?` positive test; no positive `/` test. Proposal (`query_selector_all` + first laid-out) is correct and small.

use_command.rs:97-104: `run`'s on_err calls only `report_consent_required` then sets `error`, while `run_toast_err` (line 127) routes through `report_command_error_for`, which at errors.rs:171 checks `report_if_session_dead` first. errors.rs:52-55 doc explicitly says surfaces with their own error affordance 'call this first so a dead session still gets the recovery action'. `run`'s own doc (use_command.rs:80-84) justifies the consent toast as 'the one failure the inline message can never resolve', but a dead session is equally unresolvable inline and the same file's `run_toast_err` comment (lines 123-126) names it. grep confirms 24 `.run(` call sites vs 16 `run_toast_err`; no global auth-state event exists (bindings/events.rs lists only progress streams), so nothing else surfaces re-auth for these forms except the topbar Refresh-token button (shell.rs:126). Ordering in the proposal (dead-session before consent) matches the pinned test `a_dead_session_still_wins_over_the_consent_branch` (errors.rs:218-229). Host unit test is feasible with the existing `provide_session()` pattern.

verdicts.corrected_title: Sign-in AADSTS hints for 90002/900023 and 700016/700054 point at Settings → Tenant connection, which the sign-in card cannot reach; the card's own 'Change' link is the correct destination
verdicts.notes: sign_in.rs:21-24 (on_reconfigure doc) states Settings → Tenant connection 'is behind the sign-in it can never complete'; sign_in.rs:190-197 nonetheless tells the operator to 'Check the tenant ID under Settings → Tenant connection'. The card renders the correct affordance at sign_in.rs:70-80 (`Signing in to {tenant} · Change` → `on_reconfigure`). The comment at sign_in.rs:184-187 ('which is why the hint names Settings: the ids are editable there') shows it was deliberate but rests on a false premise for this surface. `recovery_hint`/`aadsts_hint` have no callers outside sign_in.rs, so the `where_to_fix` parameter in the proposal is speculative (YAGNI); the reword + test assertion is the right size. Severity downgraded to low: the wrong hint is a string fix and the correct 'Change' link sits directly above the error on the same card.

toasts.rs:18-32 pushes unconditionally and `drain(0..overflow)` drops the oldest regardless of kind/action; no dedupe anywhere in toasts.rs or components/toast.rs. components/toast.rs:128-131 defines stickiness (`Error && has_action`) only for the auto-dismiss timer, so the cap does undo it. errors.rs:56-67 pushes a fresh identical toast on every `report_if_session_dead` call and there are 7 external call sites (dr.rs ×6, bulk_action_bar.rs:564) plus 16 `run_toast_err` sites via `report_command_error_for`. Premise and proposal hold. Severity downgraded to low: the dr.rs sites are in separate handlers and rarely fire together, so a 6-toast burst with a sticky eviction is an edge case; identical-toast duplication is the more common symptom and is cosmetic.

docs/architecture/frontend-workspace.md:4 and :11 name `web-rs/src/state.rs`, but state is a directory (state/mod.rs, tenant.rs, navigation.rs, open_items.rs, toasts.rs, errors.rs). Line 114 says 'drain-oldest on overflow' while open_items.rs:87-95 evicts `min_by_key(focused_at)` and lines 97-120 push an Info toast with a 'Reopen' action (pinned by state/mod.rs:524-569 `open_item_cap_evicts_the_least_recently_focused`). The doc has zero mention of the tenant-keyed `localStorage` snapshot (`azapptoolkit:workspace:{tenant_id}`, open_items.rs:264-272), the single write path `update_open_items` (255-262), `restore_open_items` (221-241), or the `restore_open_items_never_crosses_tenants` test (state/mod.rs:571). CHANGELOG.md:82-87 records the behaviour change but the deep-dive was not updated. state/mod.rs:325-326 lists 4 Security sub-tabs while global_search.rs:545-580 routes to 6 (findings, apps, credentials, sso-certificates, grants, app-permissions). Medium is fair: `Session.open_items` is a `pub RwSignal`, so the doc is the only cross-file guard against a view bypassing `update_open_items` and desyncing the snapshot.

verdicts.corrected_title: Post-mutation refetch loses list scroll position because Suspense remounts `LoadedApps` (and thus `VirtualList`); the `items`-change snap effect is not the cause
verdicts.corrected_proposal: The scroll reset after `apps_reload`/`enterprise_apps_reload` bumps comes from the `<Suspense>` + `Suspend::new(async move { match apps.await { Ok(items) => <LoadedApps items=items .../> } })` structure (application_list.rs:315-345; same shape in enterprise_application_list.rs:171-209 and managed_identities/mod.rs:156-206): a refetch tears the loaded subtree down and mounts a fresh `VirtualList` whose scroller starts at 0 and whose snap effect skips its first run. A `reset_key` prop on `VirtualList` would not change this. To preserve scroll across a refetch, either (a) keep `LoadedApps` mounted by passing the resource as a signal and reading it inside memos (the comment at application_list.rs:318-321 already keeps filter changes from tearing it down), or (b) lift `scroll_top` per list into `TenantScopedUi` (with a `reset()` line + pinning test) and restore it on mount. Keep the existing snap-to-top for search/facet/sort changes.
verdicts.notes: Effect at virtual_list.rs:132-144 is as quoted, but `items` for the App Registrations list is `sorted: Memo<Arc<Vec<_>>>` (application_list.rs:458-472) derived from `use_filtered_list`, which takes a plain `Vec<T>` (use_filtered_list.rs:114-133) captured at `LoadedApps` mount. A refetch re-runs the Suspend closure and constructs a new `LoadedApps`, so `items` never 'changes' on the same VirtualList instance — the component is replaced. The symptom (operator thrown to row 0 after a mutation) is real, but the diagnosed mechanism and the proposed fix are wrong; the GUI test proposed ('bump the items signal with same-length rows') would pass today because the effect is not what fires. Severity lowered to low: a scroll reset after an explicit mutation is a common, if annoying, list behaviour, and the fix is larger than described.

verdicts.corrected_title: ~70 lines of dead CSS (command palette, `.mi-grant`/`.mi-scope-panel`, `.owner-list`, `.dash-links`/`.dash-link`, `.checkbox-list`, `.centered-pad`, `.sso-claims__row`, `.dr-view__secret-value`) match nothing in src; `.dr-view__secrets`/`__secret-name` are live and `.ui-kbd` should be adopted, not deleted
verdicts.corrected_proposal: Delete the rules with zero source references: styles.css:2124-2171 (`.cmd-palette*`), 1461 `.mi-grant`, 1465 `.mi-scope-panel`, 1524/1532 `.owner-list`, 1822-1840 `.dash-links`/`.dash-link`, 2059 `.checkbox-list`, 2361 `.centered-pad`, 3616 `.sso-claims__row` plus its entry in the 560px media block at 3451, and 4206 `.dr-view__secret-value`. Keep `.dr-view__secrets` (dr.rs:529) and `.dr-view__secret-name` (dr.rs:532). Do not delete `.ui-kbd` (3122) — wire it to the shortcut sheet per finding 8. A host-side CSS-coverage test (like tests/demo_fixture_coverage.rs) is feasible but needs an allowlist for Thaw classes and for classes assembled with `format!`.
verdicts.notes: grep -rF over src/ and tests/ confirms 0 hits for cmd-palette*, mi-grant, mi-scope-panel, owner-list, dash-links, dash-link, checkbox-list, centered-pad, ui-kbd, sso-claims__row, dr-view__secret-value. However `.dr-view__secrets` and `.dr-view__secret-name` ARE used at dr.rs:529 and 532, and the rationale 'dr.rs never renders individual secret values' is false — it renders each via `<CopyableId value=s.secret_value ...>` (dr.rs:535). `.sso-claims` (3608) is live (sso_wizard_dialog.rs:300); only `__row` is dead. The finding also conflicts with finding 8 on `.ui-kbd`.

styles.css:4281 `background: var(--surface-alt);` with no fallback; grep across web-rs (css/html/rs) finds no `--surface-alt` definition — `:root` defines `--surface`, `--surface-raised`, `--bg-subtle` (lines 12-14, 115-117). Per CSS spec an undefined custom property without fallback makes the declaration invalid at computed-value time → `background: initial` (transparent). `.ui-kbd` (3122-3135) is the finished chip style using `--bg-subtle` and has zero references in src/tests; shortcuts_help.rs:27 renders a bare `<kbd>`. `--surface-hover` (1595) and `--border-subtle` (325) are also undefined but carry fallbacks, so they are hygiene rather than bugs — correctly framed as 'also'. Proposal (class="ui-kbd" + delete the ad-hoc rule) is the one-primitive-per-pattern answer.

use_shortcuts.rs:34-45 `is_typing` treats every `<input>` as text entry; use_grid_keynav.rs:100-114 `in_text_field` excludes checkbox/radio/button/submit/reset with the stated rationale (lines 96-99, 'a row's bulk-select checkbox is explicitly not a text field'). The module comment forbids the surface hook reaching into use_shortcuts, not a shared leaf in hooks/mod.rs (which today only declares modules and re-exports `use_command`). After focusing a row checkbox, `?` and `/` are dropped at use_shortcuts.rs:151. tests/gui/shortcuts.rs has no checkbox probe. Low severity is honest — keyboard users lose two shortcuts only while a checkbox has focus.

modal_shell.rs:47-54 hardcodes `aria-labelledby="modal-shell-title"` and `<h3 id="modal-shell-title">`; there are 13 `<ModalShell` sites across 9 files, including `ShortcutsHelp` (shortcuts_help.rs:15). use_shortcuts.rs:163-166 toggles `show_help` on bare `?` with no open-dialog gate, and `is_typing` returns false for a focused modal `<button>`, so a second ModalShell stacks over an open one → duplicate ids. Each ModalShell registers its own window-level `use_escape` (modal_shell.rs:37-40; use_escape.rs:18-24 is a plain window keydown listener gated only on `open && !busy`), so one Escape closes both. The other dialogs listed at views/dialogs/*.rs use their own `role="dialog"` wiring and aren't affected by the id clash but are affected by the double-Escape when `?` stacks ShortcutsHelp over them. Per-instance id via a counter is trivial; gating `?` on an existing `[role=dialog]` is the smaller of the two Escape fixes.

date_range_filter.rs:62-66: `<label class="date-range-field__label">{label}</label>` is a sibling of the `<input type="date">`, with no `for`/`id` and no `aria-label`, so both pickers ('Created after'/'Created before') are unnamed. saved_views.rs:113-116: `<input class="saved-views__input" placeholder="View name" ...>` has placeholder only. Contrast `IconButton` requiring `aria_label` (used at date_range_filter.rs:80). Both fixes are one attribute each and carry no CSS-class rename risk for the GUI tests.

export_menu.rs:67-83 renders `role="menu"` / `role="menuitem"` with only `use_escape` (line 52) and an outside-mousedown closer; no `on:keydown`, no focus move on open. shell.rs:391 `.shell__account-menu` has `role="menu"` with `menuitem` children (413-477) and the trigger has `aria-haspopup="menu"`/`aria-expanded` (342-343); grep finds no `on:keydown` in shell.rs. The module doc (export_menu.rs:5-10) explains the plain-DOM disclosure choice (WebView2 freeze with Thaw Menu) — a sound reason for the markup, but it does not justify keeping the menu roles without the keyboard contract. `use_focus_return` exists (hooks/use_focus_return.rs:34) for the restore half. Either option in the proposal is valid; dropping the roles is the cheaper honest fix.

use_debounced.rs:16-22 `clear_pending` only calls `clear_timeout_with_handle`; the `Closure::once_into_js` at line 35 is never dropped by Rust. wasm-bindgen documents `once_into_js` as freeing the closure only when JS invokes it, so a cleared timer leaks the boxed closure plus the captured `next: String`. 10 call sites (global_search.rs:64, enterprise_application_list.rs:45, audit_view/mod.rs:61, permission_picker.rs:71, directory_search.rs:134, etc.), all keystroke-driven with 200-600 ms delays, in keep-alive components that never unmount. Other `once_into_js` users (copy_icon_button.rs:36, toast.rs:135, pairing.rs:46, global_search.rs:222, permission_tester_view.rs:310) let their timers fire, so the finding's scope is right. `StoredValue::new_local` is already used for a `Closure` in virtual_list.rs (~line 122), so the proposed fix has in-repo precedent.

shell.rs:126-142 re-implements the reauthenticate round trip with the same two toast strings as `Session::spawn_reauth` (errors.rs:24-38), and the shell path calls `session.bump_readiness_reload()` on success (shell.rs:133) while `spawn_reauth` does not — so re-authenticating from the `report_if_session_dead` toast leaves a mounted Access Readiness checklist (readiness_view.rs:173 tracks `readiness_reload`) stale. `spawn_reauth`'s own doc (errors.rs:22-23) names the shell's Refresh fallback as a user, so the split was not intended as two policies. The proposal (bump inside `spawn_reauth`, optional on_done for `reauthing`) is a small refactor consistent with AGENTS.md's one-definition-per-policy rule.

verdicts.corrected_title: Stale blanket `#![allow(dead_code)]` in toast.rs and `#![allow(unused_imports, dead_code)]` in ui/mod.rs; icon.rs's blanket allow hides two unused variants (`More`, `ExternalLink`)
verdicts.corrected_proposal: Remove the module-level allows in toast.rs:3 and ui/mod.rs:5 and run `just web-clippy` (which uses `-D warnings --all-targets --features test-support`) to confirm nothing else surfaces. In icon.rs either delete `IconName::More`/`ExternalLink` or mark those two variants individually with `#[allow(dead_code)]` and a comment; drop the file-wide `#![allow(dead_code)]`.
verdicts.notes: Confirmed: `IconName::More` and `IconName::ExternalLink` have zero uses outside icon.rs; toast.rs:1-3's justification is stale (all three `ToastKind`s and all four `ToastKind` methods are used, `ToastKind::Info` at 3 external sites incl. open_items.rs:113); every `pub use` in ui/mod.rs:22-35 has 6-46 external references. Overstated: icon.rs contains only `Icon` (line 50) and `paths` (line 79), both used — there is no 'dead helper fn' the allow hides. Note ui/mod.rs's `dead_code` allow may also be covering unused items inside the submodules (not just the re-exports); the proposal correctly defers that to clippy.

verdicts.corrected_title: Crate-wide `#![allow(private_interfaces)]` in web-rs lib.rs is broader than the test-mounting rationale needs; scoping it (or the module visibility) to the `test-support` feature would keep the lint live for the shipped build
verdicts.corrected_proposal: Cheapest honest fix: move the allow from the crate root onto the `pub mod views;` / `pub mod components;` items, or use `#![cfg_attr(feature = "test-support", allow(private_interfaces))]`. The cfg-gated double module declaration is feasible but adds six paired declarations for a lint-hygiene benefit only. Drop the claim that the Trunk bundle 'exports a public API' — Rust `pub` visibility does not create wasm exports (only `#[wasm_bindgen]` does) and unreferenced code is stripped, so there is no runtime or size cost today.
verdicts.notes: lib.rs:7-13 documents the allow and its rationale; tests/gui_*.rs import `views::` (25), `components::` (11), `hooks::` (2), `state::` (3), `bindings::` (2) — all under `--features test-support` (Cargo.toml:77; justfile web-clippy line ~276). main.rs only calls `run()`. However the cited 'real instance the allow masks' is wrong: `enum Route` (global_search.rs:408) is used only in the private `struct Destination` (line 428, field at 443) and the private `fn go_to` (line 889); no `pub` item exposes it, so `private_interfaces` would not fire there. Because `web-clippy` runs with `test-support` on, a `cfg_attr` allow keyed on that feature would still be active under the CI lint, limiting the benefit to non-test builds. Severity low; it is a hygiene refactor with no user-visible effect.

verdicts.corrected_title: `APPS_HARD_CAP` (web-rs/constants.rs:22) hand-mirrors the backend's `APPS_MAX` with a stale path comment; the SP lists already read their cap from `get_directory_index_status`
verdicts.corrected_proposal: Either extend `DirectoryIndexStatus` — which is NOT in azapptoolkit-dto but hand-mirrored in `src-tauri/src/commands/applications/mod.rs:86-96` and `web-rs/src/bindings/applications.rs:22-27` — with `app_index_cap` (and optionally `app_index_truncated`) and have `LoadedApps` read it the way `IndexCapNotice` does, or move the struct plus the cap constant into azapptoolkit-dto so both trees share one definition. At minimum fix the comment path to `commands/applications/mod.rs`.
verdicts.notes: Premise holds: constants.rs:20-22 and applications/mod.rs:75 both say 10_000 with nothing pinning them (web-rs is outside the workspace; no repo_invariants test references APPS_HARD_CAP), the comment path `commands/applications.rs` is stale (it is now `applications/mod.rs`), and index_cap_notice.rs:80 / bindings/applications.rs:30 show the SP lists reading `sp_index_cap` from the backend. Overstated: the proposal places the DTO in azapptoolkit-dto, but `DirectoryIndexStatus` lives in the command file and the binding file (dto/search.rs:55 only mentions it in a comment). Also note the backend's own doc (applications/mod.rs:80-82) deliberately excludes the app cap from the status because the App Registrations list 'can detect its own truncation' — so the drift risk is the real argument, not a missing signal. Effort remains S.

saved_views.rs:11-16 `SavedView { name, facet, search }`; save at 58-62 and apply at 90-93 touch only those two signals. list_scaffold.rs:44-47 renders `<SavedViews .../>` and then `{drawer.run()}` in the same `<Show when=filters_open>` block, and the views pass `DateRangeFilter` as that drawer (application_list.rs:311, enterprise_application_list.rs:163). application_list.rs:199-202 counts `created_after`/`created_before` in `active_filters`, so the badge does keep counting a range a saved view did not clear — exactly as described. `#[serde(default)]` on two `Option<NaiveDate>` fields is backward-compatible with existing localStorage payloads (unknown → None). Enhancement, low severity is right.

open_items.rs:221-241 `restore_open_items` decodes the snapshot and `set`s it with no length clamp or dedupe; the cap is enforced only in `open_item` (lines 76-95) and removes exactly one item per push, so a 9-item snapshot stays at 9 forever. `restore_open_items_never_crosses_tenants` (state/mod.rs:571-622) restores a single item and never exercises the cap. The module doc's own framing ('the only read is restore_open_items') makes 'restore cannot violate the model' a natural invariant to close. Sort-by-`focused_at`-desc + `truncate(MAX_OPEN_ITEMS)` + dedupe by (kind, entity_id) is a few lines and testable on the host target via the in-memory store (open_items.rs:38-55).

Evidence is real. navigation.rs:108-111 and :117-122 set `pending_app_tab`/`pending_enterprise_tab` unconditionally before `open_item`; open_items.rs:70-74 dedupes an already-open `(kind, entity_id)` by re-titling + `focus_item` and returns without a remount; the workspace mounts panes via keyed `<For>` (open_items_workspace.rs:138), so the pane's one-shot consumption at application_detail_pane.rs:80-86 and enterprise_application_detail_pane/mod.rs:188-193 never runs for an already-open item. The only other reset is the tenant switch (state/mod.rs:264-265). The MI variant (navigation.rs:129-136) is indeed immune because it writes `last_mi_tab`. Callers where re-opening an already-open item is routine exist (audit_view/row.rs:179-182, credentials_dashboard.rs:114, mailboxes.rs:73-76). The existing GUI test (tests/gui/security_findings.rs:566-585) only asserts the signal is set, never consumed. Proposal is minimal and consistent with the MI doc's stated intent.

use_shortcuts.rs:53-70 does `query_selector` (first match in document order) then bails when that single element has no offset parent — the comment's 'first filter input that is actually laid out' is not what the code does. keep_alive (util.rs:45-47) hides inactive panes with `display:none` and mounts them in declaration order (lib.rs:260-274: Home, Apps, EnterpriseApps, ManagedIdentities, Security…). Apps' input has placeholder 'Filter App Registrations by name or appId…' (application_list.rs:304), so after one visit to Apps, `/` on any later view finds the hidden Apps input and returns false. The two dead selector alternates are confirmed: SearchInput wraps Thaw `Input` (search_input.rs:21), which renders `.thaw-input__input` (thaw-0.5.0-beta src/input/mod.rs:182), and the only `search-input*` class in src is `search-input__clear`. The Global Search input's placeholder starts with 'Search' (global_search.rs:212) so it does not collide. tests/gui/shortcuts.rs has no positive `/` test (only the no-fire-while-typing case). Proposal (query_selector_all + first laid-out) is the right fix.

use_command.rs:85-105: `run`'s on_err calls only `report_consent_required` then sets `error`; `run_toast_err` (:121-131) routes through `report_command_error_for`, which at errors.rs:167-175 tries `report_if_session_dead` first. The sink's own doc (errors.rs:54-57) says surfaces with their own inline affordance must call `report_if_session_dead` first. Outside dr.rs (6 sites) and bulk_action_bar.rs, no `cmd.run(` caller (23 sites in src) reports a dead session, so form modals show a raw `refresh_missing`/`not_signed_in` message with no Re-authenticate action. AGENTS.md's 'a dead session forces re-auth in place' rule and the sink doc both support the proposal; the existing host tests (errors.rs:188-224) give the pattern for the requested unit test.

sign_in.rs:190-198 hints point at 'Settings → Tenant connection'; the same file's `on_reconfigure` doc (sign_in.rs:21-24) and lib.rs:205-212 say that surface is unreachable before sign-in, and the card renders the real escape hatch ('Signing in to {tenant} · Change', sign_in.rs:69-82) which reopens the 'Configure your tenant' form (config_screen.rs:42) holding both IDs. `recovery_hint`/`aadsts_hint` have no other callers, so the hints only ever render on the sign-in card. The nearby comment (sign_in.rs:187-189, 'the ids are editable there') is a deliberate choice built on a wrong premise, not a sound rationale. Test at sign_in.rs:270-274 asserts only 'tenant doesn't resolve'. Severity downgraded to low: the correct affordance and raw AADSTS code are on the same card, so this is a misleading sentence in a failure path, not a blocked recovery.

toasts.rs:9-35: no dedupe, and `drain(0..overflow)` evicts by position regardless of `action`, while ToastHost (toast.rs:129-131) makes 'Error + action' sticky — so the cap can indeed evict a sticky Re-authenticate/Grant-consent toast while auto-dismissing successes survive. `report_if_session_dead` (errors.rs:58-70) pushes a fresh toast per call with no guard; grep confirms no dedupe anywhere and no MAX_TOASTS test. The burst scenario is overstated: list/dashboard resources fail into `DetailLoadError` (not toasts), the bulk bar stops on the first re-auth-fatal code, and the six dr.rs sites are separate handlers — so N identical toasts needs N operator actions, which is plausible but not automatic. Downgraded to low; proposal (dedupe on kind+message+label, evict non-sticky first) is sound and small.

frontend-workspace.md:4 and :11 still cite `web-rs/src/state.rs` (now `state/` with mod.rs, tenant.rs, navigation.rs, open_items.rs, toasts.rs, errors.rs); :114 says 'drain-oldest on overflow' while open_items.rs:87-95 evicts min `focused_at` and :97-120 pushes the Info 'Reopen' toast (pinned by `open_item_cap_evicts_the_least_recently_focused`, state/mod.rs:523-568); the doc never mentions the tenant-keyed localStorage snapshot, `update_open_items` as sole writer, or `restore_open_items` (open_items.rs:7-14, 221-272; test at state/mod.rs:571). state/mod.rs:325-326 `security_tab` comment lists 4 sub-tabs vs 6 in security_view.rs:74-79 (the arch doc at :201-202 already lists all 6, so the stale copy is the code comment, plus navigation.rs:28-29). Downgraded to low: the in-file module docs on open_items.rs are complete and correct, so an agent editing that file is not actually misled; the drift is in the deep-dive only.

The snap-to-top effect at virtual_list.rs:132-144 exists as quoted, but it is not the mechanism that loses scroll on a refetch. application_list.rs:315-357 renders the loaded body via `<Suspense>` + `Suspend::new(async move { apps.await … <LoadedApps …/> })`, and the comment at :317-320 says it re-runs on every refetch (tenant switch / reload bump). A bump of `apps_reload` (tracked at :228) therefore shows the skeleton fallback and re-creates `LoadedApps` — a new `use_filtered_list`, a new `VirtualList` with fresh `scroll_top = 0` and a new scroller element — so the effect's `prev.is_some()` guard never even fires for that case. The user-visible symptom (scroll lost after a list-mutating action) is real, but the proposed `reset_key` prop would not fix it: the component is gone. The same shape applies to enterprise_application_list.rs. Note also that `shown` is a `Memo<Arc<Vec<T>>>` (use_filtered_list.rs:73), so a same-content refetch would not retrigger the effect anyway.
verdicts.corrected_title: List refetch after a mutation remounts the whole `LoadedApps` subtree (Suspense), losing scroll position
verdicts.corrected_proposal: Either (a) switch the list body to `<Transition>` and feed `LoadedApps` a signal of rows so the component instance survives a refetch, then clamp `scroll_top` on an `items` change instead of snapping; or (b) lift the scroller offset out of `VirtualList` into an optional `scroll_top: RwSignal<f64>` prop owned by the view (or `tenant_ui`) and restore it on mount. Also amend the virtual_list.rs:132 comment: 'refetch' does not reach that effect today.

verdicts.notes: Most of the list checks out with zero hits in src/ and tests/: `.cmd-palette*` (styles.css:2124-2171), `.mi-grant` (:1461), `.mi-scope-panel` (:1465), `.owner-list` (:1524/1532), `.dash-links`/`.dash-link` (:1822-1840), `.checkbox-list` (:2059), `.centered-pad` (:2361), `.ui-kbd` (:3122), `.sso-claims__row` (:3451, :3616; only `.sso-claims` is rendered at sso_wizard_dialog.rs:300), `.dr-view__secret-value` (:4206). verdicts.corrected_title: ~75 lines of dead CSS (command palette, owner list, MI scope panel, kbd chip, DR secret value, others) match nothing in src

verdicts.notes: styles.css:4281 uses `var(--surface-alt)` with no fallback; grep shows no `--surface-alt:` definition anywhere (only `--bg-subtle`, `--surface`, `--surface-raised` at :12-14 and :115-117), so the declaration is invalid at computed-value time and the `<kbd>` renders with a border and transparent fill. `.ui-kbd` (:3122-3134) is the finished chip with `var(--bg-subtle)` and has zero references in src/ or tests/. shortcuts_help.rs:27 renders a bare `<kbd>`. `--surface-hover` (:1595) and `--border-subtle` (:325) are undefined but carry fallbacks, so they render correctly; closing the token set is a nice-to-have. Proposal is a one-line class change plus a rule deletion.

use_shortcuts.rs:34-45 treats every `<input>` as typing; use_grid_keynav.rs:100-114 exempts checkbox/radio/button/submit/reset and its own doc (:96-99) forbids the surface hook from importing the window-level module — but says nothing against a shared leaf helper, and `hooks/mod.rs` already exists as that home. 19 `type="checkbox"` inputs exist in src (bulk-select rows), so after Space-toggling one, `?` and `/` no-op. No GUI test covers the checkbox case (tests/gui/shortcuts.rs uses a text probe only). Proposal is consistent with the documented boundary.

modal_shell.rs:47-54 hardcodes `id="modal-shell-title"` / `aria-labelledby="modal-shell-title"`; 8 components mount ModalShell (grep `<ModalShell`), including ShortcutsHelp (shortcuts_help.rs:15) which is always mounted in the shell (shell.rs:524). use_shortcuts.rs:163-166 toggles `show_help` on `?` with no dialog gate, and `is_typing` returns false for a focused button, so `?` from inside any open modal stacks a second ModalShell with a duplicate id. use_escape.rs:18-23 registers an independent window listener per dialog with no topmost check, so one Escape runs both `on_close`s. Other dialogs mint their own ids (scope_wizard.rs:758, add_owner.rs:187, …) so the duplicate-id half is ModalShell-only; the double-Escape half applies to any two open dialogs.

date_range_filter.rs:62-68: `<label class="date-range-field__label">` has no `for`, no `id` on the `<input type="date">`, and does not wrap it, so the input has no accessible name; the two fields are distinguished only by that label text. saved_views.rs:112-115: `<input class="saved-views__input" placeholder="View name">` has no label or aria-label. The contrast with IconButton is accurate — its `aria_label` prop is required (icon_button.rs:7-14). Both fixes are one attribute each and no test references the affected markup.

export_menu.rs:67-83 renders `role="menu"` / `role="menuitem"` with no `on:keydown`, no focus move on open, and only Escape via `use_escape` (:53); shell.rs:391-477 has the same shape (`role="menu"`, `aria-haspopup`, `aria-expanded`, no keydown anywhere in the file). The module doc (export_menu.rs:5-10) documents the plain-DOM disclosure as a deliberate WebView2 workaround for the *overlay*, not for dropping the menu keyboard contract; shell.rs:470-473 shows the roles were kept intentionally for AT visibility, which plain `<button>`s in a disclosure also provide. No GUI test queries `menuitem`/`role=menu`, so either proposal is feasible without test churn.

use_debounced.rs:16-22 clears the pending timeout and :35-38 creates each callback with `Closure::once_into_js`. wasm-bindgen's own doc (closure.rs:685-688) states: 'If the JavaScript function is never called then the FnOnce and everything it closes over will leak.' With `LIST_FILTER_DEBOUNCE_MS = 300` (constants.rs:26) and keep-alive lists, every keystroke inside the window cancels and leaks one boxed closure + the captured `String`. Minor correction to the parenthetical: toast.rs also clears timers on manual dismiss (:123, :150) and so leaks the same way, as can global_search.rs:222 / permission_tester_view.rs:310; the debounce is simply the high-frequency case. Proposal (own the `Closure` in a `StoredValue` and drop it on cancel, or one persistent closure per hook) is correct.

shell.rs:126-142 and errors.rs:24-38 both call `bindings::auth::reauthenticate(&tenant)` and emit the identical success/failure strings, but only the shell path calls `session.bump_readiness_reload()` on success — so the toast-action route (`report_if_session_dead` → `spawn_reauth`) leaves a mounted Access Readiness checklist stale, while the topbar button refreshes it (state/mod.rs:306-309 documents the Refresh-token control as the only re-check trigger). The `spawn_reauth` doc (errors.rs:22-23) even names the Refresh button's fallback as a caller, which it is not. Proposal (add the bump to `spawn_reauth`, optional `on_done` for the `reauthing` flag, and have the shell delegate) matches the 'one definition per policy' rule.

The allows exist as quoted (icon.rs:6, toast.rs:1-3, ui/mod.rs:5) and `IconName::More` / `IconName::ExternalLink` have zero uses outside icon.rs. But the premise that the allows 'hide' them is wrong: `components/mod.rs` declares `pub mod icon`, `pub mod toast`, `pub mod ui`, and lib.rs:20 makes `components` pub, so these are exported API of a lib crate and `dead_code` never fires on them regardless of the allow — removing the allows would not make `just web-clippy` (justfile:274, `-D warnings`) flag the two variants. There is also no dead helper fn in icon.rs: `paths` (:79) is called by `Icon` (:60). Every `pub use` in ui/mod.rs has ≥6 external uses, so that allow is redundant rather than harmful.
verdicts.corrected_title: Stale, redundant `#![allow(dead_code)]` / `unused_imports` in icon.rs, toast.rs and ui/mod.rs; two `IconName` variants (`More`, `ExternalLink`) are unused
verdicts.corrected_proposal: Delete the three module-level allows as dead weight and the toast.rs justification comment (its premise is no longer true). Remove `IconName::More` and `IconName::ExternalLink` (or annotate them as intentional spares) by hand — the lint cannot prove this because the enum is public API through `pub mod components`.

verdicts.notes: lib.rs:13 is a crate-wide `#![allow(private_interfaces)]` and lib.rs:19-25 exposes the modules `pub`, with the rationale written out at lib.rs:7-12 — a deliberate, documented decision the finding acknowledges but does not defeat: the crate is a lib consumed only by main.rs (`run()`), the gui shards behind `test-support` (Cargo.toml:77) and the in-crate `demo`, so there is no 'genuinely public item' for a future leak to reach, and pub-but-unused items in a wasm bin bundle cost nothing at runtime (linker/wasm-opt DCE). The cited 'real instance' is wrong: global_search.rs:408 `enum Route` is a field of the private `struct Destination` (:426), not a private type in a public signature. The cfg-doubled module tree is churn for lint hygiene only.
verdicts.corrected_title: Crate-wide `#![allow(private_interfaces)]` could be narrowed to the test-mountable modules
verdicts.corrected_proposal: If anything, move the allow from the crate root onto the `pub mod views;` / `pub mod components;` items (the only modules that need it) and leave the module visibility alone; skip the `#[cfg(feature = "test-support")]` module duplication. Correct the evidence: `Route`/`Destination` are both private and are not an instance of the lint.

verdicts.notes: Premise holds: constants.rs:20-22 hand-mirrors `APPS_MAX` (src-tauri commands/applications/mod.rs:75), nothing pins the two (no hit for `APPS_HARD_CAP`/`10_000` under src-tauri/tests or web-rs/tests), the comment path `commands/applications.rs` is stale, and the SP side already solved it via `sp_index_cap` (backend mod.rs:88-95: 'so the notice can name the number without the frontend keeping its own copy in sync'; index_cap_notice.rs:245-266). The proposal's location is wrong: `DirectoryIndexStatus` is not in azapptoolkit-dto — it is a `serde::Serialize` struct in the backend (applications/mod.rs:86-95) mirrored by a `Deserialize` twin in web-rs bindings/applications.rs:22-27. Also `app_index_truncated` would require the status command to read the apps list cache, not just the SP index.
verdicts.corrected_title: `APPS_HARD_CAP` hand-mirrors the backend's `APPS_MAX` while the SP lists already read their cap from `get_directory_index_status`
verdicts.corrected_proposal: Add `app_index_cap: usize` to the backend `DirectoryIndexStatus` (commands/applications/mod.rs:88) and its bindings mirror (bindings/applications.rs:24), populate it from `APPS_MAX`, and have application_list.rs:448/:576 read it like `IndexCapNotice` does; or, cheaper, move the single `10_000` into azapptoolkit-dto (shared by both trees) and reference it from both `APPS_MAX` and the frontend. Fix the stale `commands/applications.rs` path either way.

verdicts.notes: saved_views.rs:12-16 `SavedView { name, facet, search }` and :58-62 snapshot only those two signals; `created_after`/`created_before` are view-local `RwSignal<Option<NaiveDate>>` (application_list.rs:185-186, enterprise_application_list.rs:54-55) passed to `DateRangeFilter` in the scaffold's `drawer` slot (application_list.rs:309-311) and counted in the FilterToggle badge (:201-202) — the same drawer that hosts `SavedViews` (list_scaffold.rs:42-46). So a saved view cannot capture a date range and applying one leaves the current range active. Proposal (`#[serde(default)]` optional dates threaded from `ListScaffold`, set including to `None` on apply) is backward-compatible with stored payloads and feasible; the MI list has no date range and would pass nothing.

open_items.rs:221-241 decodes the snapshot and `set`s it with no length clamp or `(kind, entity_id)` dedupe; the cap is enforced only in `open_item` (:76-96) and evicts exactly one per push, so a >8 snapshot stays over cap. The existing tests (state/mod.rs:523-568 cap, :571-627 restore) never feed an oversized snapshot. One wrinkle in the proposal: `Vec` order is the dock order that `step_open_item` walks (use_shortcuts.rs:75-77 'the dock's own (open order), not focus recency'), so sorting by `focused_at` would reorder the dock.
verdicts.corrected_proposal: After decoding: dedupe by `(kind, entity_id)` keeping the higher `focused_at`, then while `len() > MAX_OPEN_ITEMS` remove the entry with the smallest `focused_at` (preserving Vec/dock order rather than sorting), then `set`. Add a test that a 9-item snapshot restores 8 and drops the least recently focused.

verdicts.notes: Evidence is real: apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/application_list.rs:244-251 bumps `reload` and only then spawns `invalidate_list_cache`; enterprise_application_list.rs:114-123 is the same shape. Backend `list_applications_with_pairing` (src-tauri/src/commands/applications/mod.rs:136-148) returns the cached Vec synchronously with no await before it, and `invalidate_list_cache` (commands/diagnostics.rs:52-81) is a sync command. Nothing orders the two IPCs, so the outcome is a scheduling race (frontend task order vs. tokio spawn of the async list command vs. the sync invalidate on the IPC thread) — it may often resolve favourably in practice, but nothing guarantees it and the comment's 'next tick' rationale is unproven. The repo already has the correct order in three siblings: application_detail_pane.rs:70-74, managed_identities/mod.rs:110-121 and managed_identities/detail_window.rs:195-206 all `await` the invalidate before bumping. The only test (tests/gui/application_list.rs:196-214, and the enterprise twin at :116) asserts the invalidate call happened, not its order relative to the list fetch. No AGENTS.md/architecture note documents bump-first as deliberate.

Code matches: permissions_tab.rs:110-117 toasts only created/upserted counts, sets `consent_result`, then `on_changed.run(())`; the downgrade path at :341-343 sets `scope_note`, closes the chooser (`pending_downgrade.set(None)`) and calls `on_changed`. The pane's `Suspend` (application_detail_pane.rs:136-148) rebuilds the whole subtree on reload, and credentials_tab.rs:470-475 documents exactly this ("anything held here is unmounted before it can be read"). The `consent_result` Callout (:763-779) is the only place `failures.len()` appears, and backend `grant_admin_consent_core` (src-tauri/src/commands/permissions.rs:348, :425-555) collects partial failures into `Ok(GrantResult.failures)` rather than erroring, so a partial consent really does read as an unqualified success toast. The comment at :205-206 is stale — :342 closes the chooser. Downgraded from high to medium: after the reload the permissions table shows live per-row consent state, so the operator is not left believing a permission is granted when it is not; what is lost is the explicit failure count/message (`GrantFailure.message` is not surfaced anywhere even today, only counted). No GUI test covers either note (grep of tests/gui for Downgrade/Grant admin consent finds nothing).

Premise holds: permissions_tab.rs:808-814 gates `SharePointSitesSection` on the bare value (`v == "Sites.Selected" || is_sharepoint_orgwide(v)`), unlike the row gate `row_scope_kind` (:70-81) and `has_mail` (:781-786); the enterprise pane has the identical bare gate at enterprise_application_detail_pane/permissions.rs:253-258, and the invariant at src-tauri/tests/repo_invariants/commands.rs:130-133 pins only the three Exchange names. But the impact and the proposal are overstated. The core already has a resource-aware classifier the reviewer did not engage with: `is_sharepoint_orgwide_permission(resource_app_id, value)` (crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/scoping.rs:377-388) deliberately treats BOTH Microsoft Graph and Office 365 SharePoint Online as SharePoint reach and rejects other resources — so a Graph-only gate would hide the section for SPO-resource apps, which the repo's own reach classification (and sharepoint-selected.md:13-15, 'only per-site via the SharePoint site access section') does not call for; the Graph-only limit in `is_scopable_sharepoint_resource_permission` (scoping.rs:406-410) is about offering the *conversion fix*, not about showing the per-site grant list. The realistic false positive is a third-party API exposing a `Sites.`-prefixed role, and the cost is an extra collapsible section, not a wrong verdict.
verdicts.corrected_title: SharePoint sites section (app-reg and enterprise panes) is gated on the bare `Sites.*` value instead of the resource-aware `is_sharepoint_orgwide_permission`
verdicts.corrected_proposal: Gate both call sites (permissions_tab.rs:808-814 and enterprise_application_detail_pane/permissions.rs:253-258) on `is_sharepoint_orgwide_permission(Some(&p.resource_app_id), v) || (v == "Sites.Selected" && resource is Graph or SPO)` — i.e. accept Graph + Office 365 SharePoint Online and reject other resources — or add a `is_sharepoint_site_grant_resource_permission` helper in core::scoping with that exact semantics and a unit test. Decide explicitly (doc comment on `SharePointSitesSection`, lines 7-11) whether SPO-resource apps keep the section; do not silently narrow to Graph-only. Optionally extend the repo invariant's GONE list to bare `is_sharepoint_orgwide(` calls outside core and scope_badge.

verdicts.notes: Verified end to end. navigation.rs:108-110 sets `pending_app_tab` unconditionally then calls `open_item`; open_items.rs:70-74 early-returns (retitle + `focus_item`) when `(kind, entity_id)` is already open; the workspace mounts a pane for EVERY open item (`<For each=move || session.open_items.get()>` at components/open_items_workspace.rs:138) and merely toggles `display:none` for non-shown panes (:236), so re-focusing never remounts and the only consumer (application_detail_pane.rs:81-86) never runs. The flag is cleared only by `TenantScopedUi::reset` (state/mod.rs:264), and the sole test (state/mod.rs:456-488) covers that reset. `open_enterprise_on_tab` (navigation.rs:117-122) with its consumer at enterprise_application_detail_pane/mod.rs:185-193 has the identical leak. The MI comment at navigation.rs:127-129 acknowledges the already-open case keeps its tab but not that the pending flag then leaks to the next unrelated app.

Evidence is accurate: application_detail_pane.rs:129-135 uses `Suspense` (fallback = `DetailSkeleton`), :136-148 rebuilds header, `TabBar` and every `keep_alive` tab inside the `Suspend` on each resource re-run; the `keep_alive` comment (:94-99) explains tab-switch survival only. `grep -rn Transition web-rs/src` returns nothing, so the skeleton flash claim stands. The three credentials-tab deferrals exist at credentials_tab.rs:390-397, 578-584 and 600-608, and the browser test `the_reveal_defers_the_detail_reload_until_it_is_dismissed` (tests/gui/certificate_reveal.rs:279) pins the workaround — the refactor must keep or adapt that test. The long-lived `RwSignal<Option<Arc<ApplicationDetail>>>` + Effect proposal is feasible in Leptos 0.8 and would also remove the root cause of finding 1. Effort L is honest; medium severity fits a refactor whose symptoms are already visible as separate bugs.

owners_tab.rs:36-67 and :449-536 and dialogs/add_owner.rs:42-62 and :213-261 each carry a 300 ms `use_debounced`, a 2-char gate returning `Ok(Vec::new())`, and their own results markup. The owners tab's `Suspend` checks only `filtered.is_empty()` (:482-484) so an untouched box renders "No matches." — the exact bug frontend-workspace.md:85-86 says `DirectorySearch` was extracted to end (add_owner.rs:222-228 gates on the debounced, not raw, query so it renders nothing but still drifts). The default-owners loop is duplicated at owners_tab.rs:127-150 vs add_owner.rs:125-159 with different `existing` sources, and `grep add_default_owners src-tauri/src/commands` finds no backend command. `DirectorySearch` already exposes `exclude`, `query`, `action_label`, `action_appearance`, `row_disabled`, `clear_on_pick`, `show_no_matches` (components/directory_search.rs:60-130), so the replacement is feasible; one caveat: the Owners tab's Stage/Add label flips with `replacing`, and `action_label` is a plain `String`, so either a `Signal` prop or two instances under a `Show` is needed. directory_search.rs:1-10 and frontend-workspace.md:77-86 list the four folded consumers; neither owners surface is documented as a deliberate exclusion.

credentials_tab.rs:1112-1127: the `button--danger` Primary button calls `do_rotate(true)` directly; :512-516 collects every `key_id` in `secrets` (active included); the dialog body (:1089) says only "optionally removes the existing secret(s)". Per-row removals (:1130-1160) and the expired sweep (:1162-1177) go through `ConfirmDialog` with a named subject, so the inconsistency is real. Warnings come from src-tauri/src/commands/keyvault.rs:133-182 ("failed to remove {key_id}: {e}") but the UI only shows a count with "see the log" (:539), and a grep of web-rs/src for any log viewer/open-log affordance finds none. Proposal (live count in the label, ConfirmDialog or `require_keyword` when n>1, surface warning text) is consistent with the repo's existing ConfirmDialog usage.

Both controls are free-text `<Input>`s (credentials_tab.rs:935 `gencert_validity`, :1098 `rotate_lifetime`, defaults at :279/:349). :507-511 does `parse::<u32>().unwrap_or(180).clamp(1, 730)` and :570-574 `unwrap_or(365).clamp(1, 1095)` with no error path, unlike `resolve_expiry_fields` (:125-140) which returns `Err` for the new-secret dialog. Backend: rotate also clamps (commands/applications/credentials.rs:82, MAX_SECRET_LIFETIME_DAYS=730) so the frontend clamp is redundant but the parse-failure→default is silent; `generate_self_signed_certificate` uses `validity_days.unwrap_or(365)` with no cap (credentials.rs:136), so the frontend 1095 clamp is the only cap and a typed 3650 becomes 1095 with no message. The four unit tests in credentials_tab.rs (:1199-1275) cover presets/custom expiry and secret-name sanitising, not these two paths.

expose_api_tab.rs:100 snapshots `dto.identifier_uris` into a `StoredValue` at mount; :123-139 (add) and the remove path (~:145-155) mutate that snapshot and call `set_identifier_uris(&list)`. Backend `set_identifier_uris` (src-tauri/src/commands/expose_api.rs:253-284) validates and PATCHes the client-supplied list with no live read — its own doc says "The editor loads the current list and sends the complete desired set" — whereas `upsert_api_scope` re-reads live (`fetch_expose_api`, expose_api.rs:296). The tab module doc (:6-9) claims the backend re-reads live state before every write, which is false for URIs. The SSO wizard also writes `identifier_uris` (commands/sso/mod.rs:199). The window is narrower than implied — the tab refetches after each of its own saves (:61-65) and the whole pane remounts on `on_changed` — but it is a real lost-update on a security-relevant field with a misleading doc. Either proposed fix (delta commands re-reading live like `upsert_api_scope`, or a `get_expose_api` immediately before computing the list) fits the repo's 'full-collection PATCH: re-read live, mutate, write back' convention.

All four cited branches exist verbatim (expose_api_tab.rs:81-83, authentication_tab.rs:66-69, federated_tab.rs:557-559, permission_picker.rs:243-248) and the drift is larger than stated: sharepoint_sites_section.rs:319, enterprise_application_detail_pane/app_roles.rs:263 and enterprise_application_detail_pane/permissions.rs:222 are the same hand-rolled `Body1.form-error` on a load failure. activity_tab.rs:83-91 and conditional_access_tab.rs:70-78 already use `DetailLoadError` with an `on_retry` that bumps `reload`, and frontend-workspace.md / .claude/rules/frontend.md name `DetailLoadError` as the single load-failure primitive, so this is a documented-invariant violation rather than a taste call. Medium is fair given AGENTS.md's 'one primitive per UI pattern' rule; the fix is mechanical.

Premise mostly true: authentication_tab.rs:184-196 renders only Save (disabled on busy), no Reset/dirty state; overview_tab.rs:84-111 computes the diff inside the async closure so a clean form still dispatches, and backend `update_application` (commands/applications/mod.rs:383-400) PATCHes whatever it receives and then `invalidate_app_lists` — so an unchanged save costs a Graph PATCH *and* a list-cache bust. `grep -rn dirty|unsaved web-rs/src` finds nothing. Overstated: the Overview edit DOES have a Cancel (`cancel` at overview_tab.rs:113-116), so 'no Cancel' applies to the Authentication tab only; and the pane-level Refresh is an existing (if heavy) way back. This is a UX enhancement with a workaround, so low rather than medium.
verdicts.corrected_title: Authentication form has no Reset or dirty state; Overview Save round-trips an empty PATCH (and busts list caches) when nothing changed
verdicts.corrected_proposal: Derive a `dirty: Signal<bool>` for each form (compare `to_uris()`/flags with the loaded DTO in AuthenticationForm; compare the four fields with `app` in OverviewTab), disable Save when clean, add a Reset to the Authentication form that rebuilds the `UriListState`s from the DTO, and have Overview's `save` short-circuit with a toast when the patch is empty so `update_application` is not called (avoids the needless `invalidate_app_lists`). An unsaved-changes guard on `close_item` is optional follow-up, not part of this fix.

verdicts.notes: tests/gui/ has application_detail.rs (4 smoke tests), authentication_tab.rs, certificate_reveal.rs and credential_sweep.rs; per-string greps confirm no GUI test mentions Downgrade, Grant admin consent, Revoke, Replace all, Add Default Owners, Add a scope or New secret, and 'Rotate' matches only a notes fixture string (application_detail.rs:35). permissions_tab.rs has 5 `#[test]`s of pure helpers, owners_tab.rs and expose_api_tab.rs have 0. AGENTS.md states the browser GUI tests are the frontend's only behavioural gate, so the mutation-heavy tabs are indeed ungated. Note for the proposal: the detail-pane modules live in tests/gui_1.rs and `just web-itest-size` enforces a per-shard ceiling, so new modules may need a new shard (frontend-workspace.md sharding rules).

`grep -rn 'apps/desktop/web/' web-rs/src` returns exactly the eight cited references (application_detail_pane.rs:3, application_list.rs:2, owners_tab.rs:2, create_app_dialog.rs:3, tabs/mod.rs:1, views/mod.rs:1, hooks/mod.rs:1, state/tenant.rs:17) and `ls apps/desktop` shows only src-tauri and web-rs. app_tab.rs:59 and enterprise_tab.rs:27,64 still cite Thaw's `Tab`/`TabList`, while components/ui/tab_bar.rs:19-20 documents that `TabList` was replaced app-wide. Purely a docs fix; a repo-invariant scan is cheap and consistent with the existing source-scanning tests.

All claims check out and one is understated. `no_tenant()` (util.rs:88-96) is bypassed by inline structs at application_detail_pane.rs:44-50, permission_picker.rs:130-135, exchange_scoping_section.rs:173 and enterprise_application_detail_pane/mod.rs:113. `copy_text` (util.rs:76-86) is re-implemented at credentials_tab.rs:972-982, secret_reveal_dialog.rs:21-28 AND sso_summary.rs:122-131 — even though util.rs:77 claims the SSO summary uses it — and components/ui/copy_icon_button.rs:12-16 declares `CopyIconButton` the single home of copy feedback. permission_picker.rs:31 redefines the Graph app id as a literal while core::scoping::MICROSOFT_GRAPH_APP_ID (scoping.rs:26) exists and is used by scope_wizard tests. create_app_dialog.rs:88-97 hard-codes the four audiences that overview_tab.rs:12-26 keeps in `SIGN_IN_AUDIENCES`. bindings/mod.rs:1 is `#![allow(dead_code)]` with no rationale comment. result.area_summary: The frontend's a11y foundations are unusually strong for a desktop admin app: every click handler sits on a real <button> (57/57), all 13 dialogs wire use_focus_trap + use_escape + aria-labelledby, TabBar implements the full WAI-ARIA tabs pattern, the open-items workspace uses inert + focus return, colour tokens all clear WCAG AA (worst text pair is dark --text-faint on --surface-raised at 4.05:1), 34 :focus-visible rules pair with the outline:none resets, and prefers-reduced-motion is handled globally. The weaknesses are (1) the documented primitives are widely bypassed — Badge 45 bypasses vs 20 uses, ~11 raw data-tables without DataTable/keynav, ~10 load failures that skip DetailLoadError, Spinner as Suspense fallback in ~9 content regions, 8 row buttons missing the documented cell-mid — so the "one primitive per pattern" invariant is aspirational in places; (2) async outcomes are largely silent to AT (66 form-error sites, one with a role; DetailLoadError and the Copied badge have no live role) and structural ARIA is thin (0 of 87 <th> carry scope, accordion headers and FilterChips lack expanded/pressed state, two role=menu disclosures lack the menu keyboard contract, the date-range labels are not associated with their inputs); (3) two fresh instances of the documented aria-boolean-attribute bug and a hard-coded-plural / date-format sprawl (120 "(s)" strings, three expiry phrasings, six date formats) with no GUI test pinning any ARIA state value.

The GUI harness already drives real DOM (`ts::press_key`, active_element checks in open_items_dock.rs:267-291), so asserting `getAttribute('aria-selected') === 'true'` on the active TabBar tab, `aria-expanded` on FilterToggle, `aria-pressed` on a sort toggle, and `role="alert"` on a rendered load error is cheap and would have caught both new instances.

findings.title: `?` opens the shortcuts sheet over an open modal, stacking two ModalShells with the same id and two focus traps; ten dialogs still hand-roll the ModalShell scaffold
findings.rationale: With the update splash (or any ConfirmDialog) open, pressing `?` while focus is on a button opens the shortcuts sheet on top: two `id="modal-shell-title"` elements exist, both window-level Tab-cycling handlers are active, and one Escape closes both dialogs (every use_escape fires). Low frequency, but it is a real state the code allows. The ten hand-rolled dialogs also each hard-code a unique title id, which is why ModalShell's single fixed id was never questioned.
findings.proposal: (1) In use_shortcuts skip bare-key bindings when `document.querySelector('.modal-backdrop')` exists (the workspace already uses this test — lift it into a `modal_is_open()` helper in hooks). (2) Give ModalShell a per-instance id (`format!("modal-title-{}", counter)`). (3) Migrate the 10 hand-rolled dialogs onto ModalShell (they are byte-identical outside their children), which also removes 10 copies of the hardcoded-id pattern and makes the FOCUSABLE fix below land once.

Add a small `just` recipe / repo_invariants test that extracts `^\.[a-z][\w-]*` selectors from styles.css and fails on any not found in web-rs/src or tests (allow-listing the `thaw-*` overrides and the format!-built prefixes), so the sheet cannot silently re-accumulate.
