verdicts.notes: All evidence real. sso/mod.rs:466-468 joins get_service_principal_sso_fields with list_assigned_claims_mapping_policies; policies.rs:51 shows the READ takes policy_write_token(); mod.rs:510-513 collapses Err into (None, None); dto/sso.rs:297-299 documents that None means either 'no policy' or 'read skipped'. sso_tab.rs:543 seeds ClaimsEditorState from unwrap_or_default() (include_basic=true, empty schema) with no discriminator. set_claims_mapping (mod.rs:1643-1661) detaches every assigned policy before create, and an empty policy yields None (no replacement). The consent path makes it worse: grant_consent (sso_tab.rs:675-685) does NOT bump reload, so even after consent the editor still shows the never-loaded state and the 'Save again' toast walks the operator straight into the detach. No AGENTS.md/architecture rationale covers the data-loss path; auth-and-consent.md only justifies not prompting on read. Proposal is consistent with repo conventions (Callout primitive, request_scope_consent 'policy_write' already used at sso_tab.rs:682).

Mechanism verified: rotate_cert (sso_tab.rs:618-624) sets rotated_cert then bumps the OUTER reload; SsoContent's config LocalResource tracks reload (sso_tab.rs:19) and its Suspend re-renders <SsoEditor cfg=cfg reload=reload/> (line 45), and rotated_cert is RwSignal::new(None) inside SsoEditor (line 541) — so the <pre class="secret-reveal"> at 766-774 is gone once the refetch resolves. The staged path is immune because staged_pem lives in SigningCertRolloverPanel with its own reload (lines 66,70). tests/gui/certificate_reveal.rs:53-59 documents this exact teardown class for the credentials tab, so the repo treats it as a real bug pattern. No GUI test covers rotate (grep confirms). Severity downgraded from high to medium: unlike a private key, the SAML public signing certificate is recoverable out of band from the federation metadata URL shown in SamlSummaryView (Entra publishes it; probe_federation_metadata even returns published_certs), so the loss is of the in-app convenience copy, not of an irrecoverable secret. Proposal (lift rotated_cert to SsoContent or stop bumping the outer reload) is sound.

sso_tab.rs contains no ConfirmDialog (verified by reading the whole file); rotate (759-765) and retire (473-479) fire directly via cmd.run_toast_err. Siblings do stage ConfirmDialog: mod.rs:373-385 (delete SP, typed DELETE for foreign), access.rs (remove/assign/add-to-group), owners.rs. Backend doc calls rotate a big-bang that stops sign-in for static-cert apps (also the UI's own Callout at 753-755). One correction: the cited frontend-workspace.md:98-104 passage is about button--danger STYLING ('Reversible actions stay un-reddened'), not about confirmation dialogs, and auth-and-consent.md:191-193 'stays an explicit action' means a dedicated button rather than automatic removal — neither doc mandates a confirm. The finding stands on the in-pane inconsistency and outage risk. Proposal is feasible; note the existing GUI test staging_a_certificate_does_not_activate_it clicks '.cert-rollover button' (first = Stage), which the change would not disturb.

sso_tab.rs:395-406 and 766-774 render bare <pre class="secret-reveal"> with no copy affordance (the rotate one has no label/hint). sso_summary.rs:113-145: CopyBlock is a private `fn` and hand-rolls navigator.clipboard().write_text via spawn_local, duplicating util::copy_text (util.rs:76-85) whose doc claims to be the shared copier — though CopyBlock needs a completion callback for its 'Copied' state, which copy_text lacks, so extending copy_text is required as the proposal says. Minor correction to the evidence: there IS a certificate save command, save_generated_certificate_pfx (lib.rs:98, credentials_tab.rs:1000-1064 'Save .pfx…'), for app-registration generated certs; none exists for the SAML signing public cert. Proposal is reasonable and matches the one-primitive rule.

sso/mod.rs:1738-1745: get_sso_summary calls get_sso_config again, then only wraps fields plus oidc_summary_urls/saml_summary_urls (pure functions of tenant/app id). get_sso_config = SP fields ∥ claims read, then find_application_by_app_id, then get_application_sso_fields (mod.rs:466-486). None of these reads are cached: get_json's third arg is consistency_eventual, not a cache flag (transport.rs:357-362), and the sso_fields/find_application methods call get_json directly. sso_tab.rs:550-561 fires get_sso_summary only after config resolved (serial), and SigningCertRolloverPanel (73-83) reads the SP a third time. Untagged serde_json::Value round-trip and silent 'Summary unavailable.' on mismatch confirmed at 872-887. Option (a) or (b) is feasible; the URL formulas are already pure helpers.

mod.rs:65-77 cred_status uses chrono num_days() (truncates toward zero), so end in (-24h,0) gives days==0 -> misses the <0 arm -> renders '0d left' badge--danger. auth-and-consent.md:181-184 documents that the SSO cert path was fixed with div_euclid (sso/mod.rs:1538) precisely to avoid this. Sibling copies confirmed: credentials_tab.rs:30-61 (days_until num_days, WARN_DAYS/CRITICAL_DAYS), application_list.rs:159, credentials_dashboard.rs:20-21,136, sso_certificates_dashboard.rs:29-30,300; core has EXPIRY_WARNING_DAYS (audit/permissions.rs:19). The finding UNDERSTATES scope: core::audit::credentials.rs:24,40 also uses num_days() and credential_status maps 0 -> ExpiringSoon (credentials.rs:76-82), and types.rs:110-113 likewise, so the two dashboards that take days_to_expiry/status from the backend show '0d left' for a credential expired <24h ago as well. Corrected proposal: floor in core (summarize_credentials + ListCredentialStatus) with EXPIRY_CRITICAL_DAYS there, then one frontend badge helper consuming it.

Evidence is real (access.rs:137-141 DataTable; roles_grants.rs:83-86 collect_all_pages; dto AppAssignmentDto lacks principal_id though core AppRoleAssignment.principal_id exists at models.rs:371; DirectorySearch exclude prop unused by access.rs). But the unwindowed rendering is a DOCUMENTED deliberate decision the reviewer did not engage with: data_table.rs:17-22 states DataTable is 'Intentionally uncapped' because callers incl. 'an SP's assignees' are admin-bounded, and 'Add a cap here only if a real tenant is shown to stall on one of these tables.' The reviewer's concern (per-user SaaS apps with thousands of appRoleAssignedTo rows) is plausible but is exactly the evidence the doc asks for before changing it. The exclude proposal is also flawed as written: Graph permits one principal to hold several app roles (it rejects only a duplicate principal+role pair), so excluding by principal_id alone would block valid second-role assignments; the exclusion must be keyed on (principal_id, selected_role). Corrected title: 'Access tab drops principal_id from AppAssignmentDto, so DirectorySearch cannot hide principals already holding the selected role; a client-side filter would help large apps'. Corrected proposal: add principal_id to the DTO; derive exclude from assignments where app_role_id == selected_role; add a filter Input; revisit ShowMore only with a real-tenant stall per the DataTable doc.

access.rs:210-219 filters only on is_enabled; core AppRole has allowed_member_types (models.rs:177-192) and app_roles.rs:30-38 already labels 'User'/'Application'. claims_editor.rs:926 seeds from BASIC_CLAIM_SET[0], which is the Name ID row with overridable=false (lines 51-57) and a placeholder 'URI' ('nameid (format emailAddress)') that the doc at 48-49 calls descriptive; the Edit button is rendered only `if overridable` (455-469), so the test exercises the one row the UI never seeds and asserts a value that must never reach Graph. The UI gap is real: the Provisioning Callout (actually at panels.rs:39-46 — the file is 134 lines, so the cited 282-298 line numbers are wrong) names Synchronization.Read.All and offers no consent button, while GroupMembershipSection (access.rs:539-554) offers 'Grant consent & retry', and core/capabilities.rs has no synchronization entry (keys: app_registrations, tenant_restore, admin_consent, audit_reports, conditional_access, sharepoint_*, group_membership, keyvault_*, azure_role_*, graph_activity_usage, exchange_rbac). Premise holds on every point. dr.rs:502 promises a re-run 'recreates only what is missing'; restore.rs:197-218 iterates every `app_registrations` entry and calls `create_application_core` (applications/mod.rs:329-338 — a bare POST /applications, no lookup by name/URI/marker). Nothing in restore.rs, backup.rs, CHANGELOG.md or docs/architecture/backup-and-restore.md claims or implements idempotency. The Restore button gate at dr.rs:366 reads `plan.get().is_some() && !cloud_blocked() && !restoring.get()`; `plan`/`loaded` are set at dr.rs:131-132 and never cleared — `load_file` (:125-126) and `do_restore` (:155-157) clear only `report`, so the primary button survives a successful run. The GUI test dr.rs:77-95 waits for `.dr-view__result` and never asserts the button is gone. Worse than the reviewer noted: restore.rs:750-752 (MI runbook) ALSO tells the operator to 're-run the restore to re-bind its Graph app-roles', so the report itself instructs a duplicate-creating re-run. One correction to the proposal: matching by `api://{new}` is not derivable from the manifest (the rewrite target is the new appId, known only in the report); match by display name and/or stamp a source marker (e.g. `notes`/tag `azapptoolkit:source_app_id=<guid>`) at create time so a re-run can resolve it; `find_application_by_app_id` exists (graph/client/applications.rs:446) but keys on appId, which changes. High is honest: the UI's stated remedy creates a second copy of the whole estate with fresh secrets and paired SPs in a DR destination.

tauri-sys core.rs:18-27 (pinned rev 289bd29, Cargo.toml:33) does `.map(|val| swb::from_value(val).unwrap()).map_err(|err| swb::from_value(err).unwrap())`. `UiError` is a struct, so a string rejection (Tauri's shape for invalid-args deserialization failures and ACL/permission denials) fails `from_value` and panics; lib.rs:69 installs `console_error_panic_hook`, which logs and aborts the WASM instance with no toast. `.claude/rules/backend-commands-and-caches.md:15` presents `invoke_result` as the safe path, so the rule is misleading. Nothing pins binding arg names: repo_invariants/ has cache/cancel/commands/fanout/release/sources/trust only, and command-parity-check.sh compares command *names*. The GUI harness cannot catch this because `ipc_mock::mock_err` (ipc_mock/mod.rs:265-267) only ever rejects with a `UiError`. Proposal is feasible: deserialize both sides to `serde_json::Value` first and map failures to a synthetic `UiError`, plus a source-scan that bindings/ never import `tauri_sys::core::{invoke,invoke_result}` directly (note `defaults::get_tenant_defaults` and the diagnostics bindings use bare `invoke` by design as infallible commands — the wrapper should cover those too or leave them explicitly allow-listed).

key_vault_view.rs:42-47 tracks only `session.view` and wipes `revealed`/`error`; `vault_name` (:23), `listed` (:24) and `loaded` (:30) have no tenant dependency. `set_active_tenant` (state/tenant.rs:18-39) resets `tenant_ui` and sets view=Home, which triggers the view-watch but leaves the table populated. `VaultPicker` (vault_picker.rs:27-30) resets its discovered `all_vaults` on tenant change but not `value`, so tenant A's vault name stays in the field. Every sibling tenant-scoped panel resets on `tenant.get()` (sites.rs:163-168, resource_access/keyvault.rs:168-173, mailboxes.rs:153-160 with the explicit 'cross-tenant leakage' comment). What leaks is secret names/content-types/expiry (metadata), not values — still a tenant-scoped surface violating the repo's #1 footgun rule. On the proposal: the lighter, sibling-consistent fix is an `Effect` on `tenant.get()` clearing all five signals; moving a `Vec<KvSecretItemDto>` into `TenantScopedUi` is heavier than what that struct holds today (filters/facets/flags), so prefer the Effect plus the GUI test.

grep confirms `report_if_session_dead` is called only in dr.rs (6 sites) and bulk_action_bar.rs:564; the sink's own doc (state/errors.rs:45-48) says surfaces with an inline banner should call it first. build_support.rs:110-118 `the_repos_own_changelog_has_a_section_for_the_current_version` asserts section_for(CHANGELOG, CARGO_PKG_VERSION).is_some(); src/components/release_notes.rs:86-95 `the_running_versions_changelog_section_is_baked_in` asserts the baked CURRENT_RELEASE_NOTES is non-empty and stops before the next header. build.rs:41-44 writes `unwrap_or_default()` (empty) when the changelog is unreadable or the section is absent, so the release_notes test fails on every condition the build_support one does, plus a broken bake path — strictly stronger, as claimed. Failing path is reachable end to end in the shipped build, not just tests/demo. (1) apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/state.rs:449-481: `graph_for` ALWAYS installs a `policy_write_token` ScopedTokenAdapter, so `policy_write_token()` (crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client.rs:317) never returns the `Forbidden("... not configured")` short-circuit; the read in crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/policies.rs:51 goes to `bearer()` (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/token_adapter.rs:70) → `access_token_inner` silent refresh, which for an un-consented `Policy.ReadWrite.ApplicationConfiguration` returns `AuthError::ConsentRequired` without any interactive prompt (crates/azapptoolkit-auth/src/service/mod.rs:540-546; per AGENTS.md this scope is never in the sign-in bundle, so first-time operators always hit it). (2) apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/sso/mod.rs:466-468 and 498-513: `get_sso_config` swallows that Err (and ANY other error — transient 5xx, 403 from a missing directory role) into `(None, None)`; `SsoConfigDto` has no discriminator (crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/sso.rs:297-302). (3) apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/enterprise_application_detail_pane/sso_tab.rs:543 seeds `ClaimsEditorState::from_dto(&ClaimsPolicyDto::default())` — an empty editor with `include_basic_claim_set=true`, rendered with no warning; `Save claims` (sso_tab.rs:797-803) is only disabled while `cmd.busy`. (4) First Save → `set_claims_mapping` (sso/mod.rs:1636-1639) returns `consent_required`; the `grant_consent` handler (sso_tab.rs:675-685) clears `needs_consent`, toasts 'Save again to apply your claims' and deliberately does NOT bump `reload`, so the editor keeps the never-loaded state. (5) Second Save → `ensure_policy_write_token` OK → `list_assigned_claims_mapping_policies` now succeeds → every assignment is removed (sso/mod.rs:1643-1655) → `policy.is_empty()` (dto/sso.rs:150-155) is true for the untouched editor so NO replacement is created (or a partial one containing only the operator's added rows). Result: the app's live custom claims are silently detached. Mitigating detail (does not lower severity): only the SP assignment is removed, the claimsMappingPolicy object itself survives in `/policies/claimsMappingPolicies`, so an admin can re-attach it out of band — but nothing in the app tells them it happened, and SAML sign-in for that app changes/breaks immediately. No repo_invariants test or GUI test pins this: the only SSO GUI test (apps/desktop/web-rs/tests/gui/sso_rollover.rs) uses a fixture with `claims_policy: None` and never exercises `set_claims_mapping`. Proposal is sound; would add: also bump `reload` after successful consent so the editor re-seeds from the real policy.

Reachable in the shipped build with no upstream guard. Backend apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/exchange/aap_migration.rs:364-400 sets `status = "partial"` inside a *successful* `Ok(AapMigrationItem)` (policy-remove error at :375, or `policies_safe_to_remove` false at :400 with the KEPT-the-legacy-policy warning pushed into `item.warnings`, not into `report.failures`); the loop at :113-125 only pushes to `failures` on `Err`. So a single-app run (`Some(&app_id)` from the section) can return `{dry_run:false, items:[partial], failures:[]}`. The section gate at apps/desktop/web-rs/src/components/exchange_scoping_section.rs:324 (`dry_run || !r.failures.is_empty()`) is then false, so :327 toasts "Migrated 1 policy(ies).", :328 fires `on_changed` (parent reload rebuilds the section), and `mig_result` — the ONLY thing that mounts `AapMigrationReportView` (:761) — is never set, so the KEPT/UNKNOWN warning is never shown. Second path: a cancel or dead session before the first iteration (:97-104) yields `items:[]`, `unattempted:[app]`, `incomplete:true`, `failures:[]` → toast "Migrated 0 policy(ies)." Third: no matching policy at all → `items:[]` → same 0-count success toast. The sibling dialog at views/dialogs/migrate_legacy_scope.rs:81-84 gates on `all(status == "migrated") && !items.is_empty()` (still ignores `incomplete`/`unattempted`, but for a single-app run those imply empty items so it is safe), and the report view at components/aap_migration_report.rs:27,43 treats any non-`migrated` status / `incomplete` / failures as attention-needed — so the two surfaces demonstrably disagree. No GUI test covers the section's migrate path (tests/gui/security_findings.rs:477-525 exercises only the audit dialog), and repo_invariants/{cancel,fanout}.rs pin the backend, not this frontend gate. DTO doc (crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/exchange.rs:242-262) and docs/architecture/audit-findings-and-remediation.md:198 both state a partial run must never read as complete; this surface violates that on a security-posture mutation. Severity high stands: the operator is told the legacy policy is gone / the app is RBAC-scoped when the org-wide grant is still in place and the AAP is the only confinement, inviting manual cleanup of the very policy still doing the confining. Proposal is correct as written; the toast noun fix (`items` are per-app per exchange-scoping.md:78-80) is also accurate.

Could not refute; every link in the chain checks out in the shipped (non-demo) build.

Backend creates unconditionally. apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/restore.rs:196-238 (Pass 1) iterates `backup.app_registrations` and calls `create_application_core` for each with no lookup of an existing app; `create_application_core` (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/applications/mod.rs:329-338) is a bare POST `/applications` (crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/applications.rs:391-393). Entra does not enforce displayName uniqueness, so a second run yields a second app + fresh appId. The only dedupe on the path is `ensure_service_principal` (service_principals.rs:506-516), which keys on the NEW appId and therefore never matches the prior run's SP.
